jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.summary: Jobbbler Demo Systems is the fictional internal employer that Jobbbler uses to populate its own product demonstrations, and this role sits on the team that builds the workflow screens candidates and hiring teams see inside those demos. You will own end-to-end delivery of API-backed search and matching views, working across a TypeScript and React frontend and a Node.js and PostgreSQL backend. Expect to design accessible list and detail screens, tune search relevance queries, and add instrumentation that keeps the demo catalog fast and predictable as new sample data lands. We are looking for a senior engineer comfortable owning a feature from schema through UI, with a track record of maintainable TypeScript and query performance work in PostgreSQL. The team works fully remote across Europe, the UK, and Germany, favors small pull requests over long-lived branches. Because the catalog is explicitly a demonstration surface rather than a live marketplace, correctness and clarity for the reader matter more than production traffic volume.

jobs.title: Product Design Lead
jobs.summary: This design team shapes how people experience the fictional job discovery product that Jobbbler maintains purely for its own demo flow, including the assistive agent activity views candidates see while an automated search runs. As product design lead you will set the interaction design direction for the whole surface, translating research findings into flows that make an AI-assisted job search feel legible rather than magical. Day to day you will run generative and evaluative research sessions, extend the shared design system with new patterns for agent status and progress, and pair closely with engineers in Berlin to get prototypes into working code. We want someone who has led design on a research-informed product, is fluent in Figma for exploration and production files, and can defend decisions with evidence rather than opinion. The role is hybrid out of Berlin, in the studio a few days a week for critique. Since every artifact here ultimately supports a demonstration rather than paying customers, we measure success by how clearly a first-time viewer understands the product, not by conversion metrics.

jobs.title: Technical Talent Partner
jobs.summary: Engineering hiring at Jobbbler Demo Systems exists to model what a thoughtful, bias-aware recruiting process looks like inside the product's own demo catalog, and this contract role owns that process end to end. You will design interview loops for software engineering and product roles, calibrate scorecards with hiring managers, and build sourcing plans that reach candidates outside the usual referral networks. A second focus is talent analytics: tracking pass-through rates by stage and flagging where the loop introduces unnecessary friction or inconsistency between interviewers. We are looking for a manager-level recruiter with experience running technical interview design from scratch and comfortable presenting data to skeptical stakeholders. The position is onsite in London on a fixed-term contract, working alongside the small internal team that maintains the rest of the demo organization. Interview panels here are kept deliberately small, with a single structured debrief replacing the free-for-all discussion many candidates describe from other processes.

jobs.title: Principal Platform Engineer
jobs.summary: Northstar Cloudworks builds a fictional developer platform that gives internal teams self-service access to compute, storage, and networking across multiple AWS regions. The platform team you would join owns the Kubernetes control plane, the Terraform modules that provision new environments, and the Go services that expose it all through a single internal API. As principal engineer you will set the technical direction for multi-region capacity planning, decide when to introduce new abstractions versus extend existing ones, and mentor senior engineers working across the stack. Recent priorities include cutting provisioning time and shrinking outage blast radius. We expect deep hands-on Kubernetes experience, production Go services, and infrastructure-as-code discipline in Terraform. The role is fully remote for candidates in Europe or Canada, with quarterly in-person planning weeks. Success is measured less by lines shipped and more by how many teams can self-serve without filing a ticket.

jobs.title: Cloud Reliability Engineer
jobs.summary: Reliability for Northstar's distributed cloud service falls to a small SRE group that owns observability, incident response, and capacity planning across every region the platform serves. In this senior role you will extend Prometheus dashboards and alerting so on-call engineers catch degradation before customers do, and you will lead postmortems that turn incidents into concrete changes rather than vague action items. You will also work on capacity forecasting, using historical Linux host metrics to plan ahead of seasonal traffic spikes instead of reacting to them. We want someone with real production experience running Linux systems at scale, fluency with Prometheus or an equivalent metrics stack, and a calm, structured approach to incident command. The role is hybrid from our Toronto office, with the team gathering there twice a week and rotating a shared on-call schedule the rest of the time. Interviews focus on walking through a past incident you handled rather than solving abstract system design puzzles.

jobs.title: Developer Support Engineer
jobs.summary: Customers integrating with Northstar's infrastructure platform run into the same handful of API and configuration issues, and this role exists to resolve those issues quickly while also fixing the documentation and defaults that caused them. You will triage incoming support requests, reproduce integration problems in Python against the platform's APIs, and write clear technical responses that a developer can act on without a follow-up call. Part of the job is proactive: shipping small documentation fixes and sample code so the same question stops recurring. We are looking for a mid-level engineer who is comfortable reading unfamiliar codebases, writes plainly, and enjoys the detective work of support more than pure feature building. The role is flexible, based from Dublin or remote within Europe, with the support queue covered as a team rather than assigned to one person. We track success partly through resolution time and partly through how often a documentation fix eliminates a recurring ticket.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist
jobs.summary: Forecasting decisions inside Copper Finch's analytics workspace currently rely on models that are accurate but hard for a non-technical stakeholder to trust, and this staff role exists to close that gap. You will build and maintain explainable forecasting models in Python, backed by SQL pipelines that pull from the workspace's shared metrics tables, and you will design experiments that validate whether a new model actually changes decisions for the better. Because the role sits at staff level, you are expected to set technical direction for forecasting across multiple product teams rather than just ship your own models. We are looking for someone with deep experience in applied forecasting, strong SQL for exploring messy production data, and a track record of designing experiments that hold up to scrutiny. The role is fully remote and open globally, with the team syncing over a couple of overlapping hours each week rather than requiring fixed hours. Model reviews here favor a written explanation of assumptions over a slide deck.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.summary: Copper Finch's business intelligence product depends on models that stay accurate as customer data shifts, and the team you would join is responsible for the pipelines that keep those models honest in production. As a senior machine learning engineer you will productionize model evaluation, wiring MLflow into the deployment path so every model version has traceable metrics before it ships. You will also build and maintain feature store pipelines in Python, packaged with Docker, so data scientists can reuse validated features instead of recomputing them per project. We want someone who has taken models from notebook to production before, is comfortable with MLflow or a comparable experiment tracking tool, and can debug a broken pipeline under time pressure. The role is hybrid out of our Amsterdam office, typically three days a week alongside the data science team. We evaluate engineers here on how few surprises their pipelines produce once a model reaches customers, not on model accuracy alone.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineering Intern
jobs.summary: This internship gives an early-career analyst a real seat on the analytics engineering team that maintains Copper Finch's internal dashboards and shared data models. You will help write and test SQL transformations in dbt, checking that new models match the definitions the business actually uses before they reach a dashboard. A second part of the role is data quality: building simple checks that catch broken pipelines before an analyst notices a chart looks wrong. We are looking for a student or recent graduate who has written SQL before, is starting to learn dbt or a similar transformation tool, and is comfortable using Git for version control on a shared codebase. The internship is onsite in our Montreal office so you can pair directly with the analytics engineers who own the models you will be touching. You will leave with a concrete portfolio of dbt models and data quality checks that shipped to production, reviewed the same way a full-time engineer's work is reviewed.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.summary: Blue Lantern's B2B collaboration product helps distributed teams keep shared documents and decisions in one place, and this role owns discovery and delivery for a meaningful slice of that product end to end. You will run discovery interviews with existing customers to validate problems before committing engineering time, then translate what you learn into a roadmap the team can actually execute against. Expect to work daily with engineering and design leads to sequence work, and with leadership to defend tradeoffs using usage analytics rather than opinion. We are looking for a senior product manager who has owned a roadmap from customer conversation through shipped feature, is comfortable reading product analytics without a dedicated analyst, and can manage stakeholders who do not report to them. The role is hybrid from our Paris office, with the product trio co-located two days a week. Roadmap reviews happen monthly and focus on what changed in customer behavior, not on how many features shipped.

jobs.title: UX Researcher
jobs.summary: Workplace tool decisions at Blue Lantern are supposed to rest on evidence from real users, and this contract role exists to supply that evidence for a growing suite of collaboration products. You will plan and run generative interviews to uncover unmet needs, then follow up with usability testing once a design is ready to validate, always synthesizing findings into something a product team can act on without reading a full report. A meaningful part of the role is research operations: recruiting participants, maintaining a shared repository of past findings, and making sure earlier research does not get re-litigated from scratch. We want a mid-level researcher comfortable running generative and evaluative studies independently, with strong synthesis skills and enough operational rigor to keep a pipeline moving without support staff. The engagement is fully remote for candidates in Europe, on a renewable contract. Findings are shared as short recorded walkthroughs rather than lengthy written reports, since teams here rarely have time to read the latter.

jobs.title: Design Systems Engineer
jobs.summary: Blue Lantern's design platform gives every product team a shared library of React components, and this freelance lead role owns the tooling and accessibility work that keeps that library trustworthy. You will build and maintain component tooling in React and CSS, extend the Storybook setup so every component ships with documented states and props, and run accessibility checks that catch contrast and keyboard-navigation problems before a component reaches a product team. Because the role carries lead scope, you are also expected to set conventions for how new components get proposed and reviewed across teams. We are looking for someone with strong React and CSS fundamentals, hands-on accessibility auditing experience, and comfort maintaining Storybook as a living source of truth rather than a neglected side project. The engagement is freelance with flexible hours, based from Lisbon or remote within Europe, billed hourly against agreed milestones. Component changes ship behind a documented deprecation path so consuming teams are never broken without warning.

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer
jobs.summary: ParcelSignal's security team is embedded directly with the engineers who build our fictional logistics platform, on the theory that security reviews work better as an ongoing conversation than a gate at the end of a release cycle. In this senior role you will run threat modeling sessions before major features are built, not after, helping product engineers see the failure modes they might otherwise miss. You will also own the SAST tooling that runs against our primarily Java codebase, tuning rules so findings stay actionable instead of drowning teams in noise, and you will conduct focused security reviews on the riskiest parts of the platform, such as payment and address-handling code paths. Beyond individual reviews, part of the role is coaching: helping engineering teams build enough security judgment that fewer issues need to reach you in the first place. We are looking for a senior engineer with hands-on Java experience, real threat modeling practice, and the communication skill to make a security finding land as help rather than criticism. The role is fully remote for candidates in the United States or Canada, with the security team meeting synchronously twice a week and otherwise working async. We track progress by how early in the development cycle issues get caught, not by how many vulnerabilities get logged after the fact.

jobs.title: Security Operations Analyst
jobs.summary: Alerts flowing into ParcelSignal's security operations center come from a dozen different sources, and this mid-level role exists to make sense of them before they become incidents. You will investigate alerts inside our SIEM, correlating signals across logging sources to separate real threats from noise, and you will write and refine detection rules so the same false positive stops reappearing every week. When something real does happen, you will follow and help improve our incident response playbooks, documenting what worked and what did not so the next analyst on shift benefits from what you learned. A recurring part of the job is threat intelligence: tracking indicators relevant to logistics and shipping platforms and feeding them back into detection logic before they show up as an active incident. We are looking for someone with hands-on SIEM experience, comfort scripting investigative tooling in Python, and the patience to document findings clearly even during a stressful shift. The role is onsite in our Austin operations center, working a defined shift pattern with the rest of the security operations team rather than a fully independent schedule. New analysts spend their first weeks shadowing a senior teammate on live alerts before taking primary ownership of a shift.

jobs.title: Privacy Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: Privacy has to be designed into ParcelSignal's SaaS security product from the first architecture diagram, not bolted on before an audit, and this manager role leads the small team responsible for making that happen. You will lead privacy-by-design reviews on new features, working with product and engineering leads early enough to change a data model before it ships rather than after. A second responsibility is data governance: maintaining a clear inventory of what personal data the platform collects, why, and how long it is retained, so that question never requires an emergency investigation. You will also run structured risk assessments on new integrations and vendors, deciding which risks are acceptable to launch with and which require mitigation first. As a people manager, you are expected to grow one or two privacy engineers on your team and represent privacy considerations in leadership planning conversations. We are looking for someone with hands-on privacy engineering experience, comfort with formal risk assessment frameworks, and prior experience leading a small team rather than only individual contributor work. The role is hybrid from our Stockholm office, with the team in three days a week for reviews and planning. Success shows up as fewer last-minute privacy escalations before a release, not as a count of completed audits.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.summary: Juniper Grid's energy infrastructure platform moves data pipelines that operators rely on to make real-time decisions, so uptime here is measured in more than customer satisfaction scores. As a senior site reliability engineer you will operate and harden the Kubernetes clusters that run these pipelines, building Grafana dashboards that surface degradation before it becomes an outage rather than after. You will also maintain the Terraform modules used to provision new infrastructure, keeping environments consistent across the regions the platform serves. A core part of the role is on-call operations: carrying a rotation, running blameless postmortems after incidents, and turning recurring pain points into permanent fixes instead of repeated manual workarounds. We are looking for someone with real production Kubernetes experience, working knowledge of Grafana or a comparable observability stack, and the calm judgment on-call work demands. The role is hybrid from our Warsaw office, with the team in twice a week and on-call handled through a shared rotation with clear escalation paths. We look for engineers who leave every incident with at least one concrete follow-up action, not just a summary of what happened.

jobs.title: Network Automation Engineer
jobs.summary: Manual network changes are still the biggest source of outages on Juniper Grid's utility network operations platform, and this lead contract role exists to replace risky manual steps with tested automation. You will design and build Ansible playbooks that codify network changes which used to live only in an engineer's head, and you will wire those playbooks into a CI/CD pipeline so changes get tested before they touch production hardware. Alongside the automation work, you will write Python tooling that validates network state against intent, catching drift before it causes an incident. As the lead on this initiative, you are expected to set standards for how new automation gets reviewed and to bring the networking team along rather than automating around them. We want someone with strong networking fundamentals, hands-on Ansible experience, and comfort building CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure rather than only application code. The role is onsite in our Denver office on a fixed-term contract, working closely with the operations team whose manual processes you are replacing. Rollouts are staged deliberately, starting on non-critical segments of the network before any playbook touches core infrastructure.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Program Director
jobs.summary: Reliability and delivery programs at Juniper Grid currently run through several teams that rarely coordinate timelines with each other, and this part-time director role exists to give those programs a single point of coordination. You will track cross-team infrastructure initiatives end to end, surfacing where one team's timeline silently depends on another's and forcing that dependency into the open before it causes a slip. A significant part of the role is risk management: maintaining a live register of infrastructure risks and making sure the right leader owns mitigation for each one rather than letting risks sit unassigned. You will also manage relationships with external vendors supplying hardware and managed services, holding them accountable to the commitments that operations teams depend on. We are looking for a director-level operator with real program management experience across infrastructure or operations organizations, comfort with formal risk management practice, and the credibility to hold vendors and internal teams to the same standard. The role is part-time with flexible hours, open to candidates globally, structured around a standing weekly program review rather than fixed office hours. Programs here are judged on whether commitments made three months out actually land on the date promised.

jobs.title: Senior QA Automation Engineer
jobs.summary: Commerce integrations break in ways that are hard to catch with a handful of manual checks, and this senior role exists to build automated test coverage durable enough to catch regressions before a partner does. You will write and maintain end-to-end test suites in Playwright and TypeScript, covering the checkout and integration flows that partners depend on most heavily. Alongside UI coverage, you will build API-level tests that exercise the integration layer directly, catching contract breaks earlier and faster than a full browser test would. You will also own the CI/CD pipeline that runs this suite, keeping it fast and reliable enough that engineers trust a red build rather than rerunning it and hoping it passes. We are looking for a senior engineer with strong TypeScript skills, hands-on Playwright experience, and a track record of keeping a large test suite maintainable rather than letting it rot into something nobody trusts. The role is fully remote for candidates based in Europe, with the quality team syncing a few times a week and otherwise working independently. Flaky tests here get fixed or deleted within the sprint they are found, not left in a permanently ignored state.

jobs.title: Quality Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: Product delivery across Orbit Orchard's engineering organization has grown faster than its quality practice, and this manager role exists to set a quality strategy that scales with it rather than becoming a bottleneck. You will define how testing responsibility is split between dedicated QA engineers and feature teams, then coach engineers on both sides until that split actually works in practice rather than just on paper. A significant part of the role is test architecture: deciding where automated coverage belongs in the stack and retiring redundant tests that slow builds without catching real bugs. You will also own release management, deciding what quality bar a release must clear and holding that line even under schedule pressure. As a people manager, you are expected to grow a small team of QA engineers and represent quality tradeoffs in cross-functional planning. We are looking for someone with hands-on test architecture experience, proven coaching ability, and enough backbone to say a release is not ready when the data supports it. The role is hybrid from our Vancouver office, with the team together three days a week. We measure the team less by defect counts and more by how often a real production issue was actually catchable by an existing test.

jobs.title: Performance Test Specialist
jobs.summary: Peak traffic on Orbit Orchard's high-volume marketplace platform still occasionally exposes bottlenecks that only show up under real load, and this freelance role exists to find those bottlenecks before customers do. You will design and run load and stress tests using k6, scripting realistic traffic patterns in JavaScript that mirror how the marketplace actually gets used during peak periods. Once a test run completes, you will dig into the resulting metrics to identify which specific service or query is the limiting factor, rather than reporting a vague slowdown. You will also work with engineering teams to validate that a proposed fix actually improves the numbers before it ships to production. We are looking for a mid-level specialist with hands-on k6 experience, comfort scripting in JavaScript, and the analytical patience to trace a performance regression back to its root cause. The engagement is onsite in our Prague office on a freelance basis tied to specific testing campaigns around major releases. Every performance finding here ships with a reproducible test script, so a fix can be verified against the exact same load profile that exposed the problem.

jobs.title: Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Developers joining Lattice's collaboration network often struggle with the same handful of integration steps, and this senior role exists to turn that friction into clear, practical technical education instead of another support ticket. You will write tutorials and sample applications in JavaScript that show real integration patterns rather than toy examples, and you will speak at developer conferences and meetups to explain how the platform actually gets used in practice. A significant part of the role is community building: showing up in forums and community channels consistently enough that developers trust you as someone who will actually answer, not just post announcements. You will also work closely with the product team, feeding developer confusion back as concrete product and documentation gaps rather than anecdotes. We are looking for a senior advocate with strong technical writing skills, genuine comfort speaking publicly, and enough hands-on JavaScript experience to build credible sample projects rather than borrowed ones. The role is fully remote and open globally, with travel to a handful of conferences each year built into the role rather than optional. We track impact through how often community-reported issues turn into shipped fixes, not through follower counts.

jobs.title: Open Source Program Manager
jobs.summary: Lattice maintains a handful of open developer tools that depend on outside maintainers as much as internal engineers, and this manager role exists to keep that relationship healthy and sustainable. You will coordinate maintainers across several repositories, making sure contribution guidelines and review expectations are consistent instead of varying by whichever maintainer happens to respond first. A core part of the role is program management: running a predictable release cadence across projects and tracking maintainer workload so burnout gets caught before someone quietly disappears. You will also own governance decisions, drafting and updating the policies that determine how outside contributors gain more responsibility over time. Community operations rounds out the role, from moderating discussion spaces to organizing periodic contributor calls that keep people aligned without requiring everyone to read every thread. We are looking for a manager-level operator with real open source program experience, comfort designing governance structures, and the interpersonal skill to manage volunteers who cannot simply be assigned work. The role is hybrid from our New York office, in three days a week, with maintainers spread across time zones the rest of the time. We judge the program by maintainer retention over a year, not by headline contributor counts.

jobs.title: Documentation Engineer
jobs.summary: Reference documentation for Lattice's API platform tends to fall out of date the moment an endpoint changes, and this part-time role exists to design documentation and information architecture resilient enough that it does not. You will write and maintain reference documentation directly against the API surface, in Markdown, structured so a developer can find an answer without reading unrelated sections first. A meaningful part of the role is information architecture: reorganizing navigation and cross-linking as the API grows, rather than letting new pages pile up wherever they were easiest to add. You will also build small working examples that demonstrate each endpoint in context, since a parameter list alone rarely answers a developer's real question. We are looking for a mid-level documentation engineer with hands-on API experience, strong Markdown-based writing skills, and an eye for information architecture rather than just prose quality. The role is part-time with flexible hours, based from Helsinki or remote within Europe, coordinating asynchronously with the rest of the developer relations team. Every documentation change ships alongside the API change that prompted it, reviewed in the same pull request rather than as a follow-up task.

jobs.title: Senior Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary: Prospective customers evaluating Beaconline's customer operations platform usually arrive with a specific integration question that a generic demo cannot answer, and this senior role exists to guide those technical evaluations from first call to signed deal. You will run discovery calls that dig into a prospect's existing systems and workflows, surfacing the integration questions that would otherwise only appear after purchase, and you will design a solution architecture tailored to what you learn rather than reusing a one-size-fits-all deck. A significant part of the role is hands-on: building working proof-of-concept integrations against the platform's APIs so a prospect's engineering team can see real data flowing rather than a slide describing it. You will also deliver technical presentations to audiences that range from individual engineers to executive stakeholders, adjusting depth and framing for each without losing accuracy. Because deals here often stall on a specific technical objection, part of the job is knowing when to bring in an engineer for a deeper API conversation versus handling the objection yourself. We are looking for a senior solutions engineer with genuine API fluency, strong discovery instincts, and comfort presenting to both hands-on engineers and executive buyers in the same week. The role is fully remote for candidates in the United States or Canada, working closely with an assigned account executive on every deal rather than covering the whole pipeline generically. We measure the role by how few technical surprises show up after a deal closes, not by deal count alone.

jobs.title: Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary: Customers who adopt Beaconline's workflow automation product rarely get full value from it in the first month, and this manager role owns the technical adoption plan that closes that gap over the following quarter. You will build a structured adoption roadmap for each assigned account, translating a customer's stated goals into specific configuration and workflow changes rather than generic best-practice advice. A recurring responsibility is querying customer usage data directly in SQL to spot where adoption is stalling before the customer raises it as a complaint, then proactively reaching out with a concrete recommendation. You will also run cross-functional projects internally, coordinating engineering and support when a customer's adoption blocker turns out to be a product gap rather than a training issue. Technical communication runs through all of it: translating what is happening in the platform's logs and data into language a non-technical customer stakeholder can act on with confidence. We are looking for a manager-level technical account manager with real SQL fluency for self-serve analysis, project management experience herding multiple internal stakeholders toward a deadline, and a communication style that builds trust with both engineers and business buyers. The role is hybrid from our Chicago office, with the team in two to three days a week for account planning and cross-team syncs. Account health here is reviewed quarterly against usage data, not against how the relationship simply feels.

jobs.title: Customer Support Systems Administrator
jobs.summary: Support agents at Beaconline lose meaningful time every week to manual steps that could be automated inside the tools they already use, and this mid-level role exists to find and eliminate that friction. You will administer and extend our Zendesk instance, building workflow automations that route and prioritize tickets based on actual customer impact instead of arrival order. A parallel responsibility is reporting: writing SQL queries against support data to build dashboards that show leadership where response times are slipping before it becomes a customer-facing problem. You will also maintain integrations between Zendesk and internal systems, making sure agent-facing context stays accurate as those systems change underneath the support tooling. Because agents are the primary users of everything you build, a meaningful part of the role is sitting with them to understand where automation actually helps versus where it just adds another rule nobody remembers exists. We are looking for someone with hands-on Zendesk administration experience, solid SQL for building reporting from scratch, and genuine interest in workflow design rather than only ticket-queue mechanics. The role is onsite in our Madrid office, working directly alongside the support team whose daily tools you are responsible for. New automations here roll out to a small pilot group of agents before going live for the whole team, so unintended side effects surface early rather than at scale. Success is judged by measurable time saved per agent, not by the number of automations shipped.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter
jobs.summary: Hiring workflow software is what Talent Kernel Labs builds, which means the company's own recruiting process is watched more closely than most, and this senior role owns recruiting for product and engineering roles under that scrutiny. You will run full-cycle technical recruiting, from building sourcing plans that reach engineers who are not actively job hunting through closing offers with candidates who have competing options. A meaningful part of the role is candidate experience: making sure every applicant, hired or not, comes away with an accurate impression of how the company actually works, since a bad experience here undermines the very product the company sells. You will also lean on hiring analytics, tracking time-to-fill and pass-through rates by stage to identify where the funnel is genuinely broken rather than assuming it based on gut feeling. Because the team is small, you will partner directly with hiring managers on role scoping and interview design rather than working from a fixed template handed down from above. We are looking for a senior technical recruiter with strong sourcing skills for hard-to-fill engineering roles, comfort working from data rather than intuition alone, and a genuine investment in candidate experience even under pressure to fill a role quickly. The role is fully remote for candidates based in Europe, coordinating with hiring managers across a few overlapping working hours each day. We treat every closed search as a source of process improvements, reviewing what worked and what nearly failed before opening the next requisition.

jobs.title: Recruiting Operations Specialist
jobs.summary: Behind every recruiter's smooth-looking interview loop at Talent Kernel Labs sits an operations function that keeps the underlying system consistent, fair, and measurable, and this mid-level role is part of that function. You will administer the company's applicant tracking system, configuring workflows and permissions so recruiters and hiring managers see exactly the information they need at each stage without extra manual steps. A significant part of the role is process design: documenting and refining the steps every requisition follows, from approval through offer, so process quality does not depend on which recruiter happens to own a given search. You will also own recruiting reporting, building dashboards that track funnel health and diversity of candidate pipelines across the company rather than leaving that analysis to individual recruiters' spreadsheets. Compliance runs through much of the work as well, making sure interview documentation and candidate data handling meet the standards the company would expect of its own customers. We are looking for someone with hands-on ATS administration experience, a genuine interest in process design rather than only day-to-day ticket handling, and comfort with recruiting compliance requirements across multiple jurisdictions. The role is hybrid from our Boston office, in two to three days a week alongside the recruiting team whose workflows you support. We measure the role by how rarely recruiters need to work around the system rather than through it, and by how consistently reporting numbers match what recruiters experience on the ground.

jobs.title: Candidate Experience Designer
jobs.summary: A recruitment product lives or dies by how candidates experience the parts they cannot see behind the scenes, and this senior contract role exists to research and redesign those candidate-facing moments across Talent Kernel's product. You will conduct user research directly with recent candidates, both hired and rejected, to understand where communication felt unclear or where a status update arrived too late to be useful. From that research, you will build detailed journey maps that trace a candidate's experience from application through decision, identifying the specific moments where trust is won or lost rather than describing the process in the abstract. Using a service design lens, you will then propose concrete changes to messaging, timing, and interface that a product team can actually implement, not just a set of aspirational principles. Because the work touches an active recruiting product, you will collaborate closely with recruiting operations to make sure any redesigned flow still meets compliance and process requirements already in place. We are looking for a senior designer with real service design experience, strong qualitative research skills, and enough familiarity with recruiting processes to spot problems a general product designer might miss. The engagement is a flexible contract open to candidates based in Toronto or remote across North America, structured around specific research and design milestones rather than fixed weekly hours. We consider the work successful when candidate feedback about communication and clarity measurably improves between one recruiting cycle and the next.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
jobs.summary: Sales leadership at RelayForge has historically trusted pipeline numbers less than they should, because the underlying Salesforce data has never been consistently clean, and this mid-level role exists to fix that trust problem at the source. You will maintain and improve the Salesforce data model that the whole revenue organization reports from, closing gaps that let deals slip through stages without the fields needed to forecast them accurately. A core responsibility is forecasting: building SQL-based models that combine historical close rates with current pipeline data to give leadership a number they can actually plan around, rather than a rep's optimistic estimate. You will also build data visualizations that make pipeline health legible at a glance for people who do not want to read a spreadsheet, whether that is a regional sales manager or an executive reviewing quarterly performance. Because RelayForge's own product is operations intelligence software, there is an internal expectation that our own reporting practice sets a credible example of what the product promises customers. We are looking for a mid-level analyst with strong SQL skills, hands-on Salesforce administration or analytics experience, and the ability to build visualizations that a non-technical sales leader can trust without a walkthrough. The role is hybrid from our San Francisco office, in three days a week alongside the sales operations team. We track our own success by how often a forecast built from this data turns out to be accurate within a narrow margin, not by how sophisticated the underlying model looks.

jobs.title: Technical Operations Lead
jobs.summary: Releases for RelayForge's B2B platform have grown riskier as the customer base has grown, and this lead role exists to make sure release velocity does not have to trade off against service reliability. You will own release management end to end, deciding the criteria a release must meet before it ships and coordinating the handful of teams whose work lands in any given release window. When something does go wrong, you will lead incident management directly, running the incident to resolution and then the retrospective that turns it into a permanent process or tooling fix rather than a one-time patch. A significant part of the role is automation: identifying the manual release and readiness steps that keep causing near-misses and building tooling to remove them rather than adding another checklist item. As the technical operations lead, you are expected to provide leadership to a small group of operations engineers, setting priorities and unblocking their work rather than doing all of it personally. We are looking for someone with hands-on release management experience at a growing company, real incident command experience, and enough leadership presence to hold a release gate even when a team is under deadline pressure to skip it. The role is onsite in our Seattle office, working closely with engineering leadership on a shared release calendar. We evaluate the function by how often incidents trace back to a known, already-flagged risk rather than a genuine surprise, since that gap is where the role earns its keep.

jobs.title: Sales Engineer
jobs.summary: Deals for RelayForge's operations product regularly stall on a specific technical question that a generalist account executive cannot answer alone, and this senior role exists to remove that stall point from the sales cycle. You will run technical discovery calls that dig into a prospect's existing operations stack, identifying the integration points and edge cases that a generic product demo would never surface. From that discovery, you will design and deliver solution demonstrations against the platform's APIs, building live examples that answer a prospect's actual integration question rather than a rehearsed generic scenario. You will also maintain accurate technical notes inside the CRM so that account executives, customer success, and the eventual implementation team all inherit the same understanding of what was promised and configured during the sales process. Because deals here span industries with genuinely different operational needs, part of the job is quickly learning enough about a new prospect's workflow to ask a credible technical question in the first call rather than the third. We are looking for a senior solution engineer with strong API fluency, sharp discovery instincts, and disciplined CRM habits so technical context does not live only in your head. The role is fully remote and open globally, paired with account executives across time zones rather than tied to a single regional team. We judge the role by how rarely a signed deal surfaces a technical surprise during implementation, not by how polished any single demo looked.

jobs.title: Frontend Engineering Director
jobs.summary: TidalFrame's immersive collaboration product pushes browsers harder than most web applications ever will, which makes frontend architecture and performance a genuine competitive constraint rather than a nice-to-have, and this director role sets the technical direction for that entire surface. You will make the architectural calls that determine whether the React codebase stays maintainable as the product adds increasingly demanding real-time features, weighing new abstractions against the cost of teaching the whole team to use them well. Web performance work runs through nearly everything: setting performance budgets, deciding which experiences are simply too heavy to ship as designed, and holding that line even when a feature is otherwise ready. Because this is a director-level role, people leadership is a first-class responsibility rather than a side effect of seniority, and you will grow a group of engineering managers and senior engineers while staying technical enough to review the architecture decisions that matter most. You will also represent frontend engineering in cross-functional planning, making sure performance and architectural constraints shape the roadmap early rather than surfacing as a blocker right before launch. We are looking for a director with deep hands-on React experience, a genuine track record improving web performance at scale, and demonstrated success leading engineering managers rather than only individual contributors. The role is hybrid from our Los Angeles office, with the leadership team in three days a week for planning and architecture review. We judge the organization's health by whether senior engineers can ship ambitious features without director-level intervention on every decision.

jobs.title: Senior Product Researcher
jobs.summary: How people actually collaborate inside immersive digital spaces is still an open question, and this senior role exists to study that question directly for TidalFrame's experience platform rather than assume today's product already has the answer. You will run mixed-method research that combines structured interviews with behavioral data from inside the product, since collaboration habits inside an immersive environment often do not match what participants say they do in an interview alone. A significant part of the role is prototyping speculative workflows, building rough interactive concepts that let the team test a future direction with real users well before engineering commits meaningful time to it. Synthesis is where the role earns its keep: turning research and prototype feedback into product strategy recommendations concrete enough that a product manager can act on them directly, rather than a report that gets filed away. You will work closely with product and design leadership to make sure research questions are framed around real upcoming decisions instead of general curiosity about user behavior. We are looking for a senior researcher with genuine mixed-method fluency, hands-on prototyping ability, and strong synthesis and communication skills that hold up in front of skeptical product leadership. The role is fully remote for candidates based in Europe or the United States, with research reviewed in a standing session that leadership is expected to actually attend rather than delegate. We consider a research effort successful when it visibly changes a product decision, not when it confirms what the team already believed.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.summary: TidalFrame's experience platform is expanding into AI-assisted features fast enough that technology strategy and responsible AI practice can no longer be treated as separate conversations, and this executive role exists to own both together. You will set multi-year technology strategy for the platform, deciding where to invest in new architecture versus consolidate what already exists, with enough credibility across the organization that the strategy actually survives contact with quarterly pressure. AI governance is a defined mandate rather than an afterthought: establishing how new AI-assisted features get evaluated for risk and fairness before launch, and making sure that evaluation has real authority to delay a launch when it matters. Security sits alongside AI governance as a first-class executive responsibility, with the CTO accountable for how security tradeoffs get made at the architecture level rather than delegated entirely downward. As the most senior technical executive, you will build and lead the executive leadership team beneath you, hiring and developing engineering leaders who can run their organizations without constant escalation. We are looking for an executive with a genuine track record setting technology strategy at scale, direct experience standing up AI governance practice rather than only using AI tools, and enough security fluency to ask the right questions of a specialist team. The role is flexible, based from London with global reach across the organization, structured around board-level strategy reviews rather than a fixed office routine. We judge success by whether the platform can adopt new AI capability quickly without the governance and security foundation cracking under the pace.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Climate Data Platform
jobs.summary: Wrenfield's data platform team maintains the ingestion pipelines that pull satellite imagery, weather-station readings and industrial sensor feeds into the risk models insurers and utilities rely on every day. This internship places you directly on that team for the length of the program, working alongside two mentor engineers rather than in a separate training track. You will build small services in Python that validate and normalize incoming sensor batches, write SQL transformations against the climate data warehouse, and add test coverage to ingestion jobs that currently rely on manual spot-checks. You will also shadow the on-call rotation for a few shifts to see how the team investigates a pipeline failure when a weather-station feed goes quiet without warning. The wider data platform group is about a dozen engineers split across ingestion, modeling and serving, and roughly half of past interns have gone on to receive a full-time offer at the end of the program. Fundamentals in Python and SQL count for more than finished expertise here, since most of what this specific pipeline needs you will pick up on the job, and genuine curiosity tends to matter more than a polished resume. Interviews consist of a short take-home exercise and a conversation about how you approached it, not a live whiteboard session.

jobs.title: Junior Backend Engineer, Risk Scoring APIs
jobs.summary: The backend team behind Wrenfield's risk-scoring product is expanding the internal APIs that power the dashboards insurance underwriters use to price climate risk on individual properties and portfolios. This junior role is a deliberate first step into professional backend work rather than one assuming prior production experience. You will build and test new API endpoints in Python, fix bugs surfaced through our support queue when an underwriter reports a score that looks wrong, and help keep documentation current as the underlying data model evolves alongside the risk methodology. A mentor engineer reviews your pull requests closely for the first several months, and the team runs a short weekly pairing session specifically for engineers early in their career. The risk-scoring team has roughly doubled in headcount over the past year as more insurance customers have come on board, and this opening is part of that continued growth rather than a backfill. A foundation in Python and relational databases from coursework, a bootcamp or personal projects goes a long way here, alongside a habit of asking questions rather than guessing. Code review is treated as a teaching tool, and the team is genuinely patient with engineers still building judgment about what production code should look like.

jobs.title: Associate Software Engineer, Data Source Integrations
jobs.summary: Insurers, utilities and agricultural customers keep asking Wrenfield to add new external data sources to its climate risk platform, and the integrations squad is the small team that turns each request into a working connector. This associate role focuses on building and maintaining individual integrations against satellite providers, national weather services and third-party sensor networks. Typical weeks involve writing Node.js services that pull and normalize data from a partner's API, adding retry and error-handling logic for feeds that are not always reliable, and verifying output against a sample of known-good historical readings before a connector goes live. You will work closely with a senior engineer who reviews your pull requests daily during your first few months and more loosely once you have shipped a couple of connectors independently. The backlog currently includes about a dozen requested data sources, so there is no shortage of scoped, well-defined work to learn from. Some exposure to JavaScript or another backend language and comfort reading unfamiliar API documentation count for more here than deep prior experience. The team keeps a shared runbook of gotchas from past integrations, usually the first thing a new associate engineer actually reads.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Portfolio Risk Aggregation
jobs.summary: Every night, a set of batch pipelines aggregates fresh weather and sensor readings across thousands of insured property portfolios so underwriters have an updated risk picture by the time they log in the next morning, and this role owns that pipeline. You would extend the batch jobs written in Go as new risk factors are added to the methodology, tune PostgreSQL queries that have started to show latency as the underlying dataset has grown past its original design assumptions, and coordinate with the product team on new report types that tend to ship roughly once a quarter. The role also includes rotating on-call coverage for the reporting subsystem specifically, shared across six engineers rather than the whole platform, so the pager is not constant. Recent history here includes a migration off a nightly cron-based scheduler onto a proper workflow engine, which the team is still finishing the rough edges of, and whoever takes this role will likely finish that work. Comfort with Go and relational databases at production scale is the practical bar for this opening, along with enough familiarity with Kafka to reason about ordering and replay when a pipeline needs to be rerun after a partial failure. Most collaboration happens asynchronously across European time zones, with a single weekly sync kept deliberately short, and the team treats a clean postmortem as more valuable than assigning blame after an incident.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Subscription Billing (Part-Time)
jobs.summary: Wrenfield bills customers on a mix of seat-based and usage-based plans depending on how much climate data they pull from the platform, and this part-time role maintains the billing layer that reconciles subscription events between our systems and the external payment processor. In a typical week you would review reconciliation discrepancies flagged by an automated nightly job, patch edge cases in the Go services that handle processor webhooks, and pair briefly with the finance team to confirm expected behavior before a fix ships. The position is structured around roughly twenty hours a week with flexible scheduling across time zones, which suits someone balancing this against other commitments such as a second contract or study. Go and SQL experience is the practical bar here, along with prior exposure to a payments API, since billing edge cases tend to be unforgiving of guesswork. The role reports to a senior engineer who scopes the weekly priorities so you are not left deciding what matters most on your own.

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer, Underwriter Dashboards
jobs.summary: You would join the small team responsible for the customer-facing dashboards where underwriters and risk analysts explore Wrenfield's climate data, splitting your time between a React frontend and the GraphQL services behind it. Recent projects have included rebuilding a flood-exposure heatmap component that was struggling with larger portfolios and adding CSV export support that several enterprise accounts had requested for months. The team ships in small increments behind feature flags and expects engineers to write their own end-to-end tests rather than relying on a separate QA function to catch regressions. Three product designers and two backend engineers sit alongside this team, and this role is expected to move comfortably between all three groups depending on what a given week needs. TypeScript and React experience carries real weight here, along with enough backend comfort to reason about the GraphQL schema you are building against, since the two sides of this role are genuinely intertwined. Standups are asynchronous most days, with a single video call midweek reserved for anything that benefits from a live conversation.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Climate Data Warehouse
jobs.summary: This position focuses on the transformation layer that turns raw satellite, weather-station and sensor readings into the modeled tables that analysts and customers ultimately query. You would write and maintain dbt models as new risk factors are introduced, troubleshoot Airflow DAG failures that occasionally wake up the on-call engineer when an upstream feed changes shape without notice, and collaborate with a data analyst embedded in the team to validate new metrics before they reach production. The team spends two days a week together in the Berlin office so schema changes can be whiteboarded together rather than argued over in a pull request. The warehouse currently serves several hundred modeled tables and keeps growing as the risk methodology adds new factors, which means naming conventions and documentation carry more weight here than they might at a smaller company. Comfort with SQL and a modern transformation tool such as dbt matters more than any single certification, along with enough Python to script around the edges of the pipeline. The team treats data quality incidents seriously and runs a short retrospective after any that reach a customer-visible report, focused on process rather than individual fault.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Sensor Event Platform
jobs.summary: Billions of sensor and satellite readings flow through Wrenfield's event platform every day, and this senior role is responsible for keeping that pipeline reliable as data volume keeps climbing faster than the original architecture anticipated. You would lead the redesign of a partitioning scheme that is starting to bottleneck under current load, mentor two mid-level engineers on the team through their first significant architectural change, and represent the event platform in cross-team reviews when other teams propose changes that touch shared infrastructure. Prior experience operating a high-throughput streaming system in production matters more here than familiarity with any specific vendor, since the tradeoffs you have already learned the hard way are exactly what this role needs. The team has grown from three to six engineers over the past eighteen months, and this senior hire is expected to help formalize on-call practices that have so far been fairly informal. Go and Kafka experience at meaningful production scale is close to a hard requirement, along with the judgment to know when a redesign is worth the disruption and when it is not. The team works fully asynchronously across European time zones with a light weekly sync, and design documents are expected to circulate for written feedback before any significant change starts. The most recent architecture review took nearly three weeks of back-and-forth before consensus was reached, which the team considers normal for a change of this scale rather than a sign that the process is too slow.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Risk API Gateway (Contract)
jobs.summary: Wrenfield needs a senior contractor for roughly six months to lead a rewrite of the API gateway that fronts every customer-facing climate risk endpoint we expose. Dozens of enterprise customers have built internal tooling directly against the current gateway's quirks over the years, which is exactly what makes this rewrite delicate rather than a simple technical upgrade. The work involves designing a phased migration plan that avoids downtime for those existing integrations, implementing the new routing and rate-limiting logic in Go, and documenting the rollout clearly enough that the permanent platform team can maintain it once the contract ends. You would also run a deprecation timeline past a handful of the largest customers directly, since several of them will need to update their own client code before the old gateway can be retired. Deep experience with Go and API gateway patterns is close to a hard requirement, and just as important is strong written communication, since most collaboration on this engagement happens asynchronously with a distributed team rather than in real time. Progress is reviewed every two weeks against a plan agreed with the engineering director up front, and the expectation is a working handoff rather than an open-ended ongoing engagement. Contractors who have done a similar gateway migration before tend to do best in this kind of scoped, deadline-driven engagement.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Engineer, Climate Data Export Tooling
jobs.summary: This freelance engagement covers the design and build of a self-service export tool that lets enterprise customers pull raw climate and weather data out of Wrenfield's platform into their own warehouses rather than depending on our dashboards alone. You would scope the initial architecture with the product manager, implement the export jobs in Python against our existing data lake, and hand off a working prototype with clear documentation by the end of the engagement window. Several large customers have specifically asked for this capability during renewal conversations, so there is real business pressure behind getting a usable version out rather than a polished but late one. The role suits someone comfortable owning a project end to end with minimal day-to-day oversight, since check-ins are scheduled roughly every two weeks rather than daily. Python and SQL fluency is the practical bar, along with prior experience building data export or ETL tooling against a large dataset, ideally including something at a similar scale to Wrenfield's petabyte-class data lake. Scheduling is flexible provided the milestones land on time.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Data Platform Architecture
jobs.summary: As staff engineer you would set technical direction across the three teams that make up Wrenfield's data platform organization, an area that has grown quickly without much shared architectural review as the company added new data sources and customer segments. Concretely that means writing design documents for cross-team initiatives such as the move to a shared event schema across ingestion and modeling, chairing a monthly architecture forum where teams surface decisions that affect more than their own codebase, and stepping into individual teams' codebases when a particularly hard problem needs a second set of eyes. The organization has roughly thirty engineers today and is expected to add another ten over the next year, which is part of why this role exists now rather than earlier, when informal coordination was still good enough. You would also own the relationship with the infrastructure organization on anything touching shared Kubernetes capacity, since data platform workloads are among the heaviest consumers on the cluster. Deep experience with distributed systems and data infrastructure at scale matters here, along with the communication skill to influence teams you do not directly manage, which in practice matters as much as the technical depth itself. The role reports to the VP of Engineering but carries no direct reports of its own, and success looks like better decisions happening earlier rather than any single deliverable. Interviews focus heavily on a past architecture decision you can walk through in detail, tradeoffs included, rather than an abstract system-design prompt.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer, Climate Data Infrastructure
jobs.summary: Wrenfield is hiring a principal engineer to own the long-term technical roadmap for its climate data infrastructure, spanning ingestion from an expanding set of satellite and sensor providers, storage, and the query layer that every customer report ultimately runs against. You would be expected to identify where the current architecture will break under three years of projected data growth, propose and personally prototype alternatives before committing the wider organization to a direction, and influence hiring and leveling decisions for senior engineers joining the data organization. The company has added three new categories of data provider in the past year alone, each with its own volume and latency characteristics, and that pace is expected to continue as new markets like agricultural insurance open up. Part of the mandate is also external: this role periodically joins customer conversations where a prospective enterprise account wants technical assurance about how the platform will handle their specific data volume before signing. This is an individual-contributor role with wide latitude and correspondingly high expectations for judgment, and it reports directly to the VP of Engineering. A strong track record designing data infrastructure at scale counts for a lot here, along with enough communication skill to make that judgment legible to people outside the immediate team, including on occasion a skeptical enterprise customer. Compensation for this role is discussed directly once mutual interest is established rather than published up front, which is typical for principal-level searches here.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Lead, Platform Engineering
jobs.summary: This lead role oversees the small infrastructure team responsible for the Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines and observability stack that every product team at Wrenfield ultimately depends on. You would set quarterly priorities for two infrastructure engineers, personally drive larger initiatives such as the current migration to spot-instance-based worker pools for batch processing jobs, and act as the escalation point during major incidents regardless of which team's service is affected. Two days a week in the Berlin office overlap with most of the team, which helps considerably on the planning side of the job even though most execution happens independently. The spot-instance migration alone is projected to cut batch compute costs by close to a third once complete, and the finance team is watching that number closely, which puts a bit more visibility on this role than infrastructure work usually gets. You would also inherit ownership of the on-call rotation policy, currently under review after a stretch of incidents landed disproportionately on one engineer. Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code tooling like Terraform is the practical bar here, along with some prior experience leading a small team, even informally. The role reports to the VP of Engineering and is expected to stay close enough to the technical work to make credible calls during a live incident rather than purely coordinating from the sidelines.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Platform Infrastructure
jobs.summary: This is an internal posting for the manager role over Wrenfield's platform infrastructure group as the team grows from four to seven engineers over the next two quarters. Responsibilities include running weekly one-on-ones, partnering with the director of engineering on the hiring plan for the new headcount, and staying close enough to the technical work to make credible calls during incident retrospectives rather than deferring entirely to senior engineers. The role also involves representing infrastructure in the quarterly planning review alongside the other engineering managers, where competing priorities across teams get negotiated, sometimes contentiously given how many product teams depend on the same shared clusters. Growing the team this quickly brings its own risk, since onboarding three new infrastructure engineers at once without diluting on-call quality is a real design problem this manager will need to solve, not just a staffing target to hit. Candidates should already have context on Wrenfield's infrastructure from prior work here, which is why this opening is limited to current employees rather than posted externally, and the expectation is a fairly short ramp-up given that existing familiarity. Two of the three new hires planned for this quarter are expected to be relatively junior, which shifts a meaningful amount of this manager's early time toward mentorship structure rather than pure technical delegation.

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer, Platform
jobs.summary: Wrenfield is adding its first dedicated application security role to work alongside the backend and platform teams directly rather than sitting apart as a separate reviewing function. Customer risk models draw on sensitive geospatial and portfolio data, which makes the stakes around access control and data handling higher than they might be for a typical SaaS product. The job involves running threat-modeling sessions before major features ship, reviewing pull requests for common vulnerability classes across several codebases, and building lightweight tooling that catches issues like hardcoded secrets before they ever reach production. Because this is the first role of its kind at the company, a fair amount of the early work is also organizational: setting up a lightweight vulnerability disclosure process and deciding which SAST tooling is worth adopting rather than inheriting one by default. Experience with secure coding practices goes a long way here along with enough Python to build small internal tools, though the team is open on how many years that represents for a given candidate. Arrangements are flexible between the Berlin office and remote work, and the posting deliberately does not specify a required seniority level so candidates at different stages feel comfortable applying.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Payments Platform
jobs.summary: This internship places you on the ledger team at the center of Thistledown's payments infrastructure, the system other businesses embed into their own products to move money and track balances accurately. You will fix small bugs reported through our developer support channel, write tests around ledger edge cases such as partial refunds and currency rounding that the existing suite does not fully cover, and pair with an assigned mentor twice a week to review your progress against the goals set at the start of the program. Towards the end of the internship you will scope and ship one small feature end to end with support from the team rather than working on throwaway practice tasks. The ledger team is deliberately small, five engineers today, so an intern here gets exposure to production incidents and design discussions that a larger team might shield juniors from. Fundamentals in TypeScript or a similar typed language matter here, along with genuine interest in how financial systems handle correctness, since a wrong balance is a very different kind of bug than a wrong pixel.

jobs.title: Junior Frontend Engineer, Merchant Dashboard
jobs.summary: Business customers manage their entire relationship with Thistledown through the merchant dashboard, from viewing settlement reports to configuring payout schedules, and this junior role joins the small frontend team that maintains it. Early projects typically include fixing accessibility issues flagged in a recent audit, adding missing test coverage to older components before they are touched again, and implementing design tweaks handed off from the design team for the upcoming payout-scheduling redesign. Everyone on the frontend team, regardless of level, attends a weekly design-engineering sync where upcoming changes get discussed before implementation starts. The dashboard has accumulated a fair amount of inconsistent styling from several years of incremental changes, and part of this role's first few months is helping migrate older screens onto the newer shared component library. TypeScript and React fundamentals from coursework, a bootcamp or personal projects are expected, and a mentor is assigned for close review during your first several months.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Payout Processing
jobs.summary: Millions of payouts move through Thistledown's platform every month on behalf of the businesses that embed our ledger, and you would own the service that batches, schedules and retries those payouts against banking rails that do not always respond quickly or predictably. Current work includes reducing duplicate payouts caused by a race condition in the queue consumer during high-volume periods and adding a delayed-retry mode for the subset of banking partners whose rejection responses arrive inconsistently. The service is written in TypeScript on Node.js and backed by PostgreSQL and Redis, and you would share on-call duty with two other backend engineers on a weekly rotation. A handful of banking partners account for a disproportionate share of the retry logic's complexity, and getting to know their specific quirks well is genuinely part of the job rather than an afterthought. Solid experience with Node.js and message queues is the baseline for this role, along with the kind of carefulness that comes from having dealt with money-handling code before, where a subtle bug can mean a real customer does not get paid on time.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Transaction Search
jobs.summary: Support agents and business customers both rely on being able to find a specific transaction quickly across millions of ledger entries, and this role sits on the small team responsible for that search experience inside Thistledown's platform. You would tune Elasticsearch relevance scoring based on real support-ticket feedback, extend the indexing pipeline to cover new transaction types as payment methods are added to the platform, and investigate the occasional slow-query report that comes in from a business customer with an unusually large transaction history. The team is based mostly in Dublin and meets in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays for planning and pairing. Comfort with Elasticsearch or a similar search technology matters here, along with solid backend fundamentals in TypeScript and PostgreSQL. Search volume spikes noticeably at the start of each month when business customers reconcile their books, and the team has learned to schedule any risky indexing changes well away from that window. The role also involves a light amount of on-call, mostly triggered by slow-query alerts rather than outright outages, and the team treats a rising p95 latency trend as worth investigating well before it becomes a customer-visible complaint.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Statement Exports (Part-Time)
jobs.summary: Thistledown needs a part-time engineer to maintain and gradually improve the statement export feature that lets business customers download their transaction history in bulk for their own accounting and reconciliation needs. The work is steady rather than urgent: triaging the occasional export failure reported through support, adding support for a new file format this quarter that a large customer specifically requested, and keeping the underlying export job queue healthy as transaction volume grows. About fifteen to twenty hours a week is expected, with async standups replacing most live meetings so the schedule stays genuinely flexible. Node.js and PostgreSQL experience is the practical bar, along with enough independence to keep a steady backlog moving without close supervision. The export feature currently supports three file formats and roughly a dozen recurring customer requests are open at any given time, so triage judgment matters more here than raw throughput.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Mobile Banking Sync
jobs.summary: Business owners frequently check balances and recent transactions from Thistledown's mobile app while away from a desk, sometimes with a patchy connection, and keeping the app consistent with the web dashboard under those conditions turns out to be a harder problem than it sounds. You would work across both native codebases to fix sync conflicts reported by users, add automated tests around the conflict-resolution logic that has caused most of the recent bug reports, and collaborate with a QA engineer who runs manual scenarios your automated tests are likely to miss. Some prior exposure to either Kotlin or Swift is expected, not necessarily both, and the team is happy to have you specialize in one platform initially. Two office days a week keep the small mobile team aligned on shared sync logic, and the team has found that pairing across the iOS and Android engineers regularly is what actually keeps the two implementations from drifting apart.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Platform Subscription Billing
jobs.summary: Separate from the ledger product we sell, Thistledown itself charges business customers a mix of platform fees and transaction-based pricing, and this role maintains the billing system behind that relationship. Recent work has involved building proration logic for mid-cycle plan changes and closing gaps between our internal billing records and the external payment processor after a handful of reconciliation incidents last quarter that finance flagged as a priority. You would work closely with a product manager and one other engineer, with finance joining planning discussions roughly monthly to flag anything upcoming on the pricing side. A new usage-based tier is planned for later this year, and whoever takes this role will likely be the one designing the metering logic behind it. Python and PostgreSQL experience is the practical bar, along with prior exposure to a payments API such as Stripe's, since the two systems interact in ways that are easy to get subtly wrong.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Real-Time Payment Rails
jobs.summary: Few engineers at Thistledown understand the real-time payment rails as deeply as this role will require, since it sits at the intersection of external banking networks that settle instantly and an internal ledger that has to stay consistent no matter what order events actually arrive in. Current priorities include reducing the rate of duplicate-processing incidents that surface when a banking partner retries a request our system already handled, and extending idempotency guarantees to a newly integrated instant-payments network launching in several European markets this year. This is a highly technical role that benefits from prior experience with event-driven architectures or payment systems specifically, since the failure modes here are subtle and often only show up under real production load. The instant-payments launch is a genuine deadline this quarter, tied to commitments already made to two large business customers, so the first few months carry more schedule pressure than the role typically will afterward.
