You would mentor two engineers newer to distributed systems work and represent the payments team in periodic architecture reviews with other platform teams, where the ledger's consistency guarantees come up more often than almost any other topic. A recent internal audit found one theoretical scenario, never triggered in production, where a specific retry pattern could double-count a payout under unusual timing, and closing that gap cleanly before the instant-payments launch is treated as a higher priority than any new feature work this quarter.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Ledger Migration Tooling (Contract)
jobs.summary: Thistledown is bringing on a contractor for approximately four months to build tooling that imports customer ledger data from three competing payment processors into our platform's internal format. The work includes writing parsers for each source format, handling the inevitable edge cases in historical transaction data that does not map cleanly onto our schema, and building a dry-run mode so our customer success team can preview a migration's results before a business commits to switching providers. You would report to the engineering manager for growth and demo progress every two weeks against an agreed plan. Sales has already lined up a handful of prospective customers who are waiting specifically on this tooling before they will commit to switching providers, so there is real business pressure attached to a working, not just theoretically correct, dry-run mode. Strong Python and data-migration experience is close to a hard requirement, along with the patience to deal with messy real-world financial data that rarely matches its documentation, and prior work specifically with one of the three processors involved would be a meaningful head start. The sales team has also asked, somewhat optimistically, whether the tooling could be extended to a fourth processor before the contract ends, and the engineering manager has been candid that this is unlikely to be realistic within the current scope and timeline.

jobs.title: Senior Frontend Engineer, Card Issuing Console
jobs.summary: The card issuing console lets business customers create, freeze and manage employee cards at scale, and this senior role focuses specifically on the console's performance as customers with thousands of cards have started to report noticeable lag. You would profile rendering slowdowns in the card-list view under large datasets, redesign parts of the virtualization layer that struggle once a business issues more than a few thousand cards, and coach two other frontend engineers on the team through code review on the shared component library. The team spends one day a week together in the London office for design reviews with the product and design teams. One enterprise customer alone now issues close to twenty thousand cards through the console, which is well beyond what the original implementation was designed around, and their feedback has effectively become the team's informal performance benchmark. Strong TypeScript and React experience carries real weight here, along with a track record of diagnosing and fixing frontend performance problems in a production application, not just building new features.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Account Access Control
jobs.summary: Business banking accounts on Thistledown are often managed by several people with different responsibilities, and you would lead the redesign of the access-control system governing who can view balances, approve payouts or manage other users, a system that has grown organically over several years into rules even the original authors now find difficult to reason about. The project involves modeling a cleaner role-based system that still supports existing customer configurations without breaking them, migrating data without disrupting active business accounts mid-transition, and writing extensive tests given how much of the product depends on correct permission checks. Getting this wrong in either direction is costly: too permissive and a customer's employee can approve payments they should not be able to, too restrictive and legitimate business operations grind to a halt, so the redesign has to be conservative about default behavior. Expect close collaboration with a security-minded colleague on the infrastructure team throughout the project, since access control and security review overlap heavily here. Strong backend experience is non-negotiable for this role, specifically including some prior work on authorization or permissions systems, and comfort explaining a migration plan clearly enough that a nervous compliance team signs off on it. Compliance has asked for a dry run of the new permission model against a sample of real customer account structures before any migration begins, which effectively adds an extra validation phase most access-control projects here would not normally require.

jobs.title: Tech Lead, Onboarding and Growth Engineering
jobs.summary: As tech lead for onboarding and growth engineering, you would guide three engineers running experiments across signup, identity verification and the upgrade prompts that convert free accounts into paying business customers. Day to day the role mixes hands-on coding, mostly in the shared TypeScript codebase, with technical planning for the quarter and occasional pushback on experiment ideas that would add too much regulatory or compliance complexity for the expected upside given that this is a financial product. The team is based primarily in Dublin with two remote members across European time zones, and the lead is expected to keep both groups genuinely included in planning rather than favoring whoever is in the room. Identity verification in particular sits in a gray area between growth and compliance, since a friction-reducing experiment there can have real regulatory consequences if it is not reviewed carefully, and this lead is the person expected to catch that tension before an experiment ships. Solid full-stack experience makes a real difference here along with some prior experience leading a small team, plus comfort working alongside compliance requirements that a typical growth team would not usually encounter. The role sits between product and engineering and reports to the VP of Product Engineering, with quarterly OKRs jointly owned by both functions. Performance reviews for the engineers on this team weigh experiment quality, not just shipped volume, specifically to avoid rewarding a flood of low-value tests over a smaller number of well-reasoned ones.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Deployment Platform (Freelance)
jobs.summary: Thistledown is looking for a freelance infrastructure specialist to help modernize its deployment pipeline over an engagement of roughly three months, work that carries extra weight given that deployments here touch systems handling real money. The scope includes migrating remaining services from a legacy VM-based deployment process onto the existing Kubernetes cluster, tightening up CI pipeline reliability that has become a recurring source of complaints from engineers shipping to production, and documenting the new setup for the small internal infrastructure team to maintain afterward. Roughly a third of services are still on the legacy VM process, and those tend to be the oldest and least documented parts of the platform, which is exactly why they have not been migrated already. Scheduling is flexible provided there is meaningful overlap with European working hours for the handoff conversations. Strong Kubernetes and CI/CD experience is what the team looks for first, ideally with some exposure to deployment practices in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment, since a rollback plan matters more here than in a typical SaaS deployment. Two of the legacy services still awaiting migration handle ledger writes directly, which makes them the riskiest part of the whole engagement and the ones the internal infrastructure team has been most reluctant to touch without outside help. Weekly check-ins with the infrastructure lead are the main coordination mechanism, and the freelancer is expected to flag scope surprises early rather than absorbing them silently into the existing timeline.

jobs.title: Security Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: Three engineers split across application security and vulnerability management make up Thistledown's growing security engineering function today, and this internal posting covers the manager role leading them, needed given the compliance bar our payments product is held to. You would set the team's roadmap in partnership with the head of engineering, represent security directly in customer due-diligence calls for larger enterprise deals where security posture is often the deciding factor, and continue carrying a portion of hands-on review work rather than moving fully into management. The team has grown from a single engineer eighteen months ago to three today, largely in response to enterprise customers asking increasingly detailed security questions during procurement, and that trend shows no sign of slowing down. Because the role requires established relationships across engineering leadership and familiarity with our compliance obligations, this opening is limited to internal candidates rather than posted externally, and the expectation is that whoever takes it already knows most of the open items on the team's current roadmap. Two of the largest enterprise deals currently in procurement have named specific security requirements that do not yet have a clear owner, and resolving that ownership gap quickly is likely to be this manager's first real test in the role.

jobs.title: Product Security Engineer
jobs.summary: Reviewing designs before they are built, not only auditing after the fact, is the point of the product security role this posting describes, which embeds with feature teams rather than sitting apart from them, a distinction that matters more than usual for a platform that moves other businesses' money. The role includes running lightweight threat-modeling sessions for new features such as the upcoming instant-payments integration, triaging reports that come in through the company's bug bounty program, and building small internal tools that make secure defaults easier for other engineers to reach for without thinking about it every time. The listing does not specify a required seniority, and candidates ranging from a few years of experience to considerably more have been encouraged to apply for this particular opening. The role reports to the engineering director rather than into a dedicated security organization, which is deliberate: the company wants product security treated as an engineering discipline rather than a separate gate late in the process.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern, Robot Fleet Systems
jobs.summary: Dozens of Fernway robots operate simultaneously inside partner warehouses at any given time, and this internship is based on the fleet software team that keeps them coordinated so two robots never try to occupy the same aisle at once. You will write and test small Python modules within the fleet management service, help build a visualization tool the operations team has been requesting for months to see robot status at a glance, and spend time on the warehouse floor observing how the robots you are working on actually behave in a live facility rather than only in simulation. Fernway pairs every intern with a dedicated mentor engineer for the full duration of the program and expects you to present your work at the end. Solid Python fundamentals and genuine interest in robotics matter more than a finished portfolio, and prior ROS experience is a nice-to-have rather than a requirement. Interns typically rotate through a couple of smaller projects over the course of the summer rather than being assigned a single fixed task, which the team has found gives a better sense of whether robotics engineering is the right long-term fit before committing to a full-time offer either way.

jobs.title: Junior Embedded Software Engineer, Robot Controllers
jobs.summary: The embedded team writes the software that runs directly on the onboard computer of every Fernway robot deployed to a customer warehouse, and this junior role joins that team as its newest member. Early work typically involves fixing sensor-driver bugs found during hardware bring-up on new robot units, writing unit tests for existing navigation modules that have grown without much test coverage, and shadowing more senior engineers during on-site debugging sessions at customer facilities when a fleet behaves unexpectedly. Some coursework or personal-project experience with C or C++ is expected, and a senior engineer reviews your work closely during the first several months. The team values patience with hardware, since bugs here sometimes turn out to be a sensor issue rather than anything in the code. The onboard computer runs a fairly constrained embedded Linux build, and getting comfortable with cross-compiling and flashing firmware onto physical test units is usually the first real skill this role builds in the first month. The Denver office keeps a small fleet of test robots on-site specifically for this kind of debugging, so most early work happens on real hardware rather than purely in simulation, which the team considers a deliberate part of ramping up embedded engineers.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Navigation
jobs.summary: Warehouse aisles get rearranged by customer staff more often than anyone at Fernway would prefer, and you would work on the navigation stack that lets our robots find efficient paths through that constantly shifting layout. Current priorities include improving how robots replan around temporary obstacles like pallets left in an aisle overnight, and reducing false-positive stops triggered by reflective surfaces on certain types of shelving that have caused a handful of support tickets recently. The role involves regular time in a test warehouse near the Denver office in addition to simulation-based development, since some navigation bugs only show up on real hardware. Solid C++ and some exposure to SLAM or robotics navigation concepts matter here, along with comfort moving between simulated and physical testing environments. The test warehouse near the Denver office is set up to mimic several different customer shelving layouts, and engineers on this team rotate through hands-on testing sessions there roughly once every two weeks. A recent customer complaint about robots stalling near a particular type of mirrored refrigeration unit turned into a multi-week investigation that ultimately reshaped how the perception stack handles reflective surfaces generally, and that kind of deep-dive is fairly representative of the harder problems this role takes on.

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer, Fleet Operations Dashboard (Part-Time)
jobs.summary: Operations teams watch robot status, battery levels and task queues in real time through the fleet dashboard, and this part-time role maintains that dashboard as feature requests come in from customer-facing operations staff. Work is scoped in small, well-defined chunks: recent examples include adding a filter for robots flagged for maintenance and fixing a chart that was miscounting idle time during shift changes at one large customer site. Around twenty hours a week is expected, and the role reports to a full-time engineer who prioritizes the backlog so you always know what matters most going into a given week. Solid TypeScript and React skills matter here, along with enough backend comfort to work across the full stack when a fix requires it. Most weeks the work is genuinely light and predictable, though the pace picks up briefly around quarterly customer business reviews when operations staff want the dashboard polished for a walkthrough.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Simulation Environments
jobs.summary: Before any navigation or task-planning change reaches a physical robot, it runs first against the virtual warehouse environments the simulation team builds and maintains, and this role is part of that team. You would extend the simulator to model new shelving configurations that customers have requested for their specific facilities, write regression tests that catch navigation regressions automatically before a change ever reaches hardware, and work with the navigation team to reproduce field issues that are difficult to debug directly on a live warehouse floor. The simulator now models close to a dozen distinct warehouse layouts drawn from real customer facilities, and keeping that library current as customers renovate their spaces is a steady stream of the team's work. Solid C++ and Python matter here, along with familiarity with a robotics simulation tool such as Gazebo, though strong candidates who have used a comparable tool are welcome to apply. The Toronto team meets in person a few days a week to review simulation results together, usually walking through a recorded playback of whatever navigation edge case is under discussion.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Fleet Task Planning
jobs.summary: Balancing speed against battery life and charging-dock availability across an entire robot fleet is a genuinely hard scheduling problem, and this senior role owns the task-planning system that makes those tradeoffs for every pick-and-move job Fernway's robots execute. You would redesign parts of the scheduling algorithm to handle the larger fleet sizes newer customers are deploying, work through tradeoffs with the customer success team when planning decisions produce results operators find confusing or counterintuitive, and mentor a mid-level engineer newly assigned to the team. Strong intuition for optimization under real-world constraints matters more here than familiarity with any specific framework, since the constraints themselves are what make this problem interesting. The largest deployment today runs close to two hundred robots on a single site, well beyond what the scheduler was originally tuned for, and that customer's feedback has become the team's de facto stress test for any new planning approach. Solid experience with optimization or scheduling algorithms is the baseline for this opening, along with enough robotics context to reason about the physical constraints involved. The customer running the two-hundred-robot deployment has agreed to a joint tuning exercise with the engineering team next quarter, which will likely be this role's first opportunity to validate a redesigned scheduler against a real fleet at that scale rather than only in simulation.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Fleet Telemetry (Contract)
jobs.summary: Every deployed Fernway robot streams sensor and performance data back to our cloud, and Fernway needs a contract engineer for about five months to rebuild the telemetry pipeline that collects and stores it. The project involves replacing an aging batch-upload process with a streaming pipeline that supports near-real-time dashboards for operations teams, designing a schema that will scale as fleet sizes grow well beyond current levels, and training the permanent data engineering team on the new system before the contract concludes. Deliverables are structured around biweekly milestones agreed with the engineering director rather than an open-ended scope. The current batch process uploads once every fifteen minutes, which several customers have flagged as too slow to catch a stuck robot promptly, and closing that gap is the main measurable outcome this engagement is judged against. Strong Python and streaming-data experience would serve you well here, ideally including Kafka or a comparable system, along with the ability to hand off cleanly to a team that will own this after you leave.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Sensor Fusion
jobs.summary: You would take ownership of the sensor fusion layer that combines lidar, camera and wheel-encoder data into a single reliable estimate of each robot's position, arguably the piece of software a robot's safe operation depends on most directly. Recent field issues have traced back to sensor timing drift under certain temperature conditions, and resolving that class of problem for good is a primary focus of this role rather than a one-off fix. The position includes periodic travel to customer sites to observe hardware behavior that is difficult to reproduce back at the Denver lab, since some of these issues only show up after hours of continuous operation, often on the night shift when a warehouse runs coldest. Two customer sites in particular, both in climate-controlled cold-storage facilities, have produced most of the recent drift reports, and they are likely to be the first places any fix gets validated. Strong C++ and real-time systems experience is what previous hires in this seat have had in common along with specific prior exposure to sensor fusion or state estimation, since this is not an area where general embedded experience alone is enough. The role reports to the staff engineer for fleet systems and works closely with the hardware team whenever a software fix alone is not sufficient. A firmware-level change to sensor sampling rates is also under discussion as a possible fix for the drift issue, and this role would be expected to make the call, backed by data rather than intuition, on whether that hardware change is actually necessary or whether the fix belongs entirely in software.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Fleet Systems Architecture
jobs.summary: Fleet coordination, task planning and customer dashboards fit together less cleanly than they should at Fernway, an inconsistency that has accumulated as the company scaled quickly from a handful of pilot customers to dozens of live deployments, and this staff role is accountable for fixing that. The work includes writing a proposal for a cleaner service boundary between fleet coordination and task planning that the current architecture blurs together in ways that make changes riskier than necessary, reviewing architecture decisions from teams across the engineering organization, and personally prototyping the riskiest parts of any major redesign before handing it off to the teams who will build it out. The company has roughly tripled its number of live customer deployments in the past two years, and much of the current architectural debt traces directly back to shortcuts taken during that growth spurt, which this role now has the mandate to unwind. You would also weigh in on hiring decisions for senior engineers across the robotics software organization, since staff-level technical judgment is still fairly concentrated in a small group of people. Deep distributed systems experience matters more than any single certification and enough robotics-specific context to reason credibly about hardware constraints; this is an individual-contributor role with broad influence but no direct reports. The role reports to the VP of Engineering and travels occasionally to the Denver office for planning weeks, typically once a quarter.

jobs.title: Engineering Lead, Navigation Team
jobs.summary: The current navigation lead is moving into a cross-team architecture position, and this posting covers the lead role left behind, filled internally given how much context it requires about the present state of the navigation stack. Responsibilities include running sprint planning for four engineers, staying hands-on with the trickiest navigation bugs that come in from the field rather than delegating everything technical, and coordinating closely with the hardware team on sensor placement decisions for the next robot revision currently in design. The next hardware revision is roughly six months out, and decisions made now about sensor placement will be difficult to reverse once tooling is committed, which is part of why this handover is happening earlier than it otherwise might. Strong navigation and robotics experience is the standard the team hires against along with some prior experience leading a small team, even informally, and the posting is limited to internal applicants given the depth of context required from day one.

jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer, Cross-Functional Rotation
jobs.summary: Variety over deep specialization suits whoever takes this rotation-style role, working across navigation, task planning and fleet coordination depending on where the robotics team needs help in a given sprint. Typical work spans debugging an odd navigation edge case one week and adding a small feature to the fleet dashboard the next, with the specific assignment shifting based on what is most urgent across the robotics organization at any given time. The posting does not specify a required experience level, since the hiring team has found that the right fit and genuine curiosity about robotics matter more than years on paper for this particular role. Solid C++ and Python fundamentals count for a lot here along with comfort context-switching between fairly different kinds of problems. Engineers who have taken this rotation in the past have generally moved on to a more specialized navigation or fleet-systems role within a year or so, and the hiring team is upfront that this is meant as a launching point rather than a long-term generalist career track.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Fleet Cloud Platform
jobs.summary: Every deployed robot connects back to a cloud platform for fleet coordination, software updates and telemetry collection, and this role maintains the infrastructure underneath that platform. You would manage the Kubernetes clusters serving fleet traffic, improve the CI/CD pipeline that pushes firmware updates out to robots in the field, and help design safeguards that prevent a bad deployment from reaching an entire customer's fleet at once, since a bad rollout here can strand robots mid-task. The team is based in the Toronto office with three days a week expected in person for planning and incident reviews. A canary rollout mechanism is on the near-term roadmap specifically to reduce the blast radius problem, and this role would likely lead that project. Solid Kubernetes and Terraform experience is what tends to separate strong applicants here and, ideally, some exposure to fleet or IoT-style infrastructure where devices in the field depend on the cloud staying available.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Fleet Coordination Platform
jobs.summary: A platform outage here can strand robots mid-task inside a customer's warehouse, which is why Fernway maintains a small SRE function dedicated to keeping the fleet coordination platform available around the clock, and you would join that team. Work includes improving alerting so incidents are caught before customers notice anything wrong, running blameless postmortems after outages to identify what actually needs to change rather than assigning blame, and gradually reducing the amount of manual intervention needed to recover from common failure modes that currently require a human at all hours. On-call is shared across four engineers on a weekly rotation, which keeps any individual week manageable. The team has cut mean time to recovery by more than half over the past year through better alerting alone, and continuing that trend without burning anyone out is an explicit team goal rather than an incidental nice-to-have. Solid Kubernetes and observability experience matters here along with genuine comfort operating production systems under pressure during an active incident.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Edge Deployment (Contract)
jobs.summary: Local edge computing inside customer warehouses keeps robots operating even when the connection back to Fernway's cloud drops, and this contract role focuses specifically on hardening that layer. Over roughly four months you would harden the local orchestration setup against network partitions that have caused a handful of field incidents, build tooling to remotely diagnose edge-node failures without needing a site visit every time, and document the architecture clearly enough for the infrastructure team to own it long term after the contract ends. Occasional travel to a nearby customer site for hands-on testing is expected as part of the engagement. Remote diagnosis matters more than it might sound, since a site visit today typically means a multi-hour drive and a half-day disruption to warehouse operations, both of which the customer has been vocal about wanting eliminated. Strong Kubernetes and networking experience counts for a lot here along with some exposure to edge or IoT-style deployments where connectivity cannot be assumed.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Fleet and Edge Systems
jobs.summary: Robots and edge devices operating inside customer facilities create a different kind of attack surface than a typical web application, and Fernway is hiring a senior security engineer to focus specifically on that problem. You would lead a security review of the communication protocol between robots and the fleet cloud, work with the embedded team to harden the firmware update mechanism against tampering given that a compromised update could affect an entire fleet, and build the company's first formal incident-response plan covering compromised field hardware rather than only cloud systems. No such plan exists today, which several enterprise prospects have specifically flagged during security review as a gap they expect closed before signing, giving this work a real commercial deadline attached to it. The arrangement is flexible between the Denver office and remote work, with occasional travel expected for hands-on hardware security work. Solid network and embedded security experience is the practical bar here, and prior work securing IoT or robotics systems specifically is a strong plus.

jobs.title: Junior Software Engineer, Developer CLI
jobs.summary: Every Cinderforge customer eventually reaches for the command-line tool and SDKs we ship to interact with our cloud platform, and this junior role joins the small developer-tools team responsible for them. You would fix reported CLI bugs, add test coverage for commands that currently rely on manual verification before each release, and help keep documentation examples in sync as the underlying API evolves, since stale examples are one of the most common sources of support tickets. A mentor engineer reviews your work closely for the first several months before responsibilities widen to include planning input on upcoming CLI features. Solid Go fundamentals and an interest in developer experience specifically matter here, which is a slightly different skill than general backend work. The CLI ships roughly every two weeks alongside the platform's own release train, and a large share of the bug reports the team receives trace back to a handful of commands that predate the current API version, so a good chunk of the first few months is spent modernizing those specific commands rather than writing anything new. Pairing sessions happen twice a week during onboarding, then taper to once a week once you are shipping independently, and the team keeps a running list of recurring CLI rough edges that new engineers are encouraged to add to as they notice them.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Compute Provisioning
jobs.summary: When provisioning fails, customer workloads simply do not start, which makes this role on the provisioning service that spins up virtual machines and containers for Cinderforge customers one where reliability matters more than almost anything else on the platform. Recent projects include reducing average provisioning time by caching common base images and fixing a class of race condition that occasionally left orphaned resources behind after a failed request. You would share on-call for the provisioning service with three other engineers on a rotating schedule, and the team treats provisioning incidents as a top priority regardless of what else is in flight. Orphaned resources alone were costing the company a measurable amount in wasted compute before the current fix shipped, which is part of why leadership pays closer attention to this team's incident rate than to most others. Solid Go and Kubernetes experience goes a long way here, along with comfort debugging distributed failures that do not reproduce easily in a local environment.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Billing and Usage Metering
jobs.summary: Accuracy errors in usage metering have direct financial consequences for customers, and you would take ownership of the pipeline that turns raw resource consumption events into the line items on every customer's monthly invoice. The work includes redesigning parts of the aggregation logic to handle a new pricing tier launching this year, auditing historical data for a discrepancy customer support has flagged twice without a clear root cause yet, and mentoring a mid-level engineer who recently joined the billing team. This role can be based in Europe or the United States given the fully distributed nature of the team, with meeting times rotating to share the time-zone burden fairly. The unresolved discrepancy affects a small number of large accounts and has already prompted one uncomfortable finance escalation, so tracking down its root cause is effectively this role's first real test. Strong Go and distributed systems experience is close to a hard requirement, along with the carefulness that comes from having worked on financially sensitive systems before.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Core Platform
jobs.summary: The infrastructure Cinderforge's own product runs on is distinct from the customer-facing compute platform we sell, and this role helps operate it as the company continues expanding into new regions. You would extend Terraform modules used to provision new regions as the expansion plan calls for, improve monitoring coverage for services that have historically been under-instrumented relative to how critical they actually are, and participate in the quarterly disaster-recovery exercise that tests failover between regions under realistic conditions. The team spends Tuesdays and Wednesdays together in the Austin office, which has become the default time for cross-team planning conversations. Solid Terraform and Kubernetes experience matters here along with genuine interest in infrastructure reliability practices. The most recent region launch took noticeably longer than planned because several Terraform modules assumed configuration that turned out to be specific to the original region, and part of this role's first project is cleaning up those assumptions before the next expansion. The team runs a lightweight version of a reliability review before any new region goes live, and this role would take an active part in defining what that checklist actually covers.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Storage Platform
jobs.summary: Underneath every customer compute instance sits a distributed block and object storage layer, and you would join the storage platform SRE team responsible for keeping it healthy under continuous production load. Day-to-day work includes tuning storage cluster performance based on production metrics that occasionally reveal surprising bottlenecks, participating in incident response when a storage node degrades under load in ways that risk customer-visible latency, and automating the manual recovery steps that currently require a human to intervene at three in the morning more often than anyone would like. The role carries roughly one week of on-call every five weeks, which the team has deliberately kept sustainable. Solid Kubernetes and distributed storage experience carries real weight here, ideally including some exposure to Ceph or a comparable system. The team has a standing goal of reducing manual recovery interventions by half over the next year, tracked openly on an internal dashboard the whole infrastructure organization can see, which gives this role a fairly concrete metric to work against rather than an open-ended reliability mandate. Storage incidents tend to cluster around specific hardware batches more than random chance would suggest, and part of the ongoing investigation this role would inherit is figuring out whether that pattern is real or coincidental.

jobs.title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, Virtual Networking
jobs.summary: Customer workloads reach the public internet and each other across regions through the virtual networking layer this team manages, and this position sits within that networking team. You would help debug latency issues reported by customers running latency-sensitive workloads, extend automation around BGP configuration changes that used to be done by hand and were a recurring source of small mistakes, and contribute to a project modernizing how network policies are applied across the platform as part of a broader push toward infrastructure-as-code. Deep networking expertise is not assumed on day one but is expected to develop quickly given the exposure this role provides. One latency-sensitive trading-adjacent customer in particular has pushed the team to instrument cross-region paths far more precisely than was previously the norm, and their standards have effectively become the team's new baseline. Solid Linux and Terraform experience matters here along with a genuine willingness to learn networking internals on the job.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Kubernetes Platform (Contract)
jobs.summary: Cinderforge's internal Kubernetes tooling has grown into a set of custom scripts that nobody is fully happy maintaining, and this senior contractor role exists to help the platform team migrate it to a proper operator-based model over roughly six months. The engagement covers designing the operator's reconciliation logic from scratch, migrating existing clusters without customer-visible disruption during the transition, and pairing with two platform engineers who will maintain the operator after the contract ends so the knowledge does not leave with you. Weekly demos to the infrastructure director keep the project visible and on track against the agreed milestones. The current scripts have caused at least two near-miss incidents in the past year from operators running them with slightly different assumptions, which is the immediate motivation behind formalizing this into a proper operator rather than continuing to patch the scripts. Deep Kubernetes and Go experience is non-negotiable for this role, specifically including prior work building a Kubernetes operator rather than only operating existing ones.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Observability Consolidation
jobs.summary: Three overlapping metrics systems, each inherited from an earlier acquisition, currently make up Cinderforge's observability stack, and this freelance engagement focuses on consolidating them into one coherent system. Over the course of the project you would design a single OpenTelemetry-based pipeline, migrate a representative set of services as a proof of concept before the wider rollout is planned, and produce a migration guide the broader infrastructure organization can follow afterward without you in the room. The engagement is scoped around a fixed deliverable rather than a set number of hours per week, which gives some flexibility in how the work gets structured week to week. Each of the three legacy systems has its own on-call runbooks and dashboards, none of which agree with each other during a real incident, and untangling that inconsistency quietly is as much a part of this engagement as the technical pipeline work itself. Deep observability experience makes a real difference here, specifically including OpenTelemetry, and comfort designing a migration path other engineers will execute.

jobs.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Platform Reliability
jobs.summary: Reliability work at Cinderforge has historically happened team by team without much shared strategy, and as staff engineer for platform reliability you would set technical direction across the infrastructure teams responsible for compute, storage and networking to change that. Expect to lead the rollout of a company-wide chaos-engineering practice that several teams have discussed but never fully implemented, review the reliability implications of major architecture proposals before they are approved rather than after something breaks, and act as an escalation point during the most serious production incidents regardless of which team owns the affected service. The company has had three incidents in the past year that a basic chaos-engineering practice would very likely have caught before they reached customers, and that track record is a large part of why this staff-level mandate now has executive sponsorship behind it. You would also help formalize an incident-severity framework that different teams currently apply inconsistently, which has made postmortem data harder to compare across the organization than it should be. Deep distributed systems experience is what the team looks for first and enough credibility across infrastructure disciplines to influence teams you do not manage directly. This is an individual-contributor role reporting to the VP of Infrastructure, with no fixed salary range published for this posting.

jobs.title: Principal Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.summary: Cinderforge is hiring a principal engineer to own the multi-year technical roadmap for its core infrastructure, spanning compute, storage and the networking fabric that ties regions together across an increasingly global footprint. You would be expected to identify architectural risks well before they become production incidents, represent infrastructure in the highest-level technical decisions the company makes including those with real business tradeoffs attached, and directly mentor the staff and senior engineers spread across the infrastructure organization. This role is based primarily out of the Austin office with two days a week expected on-site for the cross-team design sessions that tend to happen there. The company plans to roughly double its region count over the next three years, a growth plan that the current storage and networking architecture was not really designed to absorb gracefully, which is the central problem this role exists to get ahead of. Board-level conversations about infrastructure spend increasingly reference this role's roadmap directly, which is a level of visibility principal engineers at earlier-stage companies rarely encounter. A strong track record designing infrastructure at scale across multiple disciplines is the baseline for this opening, not just deep expertise in one area. The last major architecture bet the infrastructure organization made, a multi-year commitment to a particular storage backend, is now being partially unwound at real cost, and this role's first substantive test will likely be earning enough trust from the rest of engineering that the next big bet gets more scrutiny before it is locked in.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Team Lead, Storage Migration
jobs.summary: A multi-quarter project to replace an aging storage backend with a more scalable distributed system is underway, and this lead role covers the storage infrastructure team carrying it out. You would plan the migration in phases that avoid customer-visible risk given how disruptive a storage migration can be if it goes wrong, stay hands-on with the hardest technical problems in the migration itself rather than delegating everything, and represent the storage team in the infrastructure organization's monthly planning review where competing priorities get negotiated. The team is four engineers today and expected to grow by one or two over the coming year as the migration scope becomes clearer. The current backend is already showing capacity warnings on its largest customer shard, which puts a real, if not yet urgent, deadline behind the migration rather than leaving it as an open-ended modernization project. Deep storage and Kubernetes experience would serve you well here along with some prior experience leading a small team through a genuinely risky technical project.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Cloud Networking
jobs.summary: A director-level move elsewhere in the organization has opened up the manager role for the networking infrastructure team, filled here internally rather than through an external search. Responsibilities include running the team's planning and one-on-ones, partnering with product on the roadmap for network-related customer features that come up more often than one might expect for infrastructure, and maintaining enough technical depth to participate credibly in architecture discussions rather than deferring entirely to senior engineers. Given the relationships and platform context required to be effective immediately, this opening is being filled internally, and compensation follows the company's existing internal banding process. The last three managers to hold networking-adjacent roles all moved into it from senior IC positions rather than being hired as managers directly, which shapes how the team currently defines what good technical judgment in this seat looks like.

jobs.title: Director of Security Engineering
jobs.summary: Larger enterprise customers keep asking for additional compliance certifications before they will sign, and Cinderforge is hiring a director to lead its security engineering organization as it pursues them. The role involves setting a multi-year security roadmap spanning platform hardening, customer-facing security features and internal compliance processes that currently lag behind what the sales pipeline now requires, managing two engineering managers, and acting as the executive-level point of contact during any serious security incident. Regular travel to the Austin headquarters is expected even though the broader team works in a hybrid arrangement most weeks. Two specific certifications are already named in signed contracts with pending penalty clauses attached to their delivery dates, which gives this role a harder deadline than security leadership roles typically carry. The organization has roughly fifteen engineers across application security, detection and compliance today, and this director is expected to make the case for further growth backed by a credible roadmap rather than headcount requests alone. A strong track record leading security organizations through a compliance-driven growth phase is what previous hires in this seat have had in common, along with genuine technical depth rather than a purely managerial background. No salary range is listed for this leadership-level opening, consistent with how the company handles director and above searches.

jobs.title: VP of Security
jobs.summary: Reporting directly to the CTO, the VP of Security holds overall accountability for Cinderforge's security posture across the product, the platform we sell to customers, and internal systems, a scope that has outgrown the current lightweight leadership structure. The mandate includes building out a security leadership team as headcount roughly doubles over the next eighteen months, owning the relationship with our external auditors through an upcoming certification renewal that several large deals are contingent on, and briefing the executive team and board on risk at a cadence they have found lacking in the past. This is a fully remote position provided the candidate can travel regularly for board and customer meetings when needed. The board has asked for a formal risk briefing at every quarterly meeting going forward, a cadence the company has never actually sustained, and building the internal process to make that reliable rather than a one-time report is part of the job description in practice even if it is not written down anywhere. Prior experience as a security executive at a company of comparable scale is expected; as with most executive searches, no salary range is published and compensation is negotiated directly once both sides are confident in the fit. The board has also asked, somewhat informally so far, whether the company should commission a second-party security assessment of a key vendor before renewing a major contract, a question this VP would likely be the one to formally scope and answer.

jobs.title: Security Engineer, Cloud Platform Hardening
jobs.summary: Every customer workload ultimately runs on top of shared infrastructure, and Cinderforge is expanding its platform security function with a role focused specifically on hardening that shared layer rather than any single customer-facing feature. Work includes reviewing new infrastructure services for security gaps before launch, building automated checks that catch common cloud misconfigurations before they reach production rather than after an audit finds them, and contributing to incident response when something does go wrong despite those checks. The posting leaves seniority open, since the hiring manager is evaluating candidates across a fairly wide experience range for this particular opening and has said fit matters more than a specific number of years. Solid cloud security fundamentals are the practical bar here, ideally including hands-on Kubernetes security experience. The automated misconfiguration checks this role would build are expected to run against every new infrastructure service before it reaches production, which means false positives carry a real cost in developer trust and have to be tuned carefully rather than left aggressive by default. The team currently reviews a handful of new services each month, and demand for security review has been outpacing the function's current capacity, which is part of why this opening exists now.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Network Management Portal
jobs.summary: Carrier customers configure and monitor their entire SD-WAN deployment through the web portal this role works on, which means a confusing interface here translates directly into support tickets rather than staying a cosmetic problem. Recent work has included redesigning the device-health view after customer feedback that it was too cluttered to use effectively during an active incident, and adding bulk-configuration support for customers managing hundreds of sites at once who had been scripting around the missing feature themselves. The team ships weekly and treats customer support tickets as a primary source of prioritization rather than relying only on a formal roadmap process. One carrier customer manages close to eight hundred sites through the portal alone, and their support tickets have become a fairly reliable early warning system for usability problems before they show up more broadly. Solid TypeScript and React experience is what the team screens for first, along with backend comfort in Node.js, since this role spans the full stack behind the portal.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Configuration Management
jobs.summary: Thousands of physical SD-WAN devices deployed at customer sites worldwide receive their network policy changes through the configuration management system this senior role owns, a system where a bad rollout can take real customer sites offline. You would redesign the rollout mechanism to better contain the blast radius of a bad configuration push following an incident earlier this year that affected more sites than the team was comfortable with, work directly with field engineers to understand failure modes that only show up on real hardware in real customer environments, and mentor two engineers newer to distributed systems work through the redesign. The role also involves periodic collaboration with the hardware team on firmware compatibility as new device models roll out. The incident referenced above affected close to three hundred sites simultaneously and took the better part of a day to fully resolve, and it remains the reference point the team uses whenever someone proposes a change to the rollout mechanism. Strong Go and distributed systems experience is the standard the team hires against, along with a healthy respect for the blast radius of any change to a rollout mechanism. Field engineers who lived through the incident still bring it up unprompted in planning meetings, which the team has come to see as useful institutional memory rather than something to move past too quickly.

jobs.title: Junior Network Operations Engineer
jobs.summary: Glasspoint's global backbone and customer SD-WAN deployments are watched around the clock from the network operations center this entry-level role joins. You would learn to triage alerts, escalate genuine incidents to senior engineers while filtering out the considerable noise that any large network generates, and gradually take on small configuration tasks under supervision as your networking knowledge builds over the first several months. The role works a fixed shift pattern within the London office rather than a fully flexible schedule, since NOC coverage needs to be predictable and someone needs to be watching at all hours. A genuine interest in networking matters here, along with some foundational knowledge from coursework or a certification track and the calm temperament that this kind of monitoring work rewards. Shifts rotate on a fixed schedule that covers evenings and occasional weekends, and new hires typically shadow an experienced analyst for the first month before taking alerts independently. The NOC currently handles somewhere around two hundred alerts on a typical day, the large majority of which turn out to be noise, and learning to tell the difference quickly is really the core skill this role is designed to build.

jobs.title: Network Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.summary: Glasspoint's own physical backbone network sits apart from the SD-WAN equipment we deploy at customer sites, and this role helps operate and gradually automate that backbone infrastructure. Typical work includes writing scripts to replace manual configuration steps that currently rely on tribal knowledge held by a small number of senior engineers, participating in planned maintenance windows for core routing changes that have to be coordinated carefully to avoid customer impact, and documenting runbooks that the wider infrastructure team can follow during an incident rather than needing to page the same two people every time. Two office days a week keep the team aligned on maintenance scheduling, and solid BGP and networking fundamentals matter here along with some scripting ability to support the automation work. Maintenance windows for core routing changes are scheduled roughly once a month and require sign-off from two senior engineers before they proceed, a process this role would participate in from early on even before taking full ownership of a change. The backbone itself spans several physical points of presence across Europe, and understanding the quirks of each one tends to take longer than any amount of documentation can really substitute for.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Monitoring (Part-Time)
jobs.summary: Monitoring coverage across Glasspoint's network infrastructure has lagged behind as the network itself has grown, and this part-time role exists specifically to close that gap. In practice this means building new Grafana dashboards for infrastructure that currently has none, writing small Python scripts to catch conditions the existing alerting misses entirely, and occasionally joining a live incident to help interpret what the dashboards are actually showing to the on-call engineer. Around fifteen hours a week is expected, scheduled flexibly around the core team's working hours rather than fixed to specific days. Solid Prometheus and Grafana experience is what tends to separate strong applicants here along with enough networking background to build dashboards that actually reflect what matters during an incident. The role reports loosely to the staff engineer on the network management platform team, who reviews dashboard designs before they go live but otherwise leaves day-to-day prioritization to whoever holds this seat.

jobs.title: Network Software Engineer, Device Firmware
jobs.summary: This role works close to the hardware, developing the control-plane software that runs on Glasspoint's SD-WAN appliances themselves rather than the cloud services that manage them. You would fix protocol-handling bugs discovered during interoperability testing with third-party network equipment that customers run alongside our devices, contribute to the next firmware release cycle currently in progress, and work alongside hardware engineers when a bug turns out to be a driver issue rather than anything in the control-plane software itself. The role is based on-site at the Stockholm hardware lab, where being near the physical test rigs makes a real difference for this kind of debugging. Interoperability testing currently covers equipment from about six different third-party vendors, and each new customer environment tends to surface at least one combination the lab has not tried before. Solid C and networking-protocol experience is the baseline for this opening, along with comfort working close to embedded hardware rather than purely in software.

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer, SD-WAN Deployment Automation (Contract)
jobs.summary: Deploying SD-WAN to a new customer site currently involves more manual intervention than the team would like, and Glasspoint needs a senior contractor for around five months to build automation that removes those steps. The work covers designing an Ansible-based provisioning workflow that handles the common site configurations without hand-holding, integrating it with the existing configuration management system so the two do not drift apart, and training the deployment team on the new process before the engagement wraps up. Milestones are tracked biweekly against a plan agreed with the head of network engineering rather than left loosely defined. A typical new-site deployment today takes a field engineer the better part of a day; the target for this project is to bring that down to under an hour of hands-on time for the common cases, leaving only genuinely unusual sites requiring manual attention. Strong Python and Ansible experience would serve you well here, along with real networking depth, since automation that does not understand the underlying protocols tends to cause more problems than it solves.

jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Network Management Cloud
jobs.summary: An outage in the cloud services that manage Glasspoint's SD-WAN fleet can leave customer network devices unable to receive configuration updates until service is restored, which is what makes this reliability role higher stakes than it might first appear. The role includes leading incident response for the most serious outages, improving the automated failover between regions that has been tested but never fully relied on in a real production incident, and building better pre-incident visibility so problems are caught before customers notice anything is wrong. On-call is one week in four, which the team has found sustainable given how the responsibilities are shared. The failover mechanism was last exercised in a full game-day drill six months ago and performed well, but nobody on the team is fully confident it would hold up identically under a genuine, unplanned regional outage, which is precisely the kind of doubt this role is meant to resolve. Solid Kubernetes and incident-response experience is the practical bar here along with enough networking background to reason about the systems being protected.

jobs.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Network Management Platform
jobs.summary: The interface connecting Glasspoint's cloud management layer to physical network devices across thousands of customer sites has accumulated real inconsistencies as the product line expanded to support new hardware, and as staff engineer you would set technical direction for fixing that. The work includes proposing a cleaner abstraction between device types that currently require special-cased code scattered throughout the platform, reviewing architecture proposals from teams across network engineering before they are approved, and personally working through the highest-risk parts of any major redesign rather than only advising from a distance. The role is based full-time out of the London office, which the team has found valuable for the kind of cross-team architecture conversations this role requires. Glasspoint now supports six distinct hardware generations in the field simultaneously, each with its own quirks baked into the platform over the years, and consolidating that special-cased code without breaking any of them is the central technical challenge of this role. You would also mentor two senior engineers who have each proposed competing approaches to this problem in the past year without either one being formally adopted, a stalemate this role is expected to help resolve. Deep networking and distributed systems experience goes a long way here, with compensation for this posting discussed directly with the hiring manager rather than published.

jobs.title: Principal Network Software Engineer
jobs.summary: Some of Glasspoint's protocol implementations date back to the company's earliest hardware, and Glasspoint is hiring a principal engineer to guide the technical direction of its network software organization as it modernizes them for traffic volumes those original implementations were never designed to handle. You would be expected to evaluate where existing implementations will not scale to the volumes projected over the next several years, prototype alternative approaches personally before proposing them broadly across the organization, and mentor senior engineers across both the control-plane and cloud-management teams who will ultimately build out whatever direction is chosen. The role calls for two days a week in the London office for the cross-team design sessions that this kind of architectural work tends to require. Traffic through the largest carrier deployments has grown roughly fourfold in three years, and at least one core protocol module is now understood by only two engineers still at the company, which is as much a knowledge-continuity problem as a scaling one. A strong track record with networking protocols and distributed systems at meaningful scale is close to a hard requirement. Whoever takes this role will also inherit an unresolved internal disagreement about whether the next protocol generation should maintain backward compatibility with the oldest deployed hardware or cut that support to move faster, a decision with real commercial consequences either way.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Security Engineer, Network Product Assessment
jobs.summary: Several pending enterprise deals depend on a security certification the sales team needs, and this freelance engagement covers the security assessment of Glasspoint's SD-WAN product line required to get there. Scope includes reviewing the device-to-cloud communication protocol for weaknesses that an attacker with network access might exploit, testing the update mechanism for tampering resistance given how much damage a compromised firmware update could cause, and producing a report with prioritized remediation guidance the engineering teams can act on directly rather than a purely academic findings list. The engagement is expected to run for roughly two months with flexible scheduling around the assessment milestones rather than a fixed weekly schedule. At least two of the deals waiting on this certification are worth pursuing specifically because of their size, which is part of why sales leadership has been checking in on this engagement's timeline more closely than is typical for a security assessment. Strong network security and penetration testing experience carries real weight here, ideally including prior work assessing embedded or IoT-style devices. The last comparable assessment two years ago missed a firmware downgrade vector that a customer's own security team found independently afterward, and that miss is part of why this round is being scoped more thoroughly and given more calendar time than the previous one.

jobs.title: Device Security Engineer, SD-WAN Hardware
jobs.summary: SD-WAN devices and management software sold directly to carrier and enterprise customers have relied mostly on external assessments up to this point, and this role adds dedicated internal ownership of product security for that hardware line. Responsibilities include reviewing new features for security gaps before release, coordinating with an external penetration-testing firm on the annual assessment so findings actually get tracked and closed, and helping triage vulnerability reports that come in through customer channels when a large customer's own security team flags something. The posting does not specify a required seniority level, and the hiring team has said they are open to candidates at a range of experience levels for this particular opening. A genuine interest in network and device security specifically matters here. The role would inherit an existing backlog of about a dozen findings from the most recent external assessment, several of which touch firmware update verification specifically, and triaging that backlog realistically is one of the first concrete deliverables expected in the first quarter. Coordination with the hardware team happens informally today, mostly over chat, and part of this role's early mandate is establishing a slightly more structured review checkpoint before a new device model ships.

jobs.title: Security Team Lead, Detection Engineering
jobs.summary: Watching for suspicious activity across both corporate systems and the infrastructure supporting customer networks is the job of the detection engineering function this lead role oversees, currently three engineers building and tuning the alerting logic that does that watching. You would prioritize the detection backlog for the team, personally investigate the more ambiguous alerts that need experienced judgment to triage correctly rather than a simple rule, and represent detection engineering in the monthly security leadership review where priorities get negotiated against other security work. The team works from the London office with a hybrid-friendly schedule for the rest of security, though this particular role is expected on-site given the operational nature of the work. The detection backlog currently runs close to forty open items, several dating back more than six months, and one of this lead's first real tasks will be deciding which of those are still worth building versus quietly closing as no longer relevant. Solid SIEM and detection engineering experience is non-negotiable for this role along with genuine incident-response judgment. The team has also been asked to start building coverage for a newer class of supply-chain-style attacks against network equipment vendors, an area none of the current engineers have deep prior expertise in, which makes this lead's own judgment about what to prioritize especially consequential right now.

jobs.title: Security Operations Manager
jobs.summary: Four analysts covering detection, incident response and vulnerability management currently make up Glasspoint's security operations team, and this internal posting covers the manager role over that team following an internal restructuring. The role involves running the team's shift and on-call schedule, coordinating the response to any significant incident from the first alert through to resolution, and reporting a monthly risk summary to the head of security that leadership actually reads and acts on. The team absorbed vulnerability management from a separate group only in the last reorganization, and integrating that workflow into the existing on-call structure without overloading any single analyst is one of the first practical problems this manager inherits. Given the operational knowledge required to run the team effectively from day one, this opening is limited to internal candidates who already understand how the team's current processes work.

jobs.title: Director of Product Security
jobs.summary: Product security at Glasspoint has grown organically without a single accountable leader as the company scaled its SD-WAN hardware and cloud management software across new markets, and Glasspoint is hiring a director to change that. Responsibilities include building a small team of product security engineers largely from scratch rather than inheriting an existing one, setting the technical requirements new certifications will demand of the hardware and firmware teams well before those requirements become urgent, and briefing the executive team on product-related security risk each quarter in terms they can actually act on. The role offers a flexible arrangement between the London office and remote work, reflecting how much of the job involves working across already-distributed teams. Entry into two new regulated markets is planned for next year, each with its own certification regime, and this director's first major deliverable is expected to be a realistic roadmap for meeting both without one blocking the other. A strong track record building a security function from an early stage makes a real difference here, along with the political patience to get hardware and firmware teams that do not currently report into security to actually prioritize its requirements. Board-level interest in this expansion has grown since one prospective regulator asked pointed questions during an early exploratory conversation, and part of what this director will inherit is turning that vague board attention into a concrete, fundable plan rather than a standing item that never quite gets resourced.

jobs.title: Junior Software Engineer, Detection Rule Platform
jobs.summary: Security teams at other companies rely on the threat-detection platform Alderbrook builds, and this junior role joins the engineering team that maintains the rule-processing engine at its core, the piece of software that actually evaluates incoming security events against our detection logic. Early work typically includes fixing bugs found in existing detection rules, writing tests for edge cases the current suite misses that a customer or internal researcher has flagged, and shadowing a senior engineer during customer-reported incident investigations to see how the platform actually gets used under pressure. You would spend two days a week in the Boston office during the first year while you build context on the platform. Solid Python and SQL fundamentals matter here, and the team finalizes banding for this entry-level opening on a per-candidate basis. New engineers typically start by fixing well-scoped bugs flagged by the rule-testing suite before moving on to writing small new rules under review, and the team has found that pace works better than throwing someone directly at open-ended detection logic before they have context on how customers actually use the platform. A senior engineer walks new hires through a handful of past customer incidents in the first two weeks specifically to build intuition for what a rule getting it wrong actually costs someone downstream.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Security Alert Pipeline
jobs.summary: Security events from customer environments flow into the alert pipeline this role works on, which evaluates each one against thousands of detection rules in near real time before anything reaches an analyst's queue. Recent projects include reducing pipeline latency that had started to lag during traffic spikes on customers' busiest days and fixing a deduplication bug that was creating duplicate alerts for a subset of customers, which had started to erode trust in the platform's alert volume. The team shares on-call for the pipeline across four engineers, with a clear escalation path for anything touching detection accuracy specifically rather than general infrastructure issues. Solid Python and streaming-data experience is what the team looks for first, ideally including Kafka or a comparable message system. The pipeline processes tens of millions of events on a typical day, and the team has learned to treat any change to the deduplication logic as high-risk given how directly it affects what an analyst actually sees in their queue. New engineers typically spend their first few weeks shadowing the current on-call rotation before taking a shift themselves, and the team keeps a detailed incident log that doubles as informal documentation for how the pipeline actually behaves under load.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Customer Data Integrations
jobs.summary: Cloud accounts, identity providers and endpoint tools at customer organizations all feed security telemetry into Alderbrook's platform, and this role maintains the growing library of integrations that pull that data in. Typical work includes building a new integration for a data source customers have been requesting for several release cycles, fixing authentication issues that surface when a partner API changes without much notice, and keeping documentation current for the customer-facing integration guides that solutions engineers rely on during onboarding calls. You would work closely with a solutions engineer who often surfaces integration requests directly from customer conversations rather than through a formal backlog. Solid Python and REST API experience is the baseline for this opening along with comfort dealing with OAuth flows across a wide variety of third-party providers. The integration library currently covers close to thirty distinct data sources, and roughly a quarter of open support tickets each month trace back to some third-party provider changing behavior without much warning, which makes defensive error handling as important here as the integration work itself. The solutions engineer this role partners with keeps a running list of customer-requested sources ranked loosely by deal size, which tends to be the de facto prioritization signal for what gets built next.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Executive Reporting (Contract)
jobs.summary: Customer security leadership teams review their organization's posture through the executive reporting module this contract role will largely rebuild, and Alderbrook needs a senior contractor for roughly four months to do it. The work involves redesigning the underlying data model to support the new metrics product wants to expose in the next release, building the report-generation service in Python from the ground up, and coordinating closely with a designer on the visualizations themselves so the output is something an executive actually wants to look at. The engagement is structured around a defined scope rather than an open-ended commitment, with progress reviewed every two weeks against agreed milestones. Product has already committed the new metrics to a named release date in customer-facing marketing material, which gives this engagement a firmer deadline than a typical internal rebuild would carry. Strong Python and data-visualization experience would serve you well here for this fixed-scope engagement.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Detection Engine Performance
jobs.summary: The team has been gradually porting the detection engine that evaluates customer security telemetry against Alderbrook's rule library from Python to Rust for performance reasons, and you would take a leading role finishing that migration. The work includes completing the port for the highest-traffic rule categories that still run on the older implementation, benchmarking the new implementation against the old one to catch behavioral differences before they reach customers in the form of a missed or duplicated alert, and mentoring two engineers less familiar with Rust through the transition so the knowledge does not stay concentrated in one person. This role reports to the engineering manager for the detection platform and works closely with the detection engineering team on the security side of the business. The Rust port completed so far has cut evaluation latency by more than sixty percent on the categories already migrated, which is the main evidence the team points to when justifying the remaining migration work to skeptical stakeholders. Strong Python experience and genuine comfort with Rust go a long way here, or a track record picking up systems languages quickly. The remaining rule categories still on the Python implementation tend to be the oldest and least documented ones in the codebase, so a fair amount of this migration work doubles as an informal archaeology project into decisions nobody currently at the company remembers making.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer, Security Data Platform
jobs.summary: Ingesting and storing security telemetry at Alderbrook's current scale has grown considerably faster than the infrastructure team supporting it over the past year, and this role supports the infrastructure underneath that data platform. You would extend Terraform modules for a new storage tier the data team is introducing to handle the growing retention requirements several enterprise customers have asked for, improve CI/CD pipeline reliability that has been a recurring complaint from engineers shipping to production, and participate in the team's on-call rotation for infrastructure-level incidents. Three days a week in the Boston office overlap with most of the infrastructure team, which has made planning conversations considerably easier. Solid Kubernetes and Terraform experience is what previous hires in this seat have had in common along with some exposure to data-intensive infrastructure specifically. Retention requirements vary considerably by customer contract, some as short as ninety days and others well over a year, and the new storage tier this role helps build needs to support that variation without becoming operationally unmanageable. The team has found that CI/CD reliability complaints spike noticeably whenever a large schema migration is in flight, and smoothing that experience out is one of the more visible near-term wins available in this role.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Multi-Tenant Isolation
jobs.summary: A leak between tenants would be a serious incident for any multi-tenant platform, but it carries particular weight for a company whose entire product credibility rests on security, which is the context for this senior role owning the infrastructure work behind keeping customer environments properly isolated. The role includes auditing existing isolation boundaries for gaps that have not yet caused a problem but reasonably could, hardening the Kubernetes namespace configuration that enforces tenant separation across the platform, and working with the security team on a joint review before any change to the isolation model ships to production. Deep familiarity with Kubernetes networking is expected given how much of the isolation model depends on it working correctly. A recent internal red-team exercise found a theoretical path between two tenant namespaces that, while never exploited, was serious enough to become the top item on this role's roadmap before any new feature work is considered.
