Strong Kubernetes and multi-tenancy experience matters more than any single certification, ideally including prior work on isolation specifically rather than general platform infrastructure. The red-team finding also prompted a broader question about whether isolation boundaries should be re-verified automatically after every platform change rather than only during scheduled audits, a policy decision this role is expected to weigh in on directly.

jobs.title: Detection Engineer, Cloud Threats
jobs.summary: Research on emerging attacker techniques only matters to customers once it becomes logic that actually runs reliably against their telemetry, and that translation is the core of this detection engineer role. You would write and maintain the detection rules that form the core of Alderbrook's product, translating raw research into logic that catches real attacker behavior without generating excessive false positives that erode an analyst's trust in the alert queue. Recent work has included building detections for a newly disclosed cloud misconfiguration technique within days of public disclosure and tuning an existing rule category that several customers flagged as too noisy during their quarterly review calls. The role works closely with the threat intelligence team, who supply much of the raw research this work depends on, and with customer-facing teams who relay what customers are actually seeing in production. Turnaround time on a newly disclosed technique is treated as a competitive metric internally, and the team's stated goal is a working detection within forty-eight hours of credible public disclosure, which is often tighter than the research itself is fully mature. Solid SIEM and detection engineering experience is the standard the team hires against along with enough scripting ability to move quickly from research to a working rule.

jobs.title: Security Analyst, Threat Intelligence
jobs.summary: Alderbrook's own detection engineering team and the intelligence briefings shared directly with customers both depend on the threat intelligence analyst role this internal posting covers. Day-to-day work includes tracking emerging attacker groups relevant to our customer base across several industry verticals, writing research that detection engineering turns into new rules within the same sprint when a finding is urgent enough, and contributing to the quarterly threat landscape report customers frequently reference in their own board updates. The most recent quarterly report was cited directly in at least two customer board presentations that came back to the account team as feedback, which has raised the internal bar for how polished and defensible each edition needs to be going forward. Because the role builds directly on relationships formed during a prior internal rotation through both teams, it is open only to current employees rather than posted externally.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, Incident Response (Contract)
jobs.summary: A busy quarter following several new enterprise contracts that include dedicated incident-response retainer hours has stretched Alderbrook's IR practice thinner than usual, and this senior contractor role is meant to relieve that pressure. The work involves leading customer-facing incident investigations from initial triage through to a documented root cause, producing forensic reports customers can share directly with their own leadership without needing translation, and documenting playbooks that the permanent incident response team can reuse on future engagements rather than starting from scratch each time. The engagement runs for approximately three months with the possibility of extension depending on how demand develops over that period. Retainer hours committed to the newest contracts alone already exceed what the current permanent team can absorb without this contractor's help, which is the direct reason the role exists on this particular timeline rather than as part of a normal hiring cycle. Strong incident-response and digital-forensics experience is what tends to separate strong applicants here, ideally including prior client-facing IR work.

jobs.title: Freelance Senior Security Engineer, Red Team Exercises
jobs.summary: Validating that the detections Alderbrook sells actually catch realistic attacker behavior requires periodically attacking the company's own corporate and product environments under controlled conditions, and this freelance engagement covers that red team exercise. The scope includes planning and executing a multi-stage attack simulation against agreed targets without tipping off the defenders ahead of time, documenting which detections fired and which gaps were found during the exercise, and presenting findings to both the security and detection engineering teams in a session where hard questions are expected and welcomed. Scheduling is flexible provided the engagement concludes within the agreed two-month window rather than dragging on indefinitely. The last exercise, run about a year ago, found two gaps that led directly to new detection rules now shipped to every customer, which is the standard this engagement is implicitly being measured against. Strong red team and social engineering experience matters more than any single certification for this freelance engagement.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer, Platform Security
jobs.summary: A security company's product credibility depends on practicing what it sells, which makes this staff role setting technical direction for how Alderbrook secures its own platform an unusually visible one internally. The work includes leading the security review for any major new platform capability before launch rather than after the fact, building automated checks that catch common misconfigurations before they ever reach production, and acting as the technical escalation point during any security incident affecting the platform itself, a scenario the company takes especially seriously given its business. This is an individual-contributor role with company-wide influence but no direct reports, reporting to the VP overseeing platform security. Every new platform capability now goes through a security design review this role would chair, a gate that did not exist eighteen months ago and was added directly in response to a near-miss that almost shipped without one. Deep security architecture experience counts for a lot here and a track record of securing production platforms at meaningful scale.

jobs.title: Principal Security Engineer, Detection Strategy
jobs.summary: Thinking about security from both an attacker's and a defender's perspective is the dual mandate behind this principal role, which owns the long-term technical direction of both the security of Alderbrook's own platform and the detection capabilities it sells to customers. You would be expected to identify strategic gaps in current detection coverage well ahead of customer complaints, prototype solutions to the hardest technical problems personally rather than only writing proposals for others to build, and mentor senior engineers across both the platform security and detection engineering teams who look to this role for technical direction. The role is based in the Boston office with flexibility for occasional remote weeks when travel or personal circumstances call for it. Coverage gaps against a specific, publicly tracked category of cloud-identity attacks have come up in three separate customer escalations this year alone, and closing that gap in a durable way, not just patching the immediate complaints, is the first major project this principal is expected to own. A strong track record spanning both offensive and defensive security work is the practical bar here for this principal-level opening. Two of the customer escalations in question came from the same industry vertical within weeks of each other, which has raised an open question internally about whether the gap is a general weakness or something specific to how that vertical's cloud environments tend to be configured, and answering that question with real evidence is expected to shape the coverage roadmap this role delivers.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Detection Engineering
jobs.summary: Six engineers responsible for the rule library that underpins Alderbrook's core product currently make up the detection engineering team, and this internal posting covers the manager role over that team following a recent reorganization. Responsibilities include running the team's roadmap in partnership with the head of product, staying close enough to the technical work to review the highest-impact rule changes personally rather than delegating every decision, and continuing the mentorship relationships built during a recent internal rotation through the team that several current members have valued. Given the context required to lead the team effectively from day one, this role is being filled internally rather than through an external search. The reorganization that created this opening also merged two smaller rule-review sub-teams into one, so an early priority is reconciling two slightly different review standards into a single one the whole team can work from.

jobs.title: Director of Security Research
jobs.summary: Original research on emerging attacker techniques is what differentiates Alderbrook's detection product from competitors relying purely on public threat feeds, and this director role leads the security research function responsible for producing it. The role involves setting a research agenda balanced between defensive publication value and material customers can act on directly in their own environments, growing a team of five researchers into a larger and more specialized group over the coming year, and representing Alderbrook at industry conferences where the team's research is often presented to a technical audience that includes both peers and prospective customers. The arrangement is flexible between the Boston office and remote work, with regular travel expected for conferences throughout the year. Two pieces of research published this past year were picked up by industry press well beyond the company's usual reach, and marketing has since started treating research output as a measurable channel in its own right, which raises the profile and scrutiny attached to whatever this director's team publishes next. A strong personal research track record goes a long way here along with some prior experience leading a research team. One of the two widely cited pieces was actually a fairly small internal finding that only became notable after a researcher pushed to publish it externally against some initial internal skepticism, and this director is expected to get better at spotting that kind of underestimated work earlier rather than relying on outside attention to reveal it after the fact.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer, Vehicle Telemetry
jobs.summary: Fernwood Fleet Analytics ingests location, speed, and diagnostic signals from roughly forty thousand vehicles across a dozen European fleet operators, and this engineer owns the pipelines that turn that raw telemetry into something the rest of the company can trust. The vehicle telemetry stack runs on Kafka and Airflow, and it has been straining under growth as several large fleets onboarded within the same quarter, so a near-term priority is redesigning the ingestion layer to handle bursty traffic without dropping records during peak commuting hours. Day to day work includes maintaining existing pipelines, building new ones as fleets add sensor types such as tire-pressure or battery-health monitors, and working with the data science team to make sure telemetry arrives clean enough for their predictive maintenance models. On-call rotations are shared across three engineers and cover business hours only, with a lightweight escalation path for anything more serious. Strong SQL and real experience with streaming systems at meaningful scale matter more here than familiarity with any particular vendor tool. Progress on this team is tracked through pipeline uptime and the freshness of data reaching downstream dashboards rather than lines of code shipped. The team runs a short weekly review of any incident from the prior week, not to assign blame but to catch the same class of failure before it recurs across a different fleet's data feed.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Fleet Utilization
jobs.summary: The fleet utilization figures that operations managers check every morning depend on a chain of dbt transformations that has grown considerably since Fernwood's early days, and this analytics engineer will keep that chain reliable as more fleets and vehicle types get added to the platform. Much of the work involves rebuilding older models that were written quickly to unblock a specific customer request and have since become fragile, adding tests so a bad upstream data load gets caught before it reaches a dashboard rather than after an operations manager notices something looks wrong. The role also includes documenting how core metrics such as utilization rate and idle time are actually calculated, since three different teams have historically arrived at slightly different numbers depending on which query they happened to copy years ago. Because Fernwood's fleets operate across different countries with different reporting conventions, some models need to account for local regulatory differences in how downtime gets classified for compliance purposes. The analytics engineer reports to the data platform lead and works closely with the data scientists who build forecasting models on top of these same tables. Comfort working with real-world data that arrives late, duplicated, or occasionally out of order is more valuable here than deep expertise in any single tool. Fully remote work across European time zones is supported, with a few hours of daily overlap expected for team syncs and pairing sessions.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Route Optimization
jobs.summary: Route optimization sits at the center of what makes Fernwood's platform valuable to fleet operators, since even small improvements in how delivery and service routes are sequenced translate directly into fuel savings and fewer missed appointment windows for the businesses that pay for the product. This engineer will work on the models that generate route suggestions, which currently blend a classical optimization solver with a learned component that predicts realistic travel times from historical telemetry rather than static map data alone. Recent work has focused on improving prediction accuracy in dense urban areas where traffic patterns vary enormously by time of day, and on making the solver fast enough to re-optimize routes mid-day when a driver falls behind schedule or a new stop gets added unexpectedly. The role involves both applied modeling work, such as experimenting with approaches to travel-time prediction, and the engineering of packaging models so they run reliably inside the production route-planning service without timing out under load during rush hour. Because route changes affect real drivers and their schedules, the team runs new approaches through a shadow-mode comparison against the current system before anything goes live to customers. Familiarity with combinatorial optimization, not just standard supervised learning, is genuinely useful given the nature of the problem being solved here. The team is small, currently three engineers plus one applied scientist, and works asynchronously across several European countries with a couple of overlapping hours reserved for joint debugging sessions each week. Success on this team is measured less by model accuracy in isolation and more by whether fleet operators actually see fewer late arrivals after a new version ships.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist, Predictive Maintenance
jobs.summary: Vehicle breakdowns are expensive for Fernwood's customers, both in repair cost and in missed jobs, and the predictive maintenance program exists to flag likely failures before a vehicle actually strands a driver on the road. As the most senior individual contributor on this program, this data scientist sets the technical direction for how failure-risk models are built, validated, and eventually trusted enough that fleet managers act on their warnings instead of ignoring them. Recent work has included redesigning the model that predicts battery degradation in electric vans after early versions produced too many false alarms during winter months, and building a framework for evaluating whether a given warning actually would have prevented a breakdown in hindsight. Beyond hands-on modeling, this person mentors two mid-level data scientists, reviews methodology across the wider data science team, and pushes back constructively when a customer request does not hold up statistically once examined closely. The role requires genuine comfort with survival analysis and time-to-event modeling, not just standard classification techniques, given how the underlying problem is structured. Because false alarms erode trust quickly, the team places heavy weight on calibration and on presenting uncertainty honestly rather than a single confident number.

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer
jobs.summary: Every product feature at Fernwood, from utilization dashboards to route optimization, ultimately depends on a shared data platform that has to serve very different workloads, from streaming telemetry to nightly batch reporting, without one workload starving another. This engineer will own pieces of that shared infrastructure, including the Snowflake warehouse, the orchestration layer that schedules hundreds of jobs each night, and the access controls that keep customer fleet data properly separated between accounts. A recurring theme in the role is diagnosing why a particular job is slow or flaky, which often means digging through warehouse query plans or orchestration logs rather than writing new code from scratch. The engineer will also help onboard new data sources as Fernwood adds fleet operators in new countries, each of which tends to bring its own quirks in how vehicles report data. Because the platform underpins customer-facing features, changes are rolled out carefully with monitoring in place before anything reaches production traffic. Comfort working independently on infrastructure problems with limited hand-holding is expected given the small size of the platform team. The team keeps a running log of past incidents and the fixes that followed, which has quietly become the closest thing Fernwood has to a platform runbook.

jobs.title: Junior Data Analyst, Fleet Operations
jobs.summary: This entry-level role gives someone early in their analytics career direct exposure to how fleet operators actually run their day-to-day business, rather than a purely internal reporting function detached from customers. The analyst will build recurring dashboards for two or three fleet operator accounts, help prepare short summaries ahead of quarterly business reviews, and gradually take on small ad hoc analysis requests, such as investigating why one region shows unusually high idle time, as confidence grows over the first several months. Senior analysts on the team review all customer-facing output before it goes out, so there is structured support built into the workflow rather than being left to figure things out alone. No prior experience with fleet or logistics data is required, though comfort with SQL from coursework or a previous internship is expected on day one.

jobs.title: Lead MLOps Engineer
jobs.summary: Fernwood is consolidating several fleet-specific model deployment setups, built independently over the past two years as different customer pilots demanded quick turnaround, into a single internal platform that the whole applied science team can rely on. This lead role owns that migration end to end, from initial design through the last customer-specific pipeline being retired. The engineer will design the shared infrastructure for packaging, deploying, and monitoring models, set technical standards for how model performance gets tracked in production, and coordinate a small rotating team of engineers pulled from different fleet-facing pods for the duration of the project. Trade-offs between short-term customer deadlines and the longer migration timeline come up constantly in planning conversations, so comfort navigating prioritization disagreements matters as much as systems design skill. A recent early win was cutting the time to deploy a new route-optimization model version from roughly two weeks to under a day. Prior experience standardizing infrastructure across teams that each have their own competing priorities is a strong plus for this role. Migration progress is tracked pod by pod on a shared board visible to the whole applied science team, partly to maintain momentum and partly so nobody is surprised when their pipeline's turn comes up.

jobs.title: Data Science Manager, Mobility Insights
jobs.summary: Managing a team of six data scientists spread across telemetry, route optimization, and predictive maintenance, this role balances hands-on technical involvement with enough distance to let each scientist own their area of the roadmap. The manager runs weekly one-on-ones, reviews major analytical deliverables for methodological soundness before they inform a customer-facing feature, and works with account leads to staff upcoming projects against the team's specific skills and interests rather than whoever happens to be free. A recent focus has been improving how the team documents modeling assumptions after a disagreement with a fleet customer about how a maintenance risk score was calculated, which took longer than it should have to resolve because the original reasoning was not written down anywhere. Direct hands-on experience with mobility or telemetry data is expected alongside the people-management background, since the team looks to this person for technical judgment calls, not just scheduling and reviews. Hiring is a meaningful part of the role this year as the team is expected to grow by two more scientists.

jobs.title: Director of Data Science
jobs.summary: As director, this person sets technical standards across all of Fernwood's data science pods and represents the practice directly in conversations with prospective enterprise fleet customers during the sales process, where technical credibility often determines whether a pilot gets approved. The role involves reviewing proposed methodologies for new customer engagements before commitments are made, resolving disagreements between managers about how scarce data science time gets allocated across competing fleet accounts, and building out a more formal career ladder for a team that has roughly tripled in size over the past two years without one. Because this posting is limited to internal candidates, familiarity with Fernwood's existing customer base, technical stack, and delivery model is assumed rather than something to be learned on the job over the first several months. The director also sits on the extended leadership team that sets company-wide quarterly priorities, which means representing data science interests in planning conversations that are not purely technical. A short quarterly note summarizing what the team learned, not just what it shipped, goes out to the wider company, partly to keep other departments aware of what the data actually shows about fleet performance.

jobs.title: Data Science Intern
jobs.summary: This six-month internship pairs a student or recent graduate with a mentor on the predictive maintenance team, giving them a realistic view of what applied analytics work looks like outside of coursework and closer to how a real fleet customer experiences the product. Early weeks focus on getting comfortable with Fernwood's internal data stack and shadowing calls with fleet operators, after which the intern takes ownership of a small, well-scoped analysis with regular check-ins from their mentor rather than being left to sink or swim. Past interns have contributed to churn analysis for smaller fleet accounts, cleanup of inconsistent maintenance-log data, and prototyping a simple dashboard now used internally by the customer success team. No prior professional experience is required, though coursework in statistics, computer science, or a related field is expected.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Rider Experience
jobs.summary: Brought on for an initial six-month contract, this analyst supports the product team responsible for the driver-facing mobile app used by thousands of drivers across Fernwood's customer fleets every day. Work includes tracking feature adoption after each app release, running lightweight in-app surveys with drivers, and turning findings into short write-ups the product manager can act on within a sprint or two rather than waiting for a quarterly report. Because the app is used across every fleet Fernwood serves, small usability problems tend to surface quickly through support tickets, so there is a steady stream of concrete, specific questions to investigate rather than open-ended exploration. The analyst will also help set up a lightweight experimentation framework for testing small changes to the app's daily check-in flow. The contract may convert to a permanent role depending on roadmap needs for the second half of the year.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Fleet Platform
jobs.summary: Fernwood's customer-facing fleet management portal has grown well past its original scope over several years of incremental feature additions, and this role exists to bring some coherence back to its roadmap after growth outpaced the team's original planning process. The product manager will interview fleet operators about recurring pain points, many of which turn out to be workarounds for gaps in the portal rather than genuinely new feature requests, prioritize a backlog that has been managed somewhat informally until now, and work with a team of four engineers to ship improvements on a steady monthly cadence. Because the portal directly affects how efficiently a customer runs their fleet, changes are validated with a handful of pilot customers before wider release. A current initiative involves consolidating three overlapping reporting views that different customer segments requested independently over time. Experience turning informal, scattered feedback into a structured and defensible roadmap is valuable here.

jobs.title: Product Operations Lead
jobs.summary: Keeping the rhythm of Fernwood's product team predictable falls to this role: sprint planning, release notes, and communication with fleet account managers about upcoming platform changes all run through product operations rather than being handled ad hoc by whichever product manager remembers to send an update. The person in this seat will also maintain a lightweight intake process for feature requests coming from customer-facing staff, which currently arrive through an inconsistent mix of chat messages, spreadsheets, and hallway conversations that are easy to lose track of. Flexible scheduling is available given the coordination-heavy nature of the work, which spans product, engineering, and customer success teams working across different time zones. A background in program or project coordination within a software company translates well into this position, more so than prior product management experience itself.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Driver App
jobs.summary: Engaged on a freelance basis for an initial quarter, this researcher will run a study into how drivers actually use Fernwood's mobile app during a shift versus how the check-in and route-acceptance flows were originally designed to be used, which internal teams suspect have started to diverge. The engagement includes conducting roughly a dozen contextual interviews with drivers across two or three fleet customers, synthesizing findings into a report for the product manager, and presenting recommendations to the wider product team at the end of the engagement. Prior research into field or frontline worker apps used in vehicles or on the move is preferred over pure office-based consumer research experience, since drivers are often interacting with the app one-handed while parked briefly between stops. There is potential for follow-on freelance work depending on what the findings surface for the next planning cycle.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Dispatch Console
jobs.summary: Dispatchers at Fernwood's fleet customers spend entire shifts inside the dispatch console, assigning jobs, monitoring vehicle status, and reacting to delays, which makes this one of the more operationally demanding interfaces the design team owns. This designer will lead a redesign of the console's job-assignment screen, which was assembled quickly under deadline pressure two years ago and has since accumulated inconsistent patterns that make training new dispatchers harder than it needs to be. The work involves interviewing dispatchers directly about their workflow during live shifts, prototyping alternatives that reduce the number of clicks needed for common actions, and running usability sessions with dispatchers from two pilot customers before anything rolls out more broadly. The designer will also start a lightweight design system so future dispatch features do not repeat the same inconsistencies that prompted this redesign in the first place. Comfort designing for dense, information-heavy, real-time screens matters more here than portfolio polish alone. Prototypes get tested with dispatchers still on an active shift where scheduling allows, since a five-minute session between calls tends to surface more honest reactions than a longer session booked well in advance.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Crop Yield Models
jobs.summary: Loamwell combines satellite imagery, soil sensor readings, and weather data to give grain and row-crop farmers a season-long yield forecast they can plan around, and this engineer will work on the models at the center of that forecast. The current model architecture blends a gradient-boosted baseline with a newer deep learning component trained on multi-spectral satellite imagery, and this role involves improving the deep learning piece so it handles cloud cover and partial-field damage from hail or flooding more gracefully than the current version does. Because the forecast directly influences decisions farmers make about grain contracts and storage, accuracy and honest uncertainty estimates matter more than squeezing out marginal gains on an offline benchmark. The engineer will also work with the research scientist team to incorporate new data sources as they become available, most recently a network of ground-based soil moisture sensors rolled out across several pilot regions this spring. This is a fully remote position open to candidates anywhere in the United States, with quarterly in-person gatherings for the broader engineering team. Model changes go through a shadow season against the previous version before fully replacing it, since a forecast that looks better on paper still needs to prove itself against a real season's worth of weather before growers should be asked to trust it.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Remote Sensing
jobs.summary: This scientist joins the small research group responsible for turning raw satellite and aerial imagery into features the rest of Loamwell's models can actually use, which is a less glamorous but foundational piece of how the company's yield and health forecasts get built. Typical work includes evaluating new imagery providers as they become available, developing methods to detect early signs of crop stress from spectral signatures before it becomes visible to the eye during a field visit, and validating those methods against ground-truth data collected by Loamwell's small agronomy team during the growing season. The team publishes internal findings on a biweekly cadence that inform which techniques the applied ML engineers eventually build into production features. Because a full growing season only happens once a year, careful experiment design matters enormously here, since a mistake in a data pipeline might not be caught until the following spring. Candidates should be comfortable moving between hands-on data analysis and writing code that other engineers will eventually build on, rather than treating research as separate from production work. The team keeps a shared log of which imagery sources and techniques were tried and rejected each season, since institutional memory here otherwise tends to evaporate between one growing season and the next.

jobs.title: Principal Data Scientist, Agronomic Modeling
jobs.summary: As the most senior individual contributor on the science side, this person sets technical direction for how Loamwell models the underlying agronomy behind its recommendations, deciding where deeper research is likely to change what the company tells farmers versus where existing approaches are already good enough. Recent work has involved rebuilding the nitrogen recommendation model after several agronomists flagged that it performed poorly on fields with unusual soil composition, which required going back to first principles on how the model represented soil chemistry rather than simply retraining on more data. The role carries no formal management responsibility but does involve mentoring several scientists and engineers informally, reviewing methodology across the research team, and occasionally meeting with large grower customers to explain how a particular recommendation was reached when a farmer's own field experience seems to contradict it. Deep domain knowledge in agronomy or soil science, not just machine learning technique, is expected given how central getting the underlying science right is to the company's credibility with farmers. The role is based at Loamwell's Fort Collins office given the frequency of in-person collaboration with the agronomy team, though some remote flexibility is available outside of the growing season. Progress here is judged less by publication output and more by whether a recommendation, once shipped, actually holds up across a full growing season in the field.

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer, Sensor Networks
jobs.summary: Loamwell's soil moisture and weather sensor network has grown from a handful of pilot fields to several thousand devices scattered across farms with spotty rural connectivity, and this engineer will own the infrastructure that gets readings from those devices into a usable warehouse despite unreliable links. The role involves building resilient ingestion pipelines that can handle devices going offline for days at a time and catching up once connectivity returns, rather than simply dropping missed readings, and working with the hardware team to understand new sensor types before they ship at scale. Because farms sit in different time zones and report on their own local schedule, timestamp handling and deduplication logic need to be treated carefully rather than as an afterthought. The engineer will also build monitoring so the team is alerted when a meaningful cluster of devices in one region goes dark, which has historically been discovered too late through farmer complaints instead. Experience with intermittent or unreliable connectivity scenarios, such as IoT deployments in remote areas, is a strong advantage for this role.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Field Trial Analysis
jobs.summary: Loamwell runs dozens of field trials each growing season to validate whether a new recommendation, whether about seed variety, fertilizer timing, or irrigation scheduling, actually improves outcomes compared to a grower's usual practice. This data scientist will design and analyze those trials, working closely with the agronomy team that manages the physical plots and the growers who host them on their own land. Because field trials cannot simply be rerun if something goes wrong partway through a season, careful upfront design and monitoring for issues like uneven irrigation or accidental treatment mix-ups matter enormously. The role also involves building reusable statistical tooling so smaller trials do not require a dedicated analyst from scratch each time a question comes up mid-season. A recurring challenge is explaining trial results to growers in terms they find genuinely useful rather than academic statistical language that does not translate to a farming decision. Prior experience with agricultural or environmental field experiments is preferred over strictly lab-based research backgrounds. Every trial design gets a second set of eyes from another scientist before it goes into the ground, since a flawed design cannot be fixed once planting has started and the season is effectively lost. Results are shared with the hosting growers directly and in person where possible, partly out of courtesy and partly because growers often notice contextual details, like a drainage issue in one corner of a field, that never made it into the trial notes.

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Irrigation Systems
jobs.summary: Water is the single most constrained input for many of Loamwell's grower customers, particularly in drought-affected regions, and the irrigation optimization product exists to help growers use less water while protecting yield. This staff engineer will anchor the technical direction for that product, currently working on a shared modeling framework that several regional irrigation models can plug into instead of each being built from scratch by a different engineer with different assumptions. Because the work spans research and production concerns, the engineer will spend real time both reading current agronomic and hydrology literature and reviewing pull requests from more junior teammates who are extending the framework to new crop types. A recent milestone was shipping an irrigation scheduling recommendation for almond orchards, a crop with very different water needs than the row crops the original framework was built around. This position is open to candidates anywhere given the asynchronous, research-heavy nature of the work, though some travel to grower sites during the growing season should be expected a few times a year.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Crop Disease Detection
jobs.summary: Hired for a focused four-month engagement, this contractor will help Loamwell evaluate whether a newer generation of computer vision models can reliably flag early signs of common fungal diseases from drone imagery, something the current rules-based detection system struggles with outside of a narrow set of well-documented conditions. Work includes benchmarking candidate models against a labeled dataset built from several seasons of confirmed disease outbreaks, running field validation against a small set of pilot farms during the current growing season, and writing up comparative findings for the science team to decide whether to invest further. The contract has a narrow, well-defined scope rather than open-ended research, which suits someone who wants meaningful applied computer vision work without a long-term commitment tied to the company. Because disease outbreaks can spread quickly once detected late, false negatives are weighted much more heavily than false positives when evaluating any candidate approach. Strong written communication is important since findings will be read by agronomists as well as engineers.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: This manager leads a team of five engineers responsible for taking Loamwell's research models, whether for yield forecasting, disease detection, or irrigation, from validated prototypes into features that actually run reliably during a live growing season when farmers are depending on them. Beyond the usual rhythm of one-on-ones and performance conversations, the role involves negotiating scope with the research team, who sometimes underestimate what it takes to productionize a promising result, and prioritizing engineering work against a calendar that does not forgive slipped deadlines the way a typical software launch might, since a missed planting-season deadline effectively means waiting a full year. A recent priority has been reducing the gap between a model being validated in research and reaching a farmer-facing feature, which had stretched to nearly three months during last year's crunch. Prior hands-on machine learning engineering experience is expected alongside people management skills, since the team looks to this person for technical judgment on tricky production issues, not just process. Hiring two additional engineers before the next growing season is a meaningful part of this year's mandate. The manager also owns the postmortem process for any production incident that touches a farmer-facing recommendation, since those write-ups have become the main way the team accumulates institutional knowledge across growing seasons.

jobs.title: VP of Data and AI
jobs.summary: Reporting to the CEO, this executive owns the overall technical strategy for Loamwell's science and engineering organization, including decisions about which sensor investments, imagery providers, and modeling approaches the company standardizes on for the next several growing seasons. The role involves regular participation in conversations with large grower cooperatives and agricultural retailers where technical credibility matters as much as the underlying roadmap, since these customers often have their own agronomists who will press hard on methodology. Because this posting is restricted to internal candidates, deep familiarity with Loamwell's existing technical stack, science team structure, and grower relationships is assumed rather than something to build from scratch. The successful candidate will also represent the company at a small number of agricultural technology conferences each year and will need to balance long-term research investment against the shorter commercial timelines the sales team is pushing for. Significant experience operating at an executive level in a company with a genuine seasonal cadence, rather than a continuous release cycle, matters more here than experience at a larger, more bureaucratic organization. This person also chairs the annual planning session where the science and commercial teams jointly decide what the next growing season's technical bets should be.

jobs.title: Junior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.summary: A recent graduate joining this role gets hands-on exposure to production machine learning systems under the guidance of a senior engineer mentor, working across whichever of Loamwell's model families needs extra support in a given month. Early responsibilities focus on writing and testing data preprocessing code, fixing small bugs in existing pipelines, and gradually taking on larger pieces of a project such as adding a new feature to the yield forecasting pipeline as familiarity grows over the first few months. The team runs a structured onboarding program during the first month that pairs technical ramp-up with a couple of days visiting a partner farm to see how the technology actually gets used in the field, which most new hires find genuinely clarifying. A degree in computer science, statistics, or a related field is preferred, though relevant coursework or personal projects involving agricultural or environmental data will also be considered seriously.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Farm Data Platform
jobs.summary: Growers who use Loamwell often want their field data to flow into other tools they already rely on, from accounting software to equipment telemetry systems, and this product manager owns the data platform and API layer that makes those integrations possible. The role involves running a regular roadmap review with engineering leads, gathering integration requirements from both growers and the third-party software vendors who build on top of Loamwell's API, and making prioritization calls when a request from one large partner competes with broader platform health work. A recent project involved rebuilding the field-boundary API after several partners reported inconsistent results depending on how a field's shape had been drawn, which required rethinking how the underlying geospatial data was stored rather than patching the symptom. Because most users of this platform are technical staff at partner companies rather than growers themselves, documentation quality and API design discipline matter more here than they might for a typical consumer-facing product. A technical background strong enough to hold your own in architecture discussions with partner engineers is expected. The role also maintains a public changelog for the API, since partner engineering teams have said repeatedly that silent changes, more than any single bug, are what erode their trust in the platform.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Grower Tools
jobs.summary: Hired on a six-month contract, this product manager will lead a focused effort to simplify the mobile app growers use in the field to log observations, view field-level recommendations, and report issues back to their agronomist. The scope includes auditing existing usage data to find where growers abandon a task partway through, prioritizing a short list of fixes with a small engineering team, and coordinating a beta program with a handful of pilot farms before wider release ahead of next season. This is a well-bounded piece of work rather than ongoing roadmap ownership, which suits someone looking for contract engagements with a clear deliverable and a defined end date. Because growers are often using the app outdoors in bright sunlight or with gloves on, usability constraints here are more physical and environmental than typical mobile product work. Prior experience with field-facing or frontline-worker mobile products is preferred given how different these constraints are from office-based software.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Grower Mobile App
jobs.summary: This freelance engagement focuses on understanding why adoption of Loamwell's grower mobile app plateaus a few weeks after a farm first signs up, a pattern the product team has seen repeatedly in usage data but has not yet investigated directly with actual growers. The researcher will design and conduct a mix of on-farm interviews and short diary studies with growers who fit this pattern, ideally observing them using the app during real fieldwork rather than only in a follow-up call, then present synthesized findings the product team can act on for the next release. Because participants are often in rural areas with limited connectivity and unpredictable schedules tied to weather and fieldwork, flexible and sometimes short-notice scheduling is a genuine requirement of this engagement rather than a nice-to-have. Prior experience researching agricultural, field-service, or other physically demanding work contexts is preferred over purely office-based consumer research backgrounds. The engagement is expected to run roughly eight weeks with a possible extension into the following season. Findings are expected in the form of a short set of concrete recommendations tied to specific screens, not a general report on grower attitudes, since the product team needs something it can act on before the next release window closes. Video clips from observed sessions, with consent, are shared alongside the write-up, since a short clip of a grower fumbling through a screen tends to land with the engineering team more effectively than a paragraph describing the same moment.

jobs.title: Design Systems Lead, Grower Products
jobs.summary: Loamwell's grower-facing products, spanning a mobile app, a web dashboard, and an internal agronomist tool, were built by different teams at different times and now show visible inconsistency in components, terminology, and even how basic actions like confirming a field boundary are handled. This lead will define a shared design system across all three surfaces, migrate the highest-traffic screens first, and set up lightweight governance so new features stay consistent going forward without slowing down a design team of only three people. Because engineering resourcing for design systems work is limited and competes directly with feature roadmap commitments, the role also involves making a credible case internally for continued investment once the initial migration is complete. A particular challenge unique to this context is designing components that work as well for a grower using the app one-handed in a field as for an agronomist reviewing detailed data on a desktop monitor. Experience introducing a design system into an organization that did not previously have one, ideally across genuinely different device contexts, is exactly the background this role needs. Adoption is tracked screen by screen rather than declared complete all at once, since forcing a big-bang migration across three products with different release schedules would likely stall everything. Component documentation includes real usage examples pulled from shipped screens rather than idealized mockups, since designers on other teams have said the abstract version alone rarely answers their actual question.

jobs.title: Junior Product Designer, Grower Mobile App
jobs.summary: This internship offers a design student real exposure to shipping features on Loamwell's grower mobile app under the mentorship of a senior designer, including a rare chance to see how a design decision holds up when tested outdoors on an actual farm rather than only in a conference room. Over the course of the internship, the intern will take on a scoped project such as redesigning a single field-logging screen, present work in progress during weekly design critiques, and incorporate feedback into higher-fidelity prototypes tested with a couple of local pilot growers if scheduling allows. Past interns have gone on to contribute directly to shipped features by the end of their term, including a redesigned crop-issue reporting flow that is still in use today. No professional design experience is required, though a portfolio demonstrating coursework or personal projects is expected as part of the application.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Learning Platform
jobs.summary: Every quiz attempt, video pause, and assignment submission on Chalkline's learning platform generates an event, and this analytics engineer will help turn that raw stream into the modeled tables that curriculum and product teams actually use to understand how students engage with a course. A lot of the existing dbt models were built quickly during an earlier growth push and have started to show their age, particularly around how partially completed assignments get counted, which has led to two teams reporting different completion rates for the same course. The role involves untangling that specific discrepancy, adding tests so similar issues get caught automatically going forward, and documenting metric definitions clearly enough that a curriculum designer without a data background can understand what a number actually represents. Because Chalkline serves both individual learners and school district accounts with very different usage patterns, some models need separate logic to avoid misleading comparisons between the two. Exposure to messy, real-world behavioral event data is more useful here than deep expertise in any particular data warehouse. New models go through a short peer review before merging, mainly to catch the kind of subtle counting mistake that caused the current completion-rate discrepancy in the first place.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Student Engagement
jobs.summary: This analyst supports the curriculum team by turning course-level engagement data into a monthly report used to flag lessons where students commonly stall out or drop off partway through. The role also involves fielding ad hoc data requests from curriculum designers, which vary widely in scope, from a quick lookup of how many students used a particular feature to a deeper look at whether a redesigned unit actually improved completion rates. Structured mentorship from a senior analyst is built into the first three months to help build fluency with Chalkline's internal data warehouse and the quirks of how learning events get logged. This is a good starting point for someone who wants to move toward a more analytical role within an education-focused product organization, and prior experience in EdTech specifically is not required.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer, Content Pipeline
jobs.summary: Chalkline's course content, videos, quizzes, reading passages, and interactive exercises, moves through a publishing pipeline that has to keep track of versioning, translations, and accessibility metadata across thousands of individual lessons, and this engineer will be responsible for keeping that pipeline fast and reliable as the content library keeps growing. Recent priorities have included reducing the time it takes for a content update to appear for students after an editor publishes a change, which had stretched to several hours during peak publishing periods before this quarter's optimization work began. The role works closely with both the platform engineering team and the curriculum team's own tooling, which increasingly depends on this pipeline being predictable rather than something they have to work around. A recurring source of complexity is that content exists in multiple languages and reading levels that all need to stay synchronized when an underlying lesson changes. Experience with content management or publishing systems at meaningful scale carries more weight here than experience with any specific programming language. The team tracks publish-to-live latency as a headline metric and reviews it monthly with the curriculum team, since a slow pipeline directly limits how quickly a lesson fix reaches students.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Course Authoring
jobs.summary: Brought in on an initial nine-month contract to cover parental leave, this product manager will own the roadmap for the internal authoring tool that Chalkline's curriculum designers use to build and update courses, at a moment when the team is pushing for several changes to how interactive exercises get created. The role involves translating curriculum designers' requirements, which are often expressed in pedagogical rather than technical terms, into specifications an engineering team can build against, and coordinating a phased rollout so existing course content is not disrupted mid-update for currently enrolled students. A specific near-term goal is reducing the number of steps it takes to add a new interactive exercise type, which currently requires filing an engineering ticket rather than something a curriculum designer can configure directly. Because the contract covers a defined leave period, a clean handover with thorough documentation at the end is expected from the outset. Familiarity with content authoring tools or curriculum design workflows is highly relevant experience for this role. Weekly check-ins with a rotating group of curriculum designers keep the roadmap grounded in what people actually struggle with day to day, rather than the handful of loudest requests that tend to dominate a shared feedback inbox. A short usability pass with two or three designers precedes any authoring workflow change, since a tool built for content experts still needs to be genuinely learnable under deadline pressure.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Assessments
jobs.summary: The assessment engine that generates and grades quizzes across Chalkline's courses is used by both individual learners studying independently and school districts that rely on it for gradebook reporting, and this manager will guide its roadmap as those two very different use cases continue to pull in somewhat different directions. Much of the work involves talking directly to teachers at partner districts who have built unexpectedly specific grading workflows around the tool, then working out which of their requests reflect genuine gaps versus edge cases not worth solving for the broader product. The manager also partners with the support team to reduce a recurring category of confusion around how partial credit gets calculated for multi-part questions, which generates a disproportionate share of support tickets relative to how often the feature is actually used. Prior experience with assessment, grading, or another rules-heavy educational product is a strong asset for this role, given how much of the complexity here is about correctly modeling grading logic rather than typical feature design. Proposed grading rule changes go through a review with a small panel of teachers before release, since a rule that looks correct in isolation can still produce results a teacher would consider unfair once applied across a real class of students with varied circumstances. The team also maintains a changelog of grading logic changes specifically, separate from the general release notes, because districts have asked for a clear audit trail when a parent disputes a grade.

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Learning Platform
jobs.summary: This role leads a group of four product managers covering different areas of Chalkline's core learning platform, with responsibility for keeping their roadmaps coherent as a whole rather than a set of disconnected initiatives that happen to share an engineering org. The group product manager runs quarterly planning across the group, resolves prioritization conflicts when two teams want the same engineering resources at the same time, and represents the product organization in leadership planning meetings where school-district sales commitments sometimes create pressure to reprioritize on short notice. A current focus is untangling technical dependencies between the assessment team and the content authoring team, which have historically planned in isolation despite sharing a substantial amount of underlying data. Experience managing other product managers, not just individual contributors, is required, along with comfort operating in an environment where a subset of customers are institutional buyers rather than the end users themselves. This group product manager also runs a monthly retrospective across the group specifically to catch dependency conflicts before they turn into a scheduling crisis two sprints later.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management
jobs.summary: As Chalkline's director of product management, this person owns strategy across the full platform and sits on the extended leadership team that sets company-wide priorities each quarter, including decisions about how much of the roadmap should serve individual learners versus the growing school-district segment. The role involves resolving cross-group prioritization conflicts that group product managers cannot settle on their own, representing product in board-level reporting, and building out a more structured product operations function as the team has grown past what informal processes can support. Because this posting is internal only, deep familiarity with Chalkline's product organization, its current roadmap, and the tension between consumer and institutional priorities is assumed rather than something to be learned. Strong written and verbal communication with executive stakeholders and, on occasion, directly with large district customers during contract renewal conversations, is essential to this role.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.summary: This role is designed as a structured entry point into product management, pairing a new associate with a senior product manager mentor for their first year at Chalkline. Responsibilities start small, such as writing up findings from teacher interviews and maintaining a backlog for a narrow slice of the assessment product, before growing to owning a small feature area under supervision as confidence and context build over the first several months. The associate will also rotate through a short stint on the support team to build genuine empathy for how teachers and students experience the product day to day, which tends to surface issues that never show up in a roadmap review. A demonstrated interest in education or product work, whether through prior internships, tutoring experience, or side projects, matters more than formal product management experience for this role.

jobs.title: Program Manager, District Rollouts
jobs.summary: Rolling out Chalkline to a new school district is a genuinely operational challenge involving data migration from a district's previous system, staff training sessions scheduled around the school calendar, and coordination across sales, support, and engineering teams that do not always naturally talk to each other. This program manager owns that rollout process end to end for every new district signed, tracking a checklist of dependencies that has grown organically over several years and is due for a proper overhaul this year. The role involves troubleshooting rollout-specific issues as they come up, whether that means a data import failing on unusual formatting from a legacy system or a training session needing to be rescheduled around exam week, and reporting rollout health to leadership in a way that flags risk early rather than after a district's launch date has already slipped. Strong organizational skills paired with genuine comfort working with school administrators, who are often juggling this alongside many other priorities, are essential to this role. A short post-launch check-in with each district, roughly a month after go-live, has become the main way the team catches quieter problems, such as a training gap, before they turn into a renewal risk.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Accessibility Compliance
jobs.summary: Several of Chalkline's district contracts include specific accessibility requirements tied to public procurement rules, and this staff product manager owns making sure the platform actually meets those obligations rather than treating accessibility as a checklist completed once and forgotten. The role involves auditing existing features against relevant accessibility standards, working with individual product teams to fix gaps without derailing their own roadmaps, and building a lightweight review process so new features get checked before launch instead of after a customer complaint or an audit finding. A recent project involved reworking how the assessment engine handles screen readers for visually impaired students taking a timed quiz, which required rethinking timing behavior rather than a simple markup fix. Because this role sits above any single product team, strong influence skills matter as much as accessibility expertise itself, since the staff product manager rarely has direct authority to force a fix into another team's sprint. Experience with accessibility compliance in a regulated or public-sector-adjacent context is directly relevant here. A quarterly audit against the district contract requirements keeps the team honest about where gaps remain, and the resulting list is prioritized jointly with whichever product team owns the affected feature. This role also runs a short accessibility training session for new engineers during onboarding, since most gaps in the platform trace back to a pattern nobody flagged early rather than to any single careless decision.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Learning Strategy
jobs.summary: This principal-level role has no direct reports but carries significant influence over Chalkline's overall product direction, particularly around whether the company should expand further into adaptive, personalized learning paths or continue investing primarily in its existing linear course model. The work involves synthesizing input from curriculum research, competitive analysis, and district customer feedback into a small number of well-argued strategic recommendations for leadership each quarter, rather than owning any single team's day-to-day roadmap. Because the role operates at a strategic altitude, execution is left to group product managers, though this person is expected to stay close enough to actual classroom usage data to keep recommendations grounded rather than purely theoretical. A recent contribution involved a proposal, ultimately adopted, to pilot adaptive difficulty in one subject area before committing to a platform-wide investment. A track record of shaping company-level product strategy, not just individual roadmaps, along with genuine interest in learning science, is expected for this role. Recommendations are grounded in a mix of internal usage data and outside learning-science research, and this person is expected to be explicit about which parts of a proposal rest on solid evidence versus a reasonable bet worth testing. Quarterly strategy memos circulate to the whole leadership team in advance of the planning meeting, so debate can focus on the substance of a recommendation rather than the framing being seen for the first time in the room.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Classroom Tools
jobs.summary: Hired for an initial six-month contract, this designer will lead the redesign of the teacher-facing classroom dashboard, which has not been substantially revisited since Chalkline's early days and now looks noticeably dated next to the rest of the product. The work includes auditing existing dashboard usage against what teachers say they actually need day to day, which often turns out to be a much shorter list than the current dashboard tries to serve, prototyping a simplified alternative, and running usability sessions with teachers at a handful of partner schools before anything ships broadly. Because dashboard changes affect how teachers plan their week, the rollout will be gradual and closely watched, with the designer expected to help interpret early feedback rather than handing that work off once designs are finalized. Experience designing for professional, task-focused users under real time pressure, such as teachers between classes, is directly relevant to this role.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Educator Feedback
jobs.summary: This part-time role, roughly three days a week, supports the design team with ongoing research into how teachers configure and troubleshoot Chalkline's classroom and grading tools throughout a typical school term. Work includes running regular usability sessions on features still in development, maintaining a repository of past research findings so teams stop rediscovering the same insights every time a new designer joins the classroom tools group, and occasionally analyzing feedback survey data collected from the educator advisory panel that meets each semester. The reduced schedule suits someone balancing other commitments, perhaps consulting work or a teaching background they still maintain, who wants meaningful ongoing involvement in product decisions without a full-time commitment. Prior in-house research experience in an education or teacher-facing product is preferred over agency-only research backgrounds, given how much of the value here comes from accumulated context about how classrooms actually operate.

jobs.title: Design Manager, Product Design
jobs.summary: Overseeing a team of five product designers spread across Chalkline's platform areas, this manager balances hands-on critique with enough distance to let each designer own their work rather than second-guessing every decision. Beyond regular one-on-ones, the role involves partnering with the design systems function to make sure new feature designs stay consistent across the classroom, assessment, and authoring surfaces, and negotiating design resourcing when two product teams both need support in the same sprint cycle. A recent challenge has been rebuilding trust with the assessment product team after a rushed design handoff caused avoidable rework late in a release, which prompted a broader look at how design and product timelines get coordinated earlier in a project. Prior experience managing designers, not just doing individual design work, is required, along with genuine interest in education products specifically rather than treating this as a generic design management role.

jobs.title: Content Designer, Course Experience
jobs.summary: Chalkline's in-product copy, from quiz instructions to progress-tracking notifications, has been written inconsistently by whichever engineer or curriculum designer happened to build a given feature, and this content designer exists to bring some order to that without slowing down shipping. The role involves auditing existing copy across the platform for tone and clarity issues, building a lightweight style guide the design and engineering teams can actually follow rather than a document that gets ignored after launch, and reviewing copy for upcoming releases before they ship to students and teachers. Because some copy, particularly around grading and assessment results, carries real emotional weight for students, precision and tone matter more in those areas than elsewhere in the product. A specific near-term project is rewriting the language used when a student fails an assessment, which current data suggests discourages some students from retrying rather than encouraging them. Experience writing for young or student audiences, rather than purely enterprise or marketing copy, is preferred for this role. Draft copy is tested informally with a handful of students where feasible, since phrasing that reads as clear and encouraging to an adult reviewer does not always land the same way with an eleven-year-old working through a difficult assignment. The style guide includes explicit guidance on tone for setbacks specifically, distinct from the more straightforward guidance covering navigation and confirmations elsewhere in the product.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Marketplace Matching
jobs.summary: Meridian Loop connects homeowners with independent electricians, plumbers, and other skilled tradespeople, and this data scientist supports the team responsible for matching a homeowner's job posting with the right set of available professionals nearby. Small ranking changes here tend to have outsized effects on both how quickly a job gets booked and how satisfied a tradesperson is with the leads they receive, which makes the tuning work more delicate than it might first appear. The role involves designing experiments to test changes to the matching algorithm, building models that predict which professionals are likely to respond quickly to a given job type, and presenting results in a way that non-technical stakeholders on the marketplace team can act on within a sprint rather than waiting for a full quarterly review. Because the marketplace has two distinct sides with different incentives, the scientist needs to be comfortable working on concurrent tests that sometimes pull in different directions for homeowners versus professionals. A background in marketplace or two-sided platform dynamics is a meaningful advantage for this role. Matching changes ship to a small percentage of traffic first, and the scientist is expected to define upfront what result would justify a full rollout rather than deciding after seeing which way the numbers happened to move.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Marketplace Metrics
jobs.summary: As the marketplace has grown, so has the number of ad hoc SQL queries analysts write directly against raw production tables, and this role exists to replace that pattern with well-modeled, tested dbt datasets that everyone can rely on. The analytics engineer will work through a backlog of high-traffic queries to identify which deserve to become proper models, build those models with appropriate tests, and document them clearly for the growing analyst team spread across marketplace, trust and safety, and finance. Because production data changes frequently as the marketplace evolves, particularly as new service categories get added beyond the original electrician and plumber focus, keeping models resilient to schema changes is an ongoing concern rather than a one-time cleanup project. Comfort working directly with messy, evolving production data is more valuable here than deep dbt expertise on day one, and hybrid work at the Toronto office is expected a few days a week for team planning.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Pricing Strategy
jobs.summary: Pricing on a two-sided marketplace is a genuinely hard problem, since changes that help professionals earn more can hurt homeowner conversion and vice versa, and this senior scientist will own the analytical work behind Meridian Loop's pricing recommendations to both sides of the platform. Recent work has involved building a model that suggests a competitive quote range to professionals bidding on a job, and evaluating, after the fact, whether professionals who followed the suggestion actually won more work without leaving money on the table compared to those who priced independently. The role reports into the pricing product manager and works closely with engineering to get models into production without the multi-week delays that have historically slowed down pricing experiments. Because pricing changes are visible and sometimes contentious with professionals who depend on the platform for their income, the scientist needs to be comfortable presenting results to skeptical stakeholders and explaining trade-offs clearly rather than simply reporting a headline number. Experience with pricing, auctions, or other two-sided marketplace dynamics is strongly preferred, and a hybrid schedule at the Toronto office supports close collaboration with the pricing product manager. The team reviews every shipped pricing change a month out to check whether it held up outside the initial experiment window, since marketplace dynamics can shift once professionals adjust their own behavior in response.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Booking Experience
jobs.summary: This product manager owns the core job-posting and booking flow that most homeowners interact with the moment they decide they need an electrician or plumber, which makes it one of the highest-traffic and most closely watched parts of the entire product. The role involves running regular interviews with homeowners who abandoned a booking partway through, reviewing session recordings to spot friction that surveys alone would not surface, and making prioritization calls that account for both the homeowner experience and the quality of information professionals receive about the job. A current initiative focuses on reducing the number of steps needed to post a job with enough detail that a professional can quote confidently without a follow-up call, which early data suggests is a major source of delay in getting jobs booked quickly. Experience with lead-generation or on-demand service marketplace products is a strong plus, and this role is based onsite at the Toronto headquarters to stay close to the engineering team shipping these changes weekly. Every change to the booking form is tested against a small holdout group first, since a field that seems like harmless extra detail to the team can quietly become the exact step where a homeowner gives up.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Provider Success
jobs.summary: Professional retention has become a board-level priority at Meridian Loop after churn among high-volume electricians and plumbers ticked up over the past two quarters, and this senior product manager will lead the response to that trend. The role involves deep-diving into why professionals leave the platform, whether that turns out to be lead quality, payout speed, or competition from other channels, prioritizing a roadmap that balances quick wins against more structural fixes, and working closely with a dedicated provider success team to pilot changes with a subset of accounts before wider rollout. Because this initiative has visibility at the executive level, clear and frequent communication about progress and setbacks, including when an experiment does not work, is expected rather than only reporting good news. A recent pilot testing faster payout timing for top-rated professionals showed encouraging early retention signals and is being considered for wider rollout. Prior experience with retention-focused product work, ideally in a marketplace with a supply side that has real alternatives elsewhere, is exactly the background this role calls for. Cohort-level retention curves are reviewed with the executive team monthly, and this manager is expected to walk in with a point of view on what is driving any shift, not just the number itself.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Marketplace Growth
jobs.summary: Supporting a growth team through a busy quarter under a four-month contract, this analyst will build and maintain dashboards tracking the professional onboarding funnel, from initial sign-up through a tradesperson completing their first job on the platform. Work includes flagging unusual drops in conversion for the product manager to investigate, pulling ad hoc data for planning meetings on short notice, and documenting how key funnel metrics are defined so future analysts do not have to reverse-engineer old queries the way this analyst will need to at the start of the engagement. The contract has a clearly defined end date tied to this specific initiative rather than being open-ended, which suits someone looking for a focused, well-scoped engagement. Comfort working somewhat independently with limited onboarding time is important given the short duration of the contract and the pace of the growth team.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Core Marketplace
jobs.summary: This lead role sits above three product managers working on different parts of the homeowner experience, from search and matching through booking and payment, with responsibility for making sure their individual roadmaps add up to a coherent overall strategy rather than three teams optimizing locally. The lead spends much of the week in cross-team planning conversations, resolving disagreements about shared engineering resources, and occasionally stepping in directly on a particularly gnarly problem, such as a recent redesign of the search results ranking that had stalled under competing opinions between two teams for several weeks. Success is measured partly through the individual product managers' output and partly through direct contributions on the hardest cross-cutting problems that no single team naturally owns. Experience leading other product managers without having formal authority over them, and comfort mediating between teams with genuinely different incentives, is valuable preparation for this role.

jobs.title: Director of Product Operations
jobs.summary: This director builds and runs the product operations function that keeps Meridian Loop's growing product organization aligned as headcount roughly doubled over the past year without a corresponding investment in shared process. The role involves designing a roadmap planning process that scales beyond the informal spreadsheet-based approach the company outgrew several quarters ago, standardizing how teams report progress to leadership, and building a small operations team to support these efforts going forward.
