Because this posting is internal, familiarity with Meridian Loop's current product organization and its specific growing pains, including the tension between homeowner-facing and provider-facing priorities, is assumed rather than something to learn from scratch. Strong facilitation skills are essential given the cross-functional nature of the role, which regularly involves getting product, engineering, and go-to-market leaders to agree on a shared quarterly plan.

jobs.title: VP of Product
jobs.summary: This executive reports to the CEO and owns product strategy across the entire marketplace, including decisions about expanding beyond electrical and plumbing work into adjacent home-service categories, a move that is becoming increasingly urgent as growth in the founding categories slows in mature markets. The role involves setting quarterly priorities across all product groups, representing product in board meetings where marketplace liquidity metrics get scrutinized closely, and building the next layer of product leadership as the organization continues to grow past what the current team of managers can fully cover. Because this posting is restricted to internal candidates, deep knowledge of Meridian Loop's marketplace dynamics, competitive position, and internal culture is required rather than something a new external hire could reasonably absorb quickly. Significant experience operating at an executive level in a marketplace business, ideally one with a skilled trades or field-services supply side, is expected for this role. This executive also chairs the quarterly review where liquidity, retention, and expansion bets are weighed against each other explicitly, rather than each being championed separately by whichever team owns it.

jobs.title: Product Management Intern
jobs.summary: This four-month internship gives a student real exposure to product management by pairing them with a mentor on the homeowner booking experience team. The intern will conduct a small number of homeowner interviews under supervision, help maintain the team's backlog, and take ownership of a narrowly scoped feature improvement, such as a small copy change to the job-posting form, from initial definition through launch and a short post-launch check on the results. Scheduling has some flexibility to accommodate coursework, with the expectation of roughly full-time hours during the core weeks of the internship period. Prior internship or coursework related to product management, human-computer interaction, or a similar field is helpful but not required for this position.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Trust and Safety
jobs.summary: Payments and identity verification underpin every job booked on Meridian Loop, which makes this a role where small mistakes carry outsized consequences and where new features tend to move more slowly than elsewhere in the product organization for good reason. The product manager will work closely with engineering and a small compliance team to ship new fraud protections and identity checks for professionals joining the platform, translating regulatory and risk requirements into specifications that engineers can actually build against without overcorrecting into friction that discourages legitimate professionals from signing up. A recent project involved rolling out a faster identity verification path for professionals with an established track record on other platforms, which required coordinating across engineering, a third-party verification vendor, and the legal team. Because trust and safety issues can escalate quickly if handled poorly, clear incident response processes are as much a part of this role as the roadmap itself. Experience with trust and safety, payments, or another highly regulated product area is important for this role. A monthly review with the compliance and support teams tracks fraud attempt patterns and false-positive rates side by side, since tightening one almost always loosens the other.

jobs.title: Senior UX Researcher, Provider Insights
jobs.summary: Supporting a research-heavy quarter for the provider success team, this freelance engagement addresses a deeper question about why certain segments of tradespeople are churning before committing engineering resources to a fix based on assumptions alone. The researcher will design and conduct a mixed-methods study combining phone and video interviews with churned professionals and survey data from the broader active provider base, then present findings that the product team can act on directly rather than a purely descriptive report. Because the findings will inform a roadmap presented to executives, clear synthesis and a well-supported narrative matter as much as the underlying research rigor itself. Prior experience researching churn or retention specifically, ideally with a supply-side or gig-economy population who have real alternatives to the platform, is a meaningful plus for this engagement. The engagement runs roughly ten weeks with scheduling flexibility to work around tradespeople's unpredictable job schedules.

jobs.title: Product Designer, Booking Flow
jobs.summary: This eight-month contract ties a designer to a booking-flow redesign initiative, working alongside a product manager and two engineers to simplify a job-posting flow that has accumulated extra steps over several years of incremental changes made by different teams at different times. The work includes auditing the current flow against drop-off data to find where homeowners actually give up, prototyping a streamlined alternative that still captures enough detail for professionals to quote confidently, and running usability tests with real homeowners before the new flow rolls out broadly across the platform. Because booking-flow changes directly affect how many jobs get posted successfully, the rollout will be gradual and closely monitored, with the designer expected to help interpret results at each stage rather than moving on once the design is handed off. Experience redesigning a checkout, booking, or similarly high-stakes conversion flow is directly relevant to this role.

jobs.title: Principal UX Researcher, Marketplace Trust
jobs.summary: Serving as Meridian Loop's most senior researcher, this person sets the overall research agenda across both the homeowner and provider sides of the marketplace, deciding where deeper investigation is likely to change roadmap decisions versus where existing evidence is already sufficient to move forward confidently. A central focus for this role is trust, both a homeowner's willingness to let an unfamiliar professional into their home and a professional's confidence that a homeowner will pay fairly and on time, which shows up differently across nearly every part of the product. The role involves mentoring three other researchers, occasionally conducting research directly on the highest-stakes questions such as how identity verification badges affect booking conversion, and pushing back when a product team wants to skip research to move faster on a decision that seems genuinely uncertain. A recent contribution was building a lightweight framework the whole team now uses to decide how much research a given decision actually warrants before committing time to a full study. Extensive experience setting research strategy, not just conducting individual studies, matters more here than any single methodology specialty. The role sits on the product leadership team's monthly planning review, not to approve every decision but to make sure trust-related risks get surfaced before a roadmap commitment is made rather than after a launch goes sideways.

jobs.title: Junior Product Designer, Provider Tools
jobs.summary: This junior role supports the provider tools design team with smaller design tasks while building toward more independent ownership over time as skills and product context develop. Early work includes producing design variations for A/B tests on the professional dashboard, maintaining consistency between existing components during smaller feature updates, and shadowing senior designers during interviews with professionals to build direct exposure to how tradespeople actually use the platform between jobs. The flexible arrangement allows a mix of remote and in-office work depending on what suits both the designer and the team's collaboration needs in a given week, particularly around joint critique sessions. A portfolio demonstrating strong design fundamentals matters more than years of professional experience for this entry-level role.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Clinical Operations
jobs.summary: Solstice builds scheduling and care-coordination software used by outpatient clinics across several European countries, and this contract role supports the clinical operations team by turning appointment and no-show data into reports clinic managers can actually act on. The analyst will build recurring dashboards tracking appointment utilization and no-show rates across partner clinics, investigate specific spikes flagged by clinic managers, such as a sudden rise in cancellations at one location, and help maintain documentation of how key operational metrics are defined given that clinics sometimes use slightly different scheduling conventions. Because the underlying data touches patient scheduling, all work happens within Solstice's existing data governance and access controls rather than requiring the analyst to build new handling processes. The initial contract runs six months with the possibility of extension depending on how the clinical operations reporting program develops. Comfort working with healthcare operational data, even without a strictly clinical background, is a meaningful advantage for this role. Reports are reviewed with clinic managers directly rather than simply emailed out, since a number in isolation, such as a rising no-show rate, tends to prompt more useful discussion when someone is available to answer the immediate follow-up questions it raises. Access to any data broken down below the clinic level requires an additional governance check, which occasionally slows down an analysis but keeps the work clearly within Solstice's data handling commitments to its clinic partners.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Patient Data Platform
jobs.summary: Working roughly twenty hours a week, this analytics engineer maintains the modeled datasets that power internal reporting on platform usage across the clinics Solstice serves, work that sits carefully outside of directly identifiable patient health information given the regulatory sensitivity involved. The analytics engineer will build and maintain a small number of dbt models feeding internal dashboards, adjust models as the underlying scheduling system's data structure changes with each release, and respond to occasional requests from the clinical operations and product teams for custom cuts of usage data. Because healthcare data handling carries real compliance weight under European data protection rules, every model this person builds goes through a review step with the data governance lead before being used for a new reporting purpose. The reduced hours suit someone balancing other work who wants a stable, ongoing part-time role with genuine subject-matter depth rather than shallow generalist analytics work.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Care Coordination Tools
jobs.summary: Clinic staff use Solstice's care coordination tool to track referrals between a patient's primary doctor and specialists, a process that used to happen mostly over fax and phone calls before clinics adopted the platform, and this product manager owns its ongoing development as adoption grows across new partner clinics. The role involves gathering feedback directly from care coordinators, whose daily workflow depends heavily on this tool and who have strong, well-informed opinions about how referral status should be tracked, and translating that feedback into a roadmap for a small engineering team supporting the product. Because a missed or delayed referral can have real consequences for a patient's care, the bar for shipping changes carefully, with clinic pilot testing before wider rollout, is higher here than for a typical internal tool. A recent project involved adding automatic reminders for referrals that had gone quiet for more than a week without a status update. Experience with healthcare workflow or care coordination software specifically is relevant, though clinical background is not required for the role itself.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Clinician Platform
jobs.summary: This role owns the clinician-facing side of Solstice's platform, where doctors and nurses review patient histories, document visits, and manage their daily schedule, an interface that clinicians interact with dozens of times during a single shift. As Solstice has taken on larger multi-site clinic groups, the platform's original design has started to show limitations around handling clinicians who split time across multiple locations, which this product manager will address over the coming quarters. The work involves interviewing clinicians directly about their workflow, which is genuinely difficult to schedule given how little spare time doctors and nurses have during a working day, prioritizing improvements against a mid-size engineering team's capacity, and balancing requests from larger clinic groups against the needs of smaller independent practices using the same platform. A recent initiative reduced the number of clicks needed to document a routine follow-up visit, which clinicians had flagged repeatedly as a source of frustration. Experience with clinical workflow software or another regulated, high-stakes professional tool is valuable preparation for this role. Every proposed change to the clinician interface is reviewed jointly with the clinical safety team before it reaches engineering, a step that has occasionally slowed a release but has also caught ambiguous wording before it reached a doctor mid-shift.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Clinical Rollouts
jobs.summary: Bringing a new clinic onto Solstice's platform involves migrating existing patient scheduling data, training clinical and administrative staff around already-packed shift schedules, and coordinating closely with a clinic's IT contact who is often managing several other vendor relationships at the same time. This program manager owns that rollout process for every new mid-size clinic group signed, tracking dependencies that have grown more complex as Solstice has moved upmarket into larger multi-location practices with more demanding requirements. The role involves troubleshooting rollout-specific issues, whether that means a legacy scheduling export arriving in an unexpected format or a training session needing to be rescheduled around a clinic's patient volume, and reporting rollout health to leadership in a way that surfaces risk early. Because delays in a clinical rollout can mean staff reverting to old paper-based workarounds out of necessity, keeping momentum during a rollout matters more here than in a typical software onboarding. Strong organizational skills combined with genuine patience for healthcare operational realities matter more here than prior experience with any specific rollout methodology. A short retrospective follows every rollout, and the resulting notes feed directly into the checklist used for the next clinic group, so the process gets a little better with each cohort.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Patient App
jobs.summary: For this freelance engagement, the designer will lead the visual and interaction redesign of the patient-facing app that lets people book appointments, message their care team, and view visit summaries, working alongside a research team that has already completed a round of discovery interviews with patients across several age groups. The engagement covers concept exploration through high-fidelity prototypes ready for engineering handoff, with particular attention to older patients and others who may have limited familiarity with mobile apps, a real constraint given the patient population Solstice's partner clinics serve. Because the work touches a patient-facing healthcare product, all designs go through an accessibility and clarity review before testing, given how much confusion or anxiety a poorly designed health interface can create for someone managing a medical concern. Comfort presenting design rationale directly to both the internal product team and, on occasion, a clinic's patient advisory group is expected, since a design choice that seems obviously right to a design team can still land badly with the patients who actually rely on the app under stress. The engagement is anticipated to run three to four months with potential for a follow-on phase covering the messaging feature. Each major screen goes through a short readability and plain-language pass before usability testing, on the theory that a confusing layout and confusing wording tend to compound each other for a patient already under stress.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Clinician Workflows
jobs.summary: As a researcher on the clinician platform team, this person will run studies into how doctors and nurses actually use Solstice's documentation and scheduling tools during a real shift, which often looks quite different from how the workflow appears in a design mockup reviewed outside of clinical hours. A given study might involve shadowing clinicians for a morning at a partner clinic, running usability tests on an upcoming documentation feature with nurses during a scheduled training slot, and synthesizing findings into recommendations the product team can weigh against engineering effort. Because clinicians have very little spare time and cannot be pulled away from patient care casually, scheduling research sessions requires real coordination with clinic administrators well in advance rather than the more flexible recruiting typical of consumer research. The researcher works closely with the accessibility specialist on the team to make sure findings account for clinicians working under time pressure or with visual or motor constraints of their own. Prior experience researching professional or clinical software, rather than purely consumer products, counts for more here than familiarity with any particular research tool. Findings get shared in a short written readout circulated before the team meeting, so the discussion can focus on what to do about a finding rather than re-explaining what was found.

jobs.title: Junior UX Researcher, Patient Experience
jobs.summary: Supporting senior researchers on the patient experience team, this entry-level hire will help study how patients experience booking appointments, receiving reminders, and communicating with their care team through Solstice's patient app and portal. Early responsibilities include note-taking and logistics coordination during patient interviews, which requires real sensitivity given that participants are often discussing health concerns alongside their experience of the software itself, gradually moving into moderating simpler sessions independently as comfort and skill develop over the first several months. The team's small size means junior researchers get involved in patient-facing work much sooner than they might at a larger healthcare organization, though always under close supervision given the sensitivity of the subject matter. A relevant degree or a portfolio from coursework and personal projects is expected, and any prior experience or coursework touching healthcare, even informally, is a genuine plus for this entry-level role. A short debrief follows every session with the supervising researcher, partly to review technique and partly to check in on how the intern is holding up after a conversation that touched on a difficult health situation.

jobs.title: Interaction Designer, Care Navigation
jobs.summary: Care navigation, the sequence of screens that guide a patient from an initial symptom description through booking the right kind of appointment, is one of the more interaction-heavy parts of Solstice's patient app, and this lead designer owns how that flow behaves in detail. The role involves refining transitions, error states, and the specific wording and sequencing of questions the app asks a patient before recommending an appointment type, work that sits somewhere between visual design and content strategy given how much the flow depends on getting the question sequence right. A recent redesign reduced the number of patients who abandoned the flow after being asked an unexpectedly clinical question they did not know how to answer, replacing it with a simpler, plain-language alternative developed with input from the clinical safety team. Because a poorly designed navigation flow could plausibly direct a patient toward the wrong type of care, every significant change goes through review with both the design and clinical safety teams before shipping. Strong interaction design fundamentals paired with genuine comfort collaborating closely with clinical stakeholders, not just other designers, round out the profile for this role. Changes to the flow ship to a small pilot group of clinics first, with abandonment and question-skip rates tracked closely before anything reaches the full patient base.

jobs.title: Design Systems Lead, Clinical Interfaces
jobs.summary: Solstice's clinician-facing screens were built by different teams at different times and now show visible inconsistency in how similar actions, such as confirming a medication change or closing out a visit note, are presented across the platform, which adds unnecessary cognitive load for clinicians already working under time pressure. This lead will define a shared design system for clinical interfaces specifically, distinct from the more consumer-oriented patient app, migrate the highest-traffic clinician screens first, and set up governance so new clinical features stay consistent without slowing down a design team that is still relatively small. Because inconsistency in a clinical interface carries real safety implications, not just aesthetic ones, this system will include explicit guidance on how critical actions like prescribing or referral changes should be visually distinguished from routine ones. The role involves close collaboration with the clinical safety team to validate that new patterns do not introduce ambiguity in high-stakes moments. Experience building a design system with genuine safety or compliance constraints, not purely a visual consistency exercise, is what makes this role different from a typical design-systems position. A small clinical advisory panel reviews the highest-risk pattern proposals before they are added to the library, which slows things down slightly but has already caught two ambiguous icon choices before they shipped.

jobs.title: Accessibility Specialist, Health Products
jobs.summary: Given the patient population Solstice's partner clinics serve, which skews older and includes people managing chronic conditions that can affect vision, motor control, or cognitive load, accessibility is treated as a core product requirement rather than a compliance checkbox handled at the end of a project. This principal-level specialist audits both the patient app and clinician tools against accessibility standards, works directly with product and design teams to fix gaps without derailing their own timelines, and builds internal training so accessibility considerations get raised during initial design rather than caught late in a review. A recent project involved reworking how the patient app communicates appointment confirmations for users relying on screen readers, since the original implementation announced information in an order that made little sense out of visual context. Because this role has real influence over ship decisions on accessibility grounds but no formal authority over any single product team, strong persuasion skills matter as much as technical accessibility knowledge itself. Deep expertise in WCAG standards combined with genuine empathy for patients navigating a health concern while also fighting an inaccessible interface rounds out what the team looks for. Success is tracked through a shrinking backlog of open accessibility issues and, increasingly, through direct feedback solicited from patients who use assistive technology.

jobs.title: Design Manager, Patient Experience
jobs.summary: This manager oversees a team of five designers working across the patient app, clinician tools, and the shared design system, balancing hands-on critique with enough autonomy for each designer to genuinely own their area of the product. Beyond regular one-on-ones, the role involves negotiating with product leadership about design staffing when the patient app and clinician platform teams both need support during the same sprint, and stepping in personally when a designer needs additional guidance on a decision with real clinical safety implications. A recurring challenge specific to healthcare products is helping designers balance genuine empathy for patients in vulnerable moments against the practical need to ship features on a predictable schedule, which can pull in different directions when a design keeps getting refined in search of perfection. Prior experience managing designers on a regulated or safety-conscious product, not necessarily healthcare specifically, is preferred given how much this role involves weighing design quality against real-world risk. This manager also reviews staffing across the two teams each sprint, since clinician-platform work tends to carry harder deadlines that can otherwise quietly starve the patient app of design attention.

jobs.title: Director of Design
jobs.summary: This director sets design strategy and quality standards across all of Solstice's patient and clinician-facing products, working directly with the executive team on decisions about which new clinic segments or care models to prioritize from a design and research standpoint, given the genuinely different needs of a small independent practice versus a large multi-site clinic group. The role involves reviewing the company's highest-stakes design initiatives at key milestones, mentoring the lead and principal-level designers across the organization, and representing design directly in conversations with prospective large clinic customers who increasingly ask detailed questions about accessibility and clinical safety during procurement. Because this posting is limited to internal candidates, deep familiarity with Solstice's existing design organization, its clinical safety review process, and current customer relationships is assumed rather than something to be learned over the first several months. Significant experience operating at a director level within a healthcare or another safety-critical product organization, rather than a purely consumer-facing one, matters more here than breadth across unrelated industries. This person also chairs the quarterly review where the clinical safety, legal, and design teams jointly decide which open design risks are acceptable to ship with and which need to be resolved first.

jobs.title: UX Research Intern
jobs.summary: This five-month internship gives a student direct exposure to healthcare research work, which involves a level of ethical and practical care around participant recruitment and consent that most internship experiences do not touch. The intern will support ongoing studies by helping with participant scheduling and note-taking during clinician and patient interviews, always alongside a supervising researcher, and gradually take on small independent tasks such as analyzing patient feedback survey responses or drafting portions of a research readout under close guidance. Scheduling has some flexibility to accommodate coursework, with an expectation of consistent weekly hours during the core internship period rather than a fixed daily schedule. Coursework in psychology, human factors, design, or a related field is helpful but not required, and genuine interest in healthcare specifically will be weighed favorably given the sensitivity of the subject matter involved.

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, Clinical Dashboards
jobs.summary: Clinical dashboards, the screens where a clinician or clinic administrator reviews patient panels, upcoming appointments, and outstanding referrals at a glance, tend to accumulate density over time as every team wants to add just one more useful data point, and this staff designer exists to keep that tendency in check across the platform. The role involves providing senior design judgment on dashboard work across two or three concurrent initiatives at once, stepping in when a dashboard redesign has stalled because different clinical stakeholders want conflicting information prioritized, and helping less experienced designers push back constructively on scope creep from well-meaning clinical advisors. A recent contribution involved redesigning the multi-site clinic administrator dashboard after feedback that it had become difficult to quickly spot which locations needed attention on a given day, a problem that had grown gradually rather than through any single bad decision. Broad experience designing for information-dense, professional-use interfaces, ideally in a regulated context, is more valuable here than deep specialization in consumer visual design. Flexible scheduling reflects the cross-team, project-based nature of the staff design role at Solstice. Clinic administrators are looped into major dashboard changes before launch, since even a well-intentioned redesign can disrupt a routine that staff have built their whole morning around.

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Smart Meter Pipelines
jobs.summary: Fenwick's platform ingests interval readings from smart meters across several regional utilities, and this engineer will work on the pipelines that turn that raw meter data into the usage records billing, forecasting, and outage-detection systems all depend on downstream. The role involves building new ingestion pipelines as utilities onboard additional meter types, maintaining existing pipelines as data volumes grow with each new utility contract, and responding to on-call alerts when a pipeline breaks during business hours, since a stalled pipeline quickly backs up billing calculations for an entire utility's customer base. Because different utilities use different meter vendors with subtly different data formats and quality quirks, part of the job involves negotiating data quality expectations with utility partners rather than simply accepting whatever arrives. Experience working across data from multiple, loosely coordinated external partners is a good fit for this role, more so than experience with any single specific data platform. A short data quality scorecard for each utility feed is reviewed monthly, which has proven more effective at surfacing slow-building problems than waiting for a customer to notice a discrepancy first.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Load Forecasting
jobs.summary: Utilities rely on Fenwick's load forecasts to decide how much power to procure ahead of time, and getting those forecasts wrong in either direction carries real financial and reliability consequences, which makes this senior scientist's work directly consequential for the utility partners who depend on it. Recent work has included evaluating a controversial change to how the model handles extreme weather events after last year's forecasts underperformed during an unusually severe heat wave, and building a framework the broader team now uses to think through weather-driven demand spikes more systematically than the previous ad hoc approach allowed. The role also involves mentoring two mid-level data scientists newer to forecasting who are still building intuition for how to validate a forecasting model beyond a standard holdout test. Comfort defending analytical conclusions to skeptical utility engineers, who often have decades of institutional knowledge about their own grid, is as important as the underlying statistical rigor itself. Forecast error is reviewed publicly with each utility partner after any significant miss, since being upfront about what went wrong has done more for the relationship than any accuracy number quoted in isolation.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Grid Anomaly Detection
jobs.summary: This five-month contract brings an engineer onto the team to productionize an anomaly-detection model that has performed well in offline evaluation but has not yet been deployed to flag likely equipment faults on the grid due to competing engineering priorities. The work includes building the serving infrastructure needed to run the model against a continuous stream of grid sensor data, setting up basic monitoring so the operations team is alerted quickly when the model flags something worth investigating, and working with the data science team that built the original model to validate that production behavior matches offline expectations under real, noisier conditions. This is a well-scoped piece of work with a defined end state rather than ongoing model development, which suits someone who wants meaningful applied engineering work without a long-term commitment. Prior experience taking models from research to production specifically, rather than pure research experience, is preferred, and familiarity with streaming sensor data is a genuine plus given the continuous nature of grid monitoring. The engineer will also write a short handover document at the end of the contract covering deployment decisions and known limitations, since the team that inherits ongoing maintenance will not have the context built up during the original research phase. Alert thresholds are tuned conservatively at launch and adjusted based on the first few weeks of live flags, since a model that cries wolf too often will simply get ignored by the operations team it is meant to help.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Outage Reporting
jobs.summary: Utility partners expect timely, accurate outage reports during severe weather events, and this analytics engineer builds and maintains the dbt models that power those reports from raw grid sensor and customer-call data. The role involves working directly with the operations analysts and utility account managers who consume these models to understand what they actually need during a live outage event, rather than building in isolation and hoping the output fits real incident-response needs, and gradually improving test coverage on models that were built quickly during earlier storm seasons under real time pressure. Because outage patterns and reporting requirements differ somewhat by utility and by region, underlying data structures change more often than in a more stable, single-customer data model. Comfort with ambiguity and a willingness to prioritize reliability during actual severe weather events over elegant long-term architecture is more valuable here than deep specialization in a single well-documented pipeline.

jobs.title: Lead Data Engineer, Grid Infrastructure
jobs.summary: Coordinating data engineering work across three utility-facing product lines that have historically built their own ingestion and processing pipelines somewhat independently, this lead role addresses duplicated effort and inconsistent data quality practices between teams that ultimately serve overlapping utility customers. The lead will design a shared data infrastructure strategy, work with each product line's engineers to migrate onto common tooling without disrupting service to existing utility partners mid-contract, and set technical standards that balance consistency against each team's genuinely different latency and reliability requirements. Because this involves changing how established teams work, strong influence and negotiation skills matter alongside technical depth, particularly when a team resists giving up a bespoke pipeline they built and understand well. A recent milestone was migrating the outage-reporting and load-forecasting teams onto a shared streaming layer, cutting duplicated infrastructure cost meaningfully. Experience consolidating fragmented data infrastructure across previously independent teams, ideally in a business serving multiple external partners with their own contractual requirements, will translate directly. The role reports into the head of platform engineering and works closely with each product line's own tech lead throughout the migration rather than dictating changes from a distance.

jobs.title: Data Science Manager, Energy Analytics
jobs.summary: Overseeing five data scientists embedded across load forecasting, anomaly detection, and outage prediction, this manager balances hands-on technical guidance with the administrative work of hiring, performance reviews, and resource planning across genuinely different problem domains that each require different modeling approaches. The role involves resolving disagreements when two product lines both want the same data scientist's time during storm season, reviewing major analyses for methodological soundness before they inform a utility-facing commitment, and building a more structured onboarding process after several recent hires struggled to get up to speed quickly given the domain-specific nature of grid data. Direct experience conducting applied data science work, not just managing it, is expected given how technical the team's work is and how often utility partners ask pointed technical questions during account reviews. A track record of growing and retaining data science talent in a specialized technical domain is valuable for this role. This manager also holds a brief joint review with the affected utility account manager after any model change that touches a customer-visible number, since a shift in methodology that seems minor internally can otherwise show up as an unexplained jump on a partner's own dashboard.

jobs.title: Senior Forecasting Scientist, Renewable Generation
jobs.summary: As utilities in Fenwick's portfolio add more solar and wind capacity, predicting how much power those sources will actually generate on a given day has become as important to grid planning as predicting demand itself, and this scientist owns the modeling work behind those renewable generation forecasts. Current priorities include improving forecast accuracy for distributed rooftop solar, which is much harder to observe directly than a single large wind farm and has to be estimated indirectly from weather data and a sample of monitored installations. The role also involves setting modeling conventions that newer scientists on the team are expected to follow as the renewable forecasting effort grows from a single-person project into a small dedicated team. A recent improvement reduced forecast error for a partner utility's solar portfolio meaningfully during a stretch of unusually variable spring weather, which the utility specifically flagged as valuable during a contract renewal conversation. Experience owning forecasting models that many downstream grid-planning decisions depend on directly is relevant preparation for this role.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Utility Portal
jobs.summary: Owning the web portal that utility account managers use to monitor grid health, review outage reports, and configure alerting thresholds for their own service territory, this product manager serves professional utility staff rather than end consumers as the primary users of the product. The role involves gathering requirements from utility partners about what portal capabilities would help their own operations teams, prioritizing platform investments against those competing requests from different utility accounts, and communicating portal changes clearly enough that utility staff are not caught off guard during a live grid event. A recent project involved building configurable alert thresholds after several utilities requested different sensitivity settings than the one-size-fits-all default the portal originally shipped with. Experience with B2B or partner-facing product management, ideally in an infrastructure or operationally critical context, is a strong plus for this role.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Field Operations Tools
jobs.summary: Field technicians who maintain grid equipment use a separate mobile tool from Fenwick to log inspections, report faults, and close out repair tickets, often while standing at a substation with limited connectivity, and this senior product manager will bring more intentional prioritization to a tool that has grown somewhat haphazardly as different utility partners requested different features over time. The role involves surveying field technicians about their biggest workflow pain points, which vary from confusing offline-sync behavior to inspection checklists that do not match how a particular utility actually structures its maintenance program, and building a roadmap that addresses the highest-impact problems first rather than whichever utility complains loudest in a given quarter. Because field tools rarely get the same visible investment as customer-facing dashboards, making a credible case for engineering resources is a recurring part of the job. Experience with field-service or frontline-worker software, where connectivity and physical working conditions genuinely shape the design, is valuable for this role. Proposed changes are tested with a handful of technicians in the field before wider rollout, since a workflow that seems reasonable on a desk review can fall apart the moment gloves or bright sunlight enter the picture. This product manager also tracks a rolling list of offline-sync failures reported from the field, which has become one of the more reliable early signals that a release needs attention.

jobs.title: Product Analyst, Grid Operations
jobs.summary: Supporting the field operations product team under a four-month contract, this analyst handles dashboard maintenance and ad hoc reporting during a period of increased project volume tied to a new utility partner's onboarding. Work includes updating dashboards as underlying inspection data sources change with each field-tool release, responding to data requests from utility account managers, and documenting metric definitions that had previously existed only in individual team members' heads rather than anywhere written down. The contract has a defined scope tied to this specific busy period rather than being open-ended, which suits someone looking for a well-bounded engagement. Comfort ramping up quickly with limited onboarding time is important given the short duration of the contract and the operational nature of the data involved.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Grid Infrastructure
jobs.summary: This technical product manager works closely with the infrastructure engineering team to prioritize investments in reliability, ingestion capacity, and internal developer tooling that rarely have the same visible impact as a utility-facing feature but matter enormously to overall platform health during high-demand events like storm season. The role involves translating infrastructure engineers' technical concerns into business cases that leadership can weigh against other priorities, and occasionally advocating for infrastructure work over more visible feature requests from utility accounts. A recent success involved securing dedicated engineering time to address an ingestion bottleneck that had been flagged internally for over a year without action until it nearly caused a reporting delay during a major storm. A strong technical background sufficient to engage credibly with infrastructure engineers on architecture trade-offs is required for this role, based out of the Dublin office serving Fenwick's growing European utility customer base. This person also maintains a short quarterly reliability scorecard shared with utility partners, which has become a useful counterweight to the more visible feature roadmap when justifying infrastructure spend internally.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.summary: This director owns product strategy across Fenwick's utility portal and field operations tooling, working with a peer who owns the core grid-analytics product lines to make sure these more operational products serve the company's overall direction rather than becoming disconnected side efforts. The role involves quarterly planning across several product managers, resolving disputes over shared engineering resources between the operational tooling and core analytics teams, and representing operational-tooling priorities in company-wide leadership planning where utility-facing analytics tends to get more attention by default. Because this posting is internal, deep familiarity with Fenwick's existing product organization and the specific tension between visible analytics features and less visible operational tooling is assumed rather than something to learn quickly. Experience balancing infrastructure and tooling investment against feature delivery pressure at a senior level, ideally in a business serving utility or other critical-infrastructure customers, is essential for this role. This director also reviews staffing requests across both areas each quarter, which usually means making an explicit trade-off rather than simply approving whichever team asked first.

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Internal Tools
jobs.summary: Overseeing three product managers responsible for different parts of Fenwick's internal tooling suite, the software the company's own operations and support staff use rather than utility customers directly, this group product manager is accountable for the group's overall output rather than any single product area. The group product manager runs regular planning across the group, mediates when two product managers want overlapping engineering resources during the same sprint, and represents the group's priorities when platform leadership makes trade-off decisions that affect internal tooling investment. A current focus has been improving how the group measures the impact of internal tools, which had previously been tracked inconsistently, or in some cases not tracked at all beyond anecdotal feedback from support staff. Experience managing other product managers, along with genuine comfort making the case for internal-facing investment that does not show up directly in customer-facing metrics, is required for this role.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer, Operations Dashboard
jobs.summary: This freelance assignment brings a designer onto the field operations team for a focused redesign of the internal operations dashboard, which support staff and grid operators have long complained is slow to load and cluttered with information most of them rarely use during a shift. The engagement covers research into current pain points through short interviews with dashboard users, prototyping a streamlined alternative organized around the handful of metrics operators actually check hour to hour, and preparing detailed specifications for the engineering team to implement after the freelance engagement concludes. Because the user base is internal Fenwick staff rather than external customers, feedback cycles can move faster than typical utility-facing work, which suits a designer who prefers rapid iteration over long approval chains involving external stakeholders. The engagement is expected to run approximately ten weeks with usage-based follow-up review afterward.

jobs.title: UX Researcher, Field Technician Tools
jobs.summary: This researcher supports the field operations product team by studying how technicians actually use the mobile inspection tool while standing at a substation or climbing equipment, conditions that are difficult to fully replicate in a typical usability lab session. Recent work has included accompanying technicians on real inspection routes to observe how gloves, bright outdoor light, and spotty connectivity affect their interaction with the app, and running follow-up interviews about specific moments of friction that came up during those observed sessions. Because the two main audiences for Fenwick's products, utility account managers and frontline field technicians, have very different expectations and vocabulary, adapting research approach and communication style to the audience is a constant part of the job rather than a one-time adjustment. Flexible work arrangements accommodate the research team's need to occasionally travel to field sites and align schedules with technicians across different regions and shift patterns. Findings are shared back with technicians directly wherever possible, since crediting the people who raised an issue tends to make the next round of field research noticeably easier to schedule.

jobs.title: Checkout QA Automation Engineer
jobs.summary: The Checkout Platform group at Vantail Systems owns the payment flows merchants embed directly into their storefronts, and this role keeps those flows dependable across dozens of card networks, wallets, and regional payment methods. You will build and extend Playwright suites that run against every checkout release, working in TypeScript alongside the engineers shipping the flow rather than behind a separate QA wall. Day to day work includes designing test scenarios for new payment methods before they reach production, maintaining the CI pipeline that gates merges into the checkout service, and chasing flaky tests to a real root cause instead of retrying them away. You will also review API contracts with backend engineers so coverage reflects actual merchant integration patterns rather than internal assumptions. The team ships on a weekly release train, and this role signs off on release readiness alongside the engineering lead. Familiarity with payment gateway quirks such as 3D Secure or wallet tokenization is a plus though not required on day one. You will also participate in the checkout team's incident retrospectives, adding new test coverage directly derived from any production issue that slipped through existing testing. The role is fully remote within Europe, with core hours overlapping Central European time, and success is tracked through defect escape rate rather than raw test count.

jobs.title: Senior Payments SDET
jobs.summary: Payment failures that only appear under load or across specific bank routing paths are the hardest bugs to catch before they hit merchants, and that is the core problem this SDET role exists to solve. Reporting into the Payments Platform engineering group, you will design automated test frameworks in Java that simulate high-volume transaction bursts, partial gateway outages, and retry storms, then wire the results into the release pipeline so regressions are caught before rollout rather than after a merchant complaint. You will partner closely with the platform's SRE team to reproduce production incidents as repeatable automated tests, closing the loop between what breaks in the wild and what the suite actually exercises. Expect to own PCI-relevant regression coverage for card tokenization and to mentor two mid-level engineers building out the newer service-level test harness. Strong Java skills, comfort reading distributed tracing, and prior exposure to payment or banking systems will make the ramp-up faster, though the team is willing to teach domain specifics to a strong test engineer. You will also present quarterly test coverage findings to the payments engineering leadership, translating technical gaps into a prioritized list they can weigh against other roadmap commitments. This is a remote role open to candidates across Europe, and the team meets twice weekly for planning and incident review.

jobs.title: Principal Quality Engineer
jobs.summary: Vantail Systems processes checkout and payment traffic for thousands of independent retailers, and a defect that slips into that path can mean lost revenue for a merchant within minutes, which is why the quality organization reports its findings directly to engineering leadership rather than sitting downstream of it. As Principal Quality Engineer, you will set the testing strategy across all four product groups, checkout, payments, fraud, and the merchant dashboard, deciding where automation investment pays off fastest and where manual exploratory testing still catches what tooling cannot. You will not write day to day test scripts yourself; instead you will design the quality architecture, choose the frameworks the teams standardize on, and build the metrics dashboard that surfaces defect trends to the VP of Engineering each month. A major piece of the first six months will be consolidating three separate automation stacks that grew independently across teams into one shared library, without slowing any team's release cadence during the migration. You will also run a quarterly quality review with each product group's engineering lead, using data rather than anecdote to prioritize the next investment. This role expects deep experience leading quality organizations through a scaling period, comfort influencing without direct authority over the engineers you are asking to change their workflow, and enough hands-on background to credibly review a test architecture proposal line by line. The role is based in Berlin on a hybrid schedule, in office three days a week, and success is measured by a sustained reduction in production incidents traced back to insufficient test coverage.

jobs.title: Order Management QA Analyst
jobs.summary: Merchants depend on the order management system to reconcile what a shopper paid against what actually ships, and small discrepancies there turn into support tickets and refund disputes fast. This entry-level role sits inside the Order Management team and focuses on manual and semi-automated testing of order state transitions: created, paid, fulfilled, refunded, and every edge case in between when a shopper cancels mid-fulfillment or a warehouse partially ships an order. You will write clear test cases in Jira, execute them against each release candidate, and file bug reports detailed enough that an engineer can reproduce the issue without asking follow-up questions. Over your first few months you will also start learning the team's emerging automation suite, pairing with a senior QA engineer to convert your most repeated manual checks into scripted tests. This is a good fit for someone early in a QA career who wants hands-on exposure to a real transactional system rather than a synthetic training environment. You will also sit in on the order management team's sprint planning, giving you visibility into upcoming changes before they reach a release candidate rather than encountering them cold. The role reports to the order management team's dedicated QA lead on a daily basis. The role is based onsite in Berlin, working alongside the order management engineers five days a week, and the team values careful documentation over speed in the first year.

jobs.title: API Test Engineer
jobs.summary: Postman collections and contract tests are the backbone of how Vantail Systems verifies its public developer API before every release, and this six-month contract role is focused entirely on strengthening that layer ahead of a major API version upgrade. You will build and maintain automated contract tests using Postman and Newman, wired into the CI pipeline so that any breaking change to a request or response schema fails the build immediately rather than surfacing in a partner integration weeks later. Working alongside the API platform team, you will audit existing endpoints for undocumented behavior, write the missing test coverage, and flag inconsistencies to the engineering lead before they become public contract commitments. The contract runs through the end of the version migration window, with a possible extension if the scope grows. This is a remote, hourly engagement open to candidates across Europe, and the team expects overlap with Central European working hours for daily standups.

jobs.title: Payments API Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: External developers integrating Vantail's Payments API are often building their first checkout flow, and this role exists to make that first integration go smoothly rather than becoming a support escalation. You will write and maintain the getting-started guides, sample applications, and reference implementations that most developers touch before their first successful test transaction, working in close partnership with the API platform engineers to keep documentation accurate as endpoints evolve. A meaningful part of the role is proactive: monitoring developer forums and support tickets for recurring points of confusion, then fixing the documentation or sample code rather than only answering the same question repeatedly. You will also represent the developer's perspective in API design reviews, pushing back when a proposed change would make integration harder without a clear benefit. Some travel is expected for developer meetups and partner workshops, roughly four to six times a year. You will also maintain a running list of the most common integration questions from support tickets, using it to prioritize which documentation gaps get fixed first each sprint. This role reports into the senior developer advocate who owns the integrations portfolio. This posting is open to internal transfer candidates first, reflecting Vantail's preference to grow this function from people who already understand the platform, and the role is fully remote within North America.

jobs.title: Senior Integrations Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Time to first successful API call is the metric this role is judged against, and lowering it across Vantail's growing base of platform integrators is the primary mandate. As a senior developer advocate focused on integrations, you will lead the technical relationship with Vantail's largest platform partners, the point-of-sale and storefront builders whose customers rely on Vantail's checkout underneath their own branding. That means building reference integrations for the three most common partner tech stacks, running technical enablement sessions for partner engineering teams, and escalating platform gaps directly to product management when a partner hits a wall the current API cannot solve cleanly. You will also mentor two more junior advocates on public speaking and technical writing, since the team is growing its conference presence this year. Strong written and verbal communication matters as much as coding ability here, along with enough backend experience to read and critique another engineer's integration code. You will also maintain a scorecard tracking integration health across the partner portfolio, flagging any partner whose implementation has quietly drifted out of date with current best practices. The role reports into the head of developer relations rather than into engineering. The role is remote within North America, with quarterly travel for partner summits, and the team reviews integration health metrics together every two weeks.

jobs.title: Staff Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Setting the multi-year developer experience strategy for Vantail's public API surface falls to this staff-level role, which operates one level above individual advocacy work and closer to product strategy. You will decide which developer segments the advocacy team prioritizes each year, merchants building custom storefronts versus platform partners versus independent app developers on Vantail's marketplace, and you will defend that prioritization to the VP of Product when resources are tight. Concretely, this means owning the annual developer experience roadmap, running the research that identifies where developers abandon integration attempts, and partnering with the API platform team to fix the underlying friction rather than only documenting around it. You will also be the final editorial reviewer for major documentation overhauls and the person other advocates escalate to when a partner relationship needs executive-level attention. Expect to represent Vantail at two or three major industry conferences a year as a featured speaker, and to publish periodic state-of-the-platform posts that set expectations with the broader developer community. This role requires a track record of shipping developer-facing programs at scale, comfort operating with significant autonomy, and enough technical depth to be credible in a room of staff engineers. The position is fully remote within North America, and the team's health is tracked through a quarterly developer satisfaction survey rather than raw content output.

jobs.title: Developer Community Lead
jobs.summary: A growing but fragmented community of independent developers builds tools and plugins on top of Vantail's platform, and this lead role exists to give that community a real home rather than leaving it scattered across side channels. You will run Vantail's official developer community spaces, moderate discussions, organize a recurring virtual meetup, and identify the most active contributors for a formal partner recognition program launching next year. Managing two community coordinators, you will set the editorial calendar for community content, decide which community-built integrations get featured in official documentation, and represent community sentiment in quarterly roadmap planning meetings with product leadership. A recurring responsibility is triaging community-reported bugs into the right engineering queue with enough context that they get picked up rather than lost. You will also run a lightweight ambassador program recognizing the community's most helpful contributors with early access to new features, giving the program's most engaged members a genuine reason to keep showing up. Community engagement metrics are reviewed together with marketing leadership every month. This is a hybrid role split between Vantail's Berlin and Amsterdam offices, roughly three days a week in one of the two locations, and success is measured through community retention and the number of community-sourced improvements that ship into the core product.

jobs.title: API Documentation Writer
jobs.summary: Clear, accurate reference documentation is what stands between a developer and a working integration, and this freelance engagement is focused on rewriting the weakest sections of Vantail's API reference ahead of a public developer conference. You will audit the existing docs for the checkout and fraud APIs against the actual current behavior of each endpoint, rewrite unclear sections, and add working code samples in at least three languages for the most commonly used endpoints. The engagement is scoped to roughly twelve weeks, coordinated closely with the API platform team so that documentation changes track any last-minute endpoint adjustments before the conference date. Strong technical writing skills and comfort reading API specifications directly, rather than relying on secondhand explanations, are essential. This is a fully remote, project-based engagement open to writers anywhere, with weekly check-ins over video call to review progress against the documentation backlog.

jobs.title: Merchant Support Engineer
jobs.summary: Merchant support tickets at Vantail range from a misconfigured webhook to a genuinely broken payment path affecting live transactions, and this role is responsible for triaging that spectrum accurately under time pressure. You will be the first technical point of contact for merchants reporting checkout or payments issues, reproducing problems where possible, and routing confirmed platform bugs to the right engineering team with clear reproduction steps. A meaningful part of the role involves reading application logs and API request traces to distinguish a merchant configuration mistake from an actual platform defect, since misrouting either wastes engineering time or leaves a merchant stuck. You will also maintain the internal troubleshooting playbooks that the wider support team relies on, updating them as new failure patterns emerge. You will also join a monthly cross-team review with the checkout and payments engineering leads, surfacing recurring merchant complaints that point to a genuine product gap rather than one-off confusion. This is a hybrid role based out of the Amsterdam office, typically three days a week onsite, and the team operates a rotating on-call schedule covering evenings during peak retail seasons.

jobs.title: Checkout Customer Success Engineer
jobs.summary: Larger merchants on Vantail's platform get a named technical point of contact rather than a general support queue, and that relationship is what this senior customer success engineer role owns for a portfolio of roughly twenty accounts. You will run quarterly technical reviews with each merchant's engineering team, proactively flag checkout performance issues before the merchant notices them, and coordinate internally when a merchant's roadmap needs earlier access to an upcoming platform feature. Because your accounts span different regions and payment method mixes, you will need to understand not just the API but the regional payment landscape each merchant operates in. Expect close collaboration with the sales team during renewal conversations, providing the technical credibility that closes expansion deals, and with product management when a pattern across your accounts points to a real product gap. You will also join the checkout team's quarterly roadmap review as the voice of merchant feedback, since patterns across your twenty accounts are often the clearest signal of where a planned feature will land well or fall flat. The role reports into the head of customer success for the payments product line specifically. This role has flexible working arrangements, with the expectation of overlapping availability with merchant time zones across Europe when a critical issue requires it, and success is tracked through account health scores and renewal rates.

jobs.title: Technical Sourcer
jobs.summary: Backend and platform engineering roles at Vantail take longer to fill than the rest of the org because the payments domain narrows the qualified candidate pool considerably, and this sourcing role exists specifically to build a deeper pipeline for those harder searches. You will partner with hiring managers across the payments and checkout engineering teams to translate vague role requirements into concrete sourcing criteria, then run targeted outreach campaigns across LinkedIn, GitHub, and niche fintech engineering communities. A typical week includes reviewing inbound applications for technical fit, building longlists for open roles through Boolean search and direct outreach, and tracking outreach response rates to refine messaging that consistently underperforms. You will work inside the team's ATS daily and report pipeline health metrics to the recruiting manager weekly. This role is based in Berlin on a hybrid schedule, three days a week in the office, and is a good fit for someone who enjoys the research and outreach side of recruiting more than the closing and negotiation side.

jobs.title: Payments Sales Engineer
jobs.summary: Enterprise merchants evaluating Vantail's payments platform almost always want a technical proof of concept before signing, and this senior sales engineer role is responsible for running that proof of concept from first technical call through a working pilot integration. You will partner with account executives on the largest deals in the pipeline, translating a prospect's existing checkout architecture into a realistic Vantail integration plan, then building the demo environment that proves the integration works with the prospect's actual payment methods and currencies. Because payment stacks vary so much by region, you will often need to configure demos covering multiple card schemes or local payment methods within a single sales cycle. You will also write technical responses to security questionnaires and RFPs, working with the security team to keep template answers current. Compensation includes a variable component tied to closed enterprise deals in your supported territory, in addition to base salary. You will also maintain the internal demo environment library so it stays current with the platform's latest payment method support, since an outdated demo undermines credibility with a technically sophisticated prospect. This role is remote within North America, with roughly twenty percent travel for onsite prospect meetings, and success is measured by technical win rate on qualified opportunities.

jobs.title: Detection Rules QA Tester
jobs.summary: New detection rules at Ironvale Security have to be validated against a library of known attack simulations before they ship, since a rule that is too loose floods analysts with noise and one that is too strict lets a real attack through undetected. This entry-level role is responsible for running that validation: executing test attack scenarios against staged detection rules, comparing actual alerts to expected outcomes, and logging discrepancies in enough detail that the detection engineering team can fix the rule logic. You will work daily inside the SIEM test environment, learning the underlying query language used to write detection logic even though you will not be writing production rules yourself in this role. Over time you will take on a growing share of the regression suite that runs before every rule library release. This is a strong first role for someone interested in a security career who wants hands-on exposure to real detection logic rather than starting purely in a generalist support seat. You will also shadow the detection engineering team during their weekly rule review meeting, building context for why certain rules are tuned the way they are rather than only testing them from the outside. This exposure is intentional, since the team hires most of its future detection engineers from within this QA function. The position is based onsite at the Austin office, working directly alongside the detection engineering team five days a week.

jobs.title: Security Research Technical Writer
jobs.summary: Ironvale's threat research team regularly discovers new attacker techniques worth publishing, but the researchers themselves are stretched thin and their draft write-ups often need real editorial work before they are ready for a public audience. This freelance engagement is focused on turning research notes into polished threat intelligence reports and blog posts, working directly with the researchers to preserve technical accuracy while making the writing accessible to a security practitioner audience rather than only to other researchers. You will also standardize the report template the team uses so that future publications require less editorial back-and-forth. The engagement is structured around a rolling queue of research write-ups rather than a fixed weekly schedule, with payment tied to completed pieces. Strong familiarity with security terminology and enough technical background to ask researchers the right clarifying questions are essential, since factual errors in a published threat report damage credibility quickly. You will also help the research team think through responsible disclosure timing on their more sensitive findings, since a report published too early can tip off the very attackers it describes before affected vendors have patched. A portfolio of prior published technical writing samples is required as part of the application. This is a fully remote, project-based engagement open to writers anywhere with a security research background.

jobs.title: Security Escalations Team Lead
jobs.summary: A customer-reported false negative, meaning an attack the platform should have caught but did not, gets escalated to this team the moment it is confirmed, and how fast that escalation moves from report to root cause often determines whether Ironvale keeps that customer's trust. As lead of the security escalations team, you will own the on-call rotation covering critical customer incidents, personally take the most severe escalations, and coach the four engineers on your team through the ones you delegate. You will build the postmortem process for detection misses, working with detection engineering to ensure each miss produces either a rule fix or documented reasoning for why the behavior was correctly out of scope. A significant part of the role is upward communication: briefing customer-facing leadership on active incidents in language that is accurate without inducing panic. This posting is open to internal candidates first, since the role requires deep familiarity with Ironvale's detection stack that is hard to build from outside. You will also run tabletop incident simulations quarterly, testing whether the team's escalation process actually holds up under a scenario more severe than anything the team has faced in recent memory. The lead also carries a pager for the most severe incidents even outside the standard weekly rotation. The role is hybrid out of Austin, and the on-call rotation includes weekend coverage shared evenly across the team.

jobs.title: Tier 1 Support Specialist
jobs.summary: The first line of Ironvale's support queue handles everything from license activation questions to customers unsure why a specific alert fired, and this role is the first real filter that keeps more complex issues from clogging the escalation path unnecessarily. You will triage incoming tickets through Zendesk, resolve straightforward configuration and account questions directly, and write clear handoff notes when a ticket needs to move to a specialist team. Expect to spend real time in your first weeks learning to read platform logs well enough to tell a genuine bug from a misconfiguration, since that judgment call is the core skill the role builds. You will also track recurring question patterns and suggest additions to the internal knowledge base so common issues get resolved faster over time. This role is based onsite at the Krakow security operations office, working a standard weekday shift with occasional weekend coverage during major incident response events.

jobs.title: Enterprise Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary: A handful of Ironvale's largest enterprise customers run security operations centers that never stop, and each one is assigned a single technical account manager who understands their specific detection tuning, integration setup, and internal escalation preferences well enough to be useful during a live incident. This twelve-month contract role covers roughly eight such accounts, running quarterly technical reviews, coordinating custom detection rule requests with the detection engineering team, and serving as the account's advocate when platform limitations affect their specific environment. You will need to become fluent in each account's unique deployment, since generic advice does not hold much value with customers this sophisticated. Expect direct exposure to security leadership at major enterprise customers and correspondingly high expectations for responsiveness. You will also document configuration decisions for each account in enough detail that a colleague could step in during a vacation or handoff without starting from zero. The engagement is remote within North America, structured as a fixed-term contract with the possibility of conversion to a permanent role depending on business needs at the end of the term.

jobs.title: Threat Escalation Engineer
jobs.summary: When an alert a customer flags as suspicious turns out to need deeper investigation than the first-line support team can provide, it lands with this role, which sits at the boundary between customer support and the detection engineering organization. You will investigate escalated alerts using the platform's own log analysis tooling, determine whether the underlying detection logic behaved correctly, and either close the loop with the customer directly or file a detailed engineering ticket when a genuine rule gap is found. A meaningful part of the job is pattern recognition across escalations: if three customers report a similar false positive within a week, you are expected to flag that trend proactively rather than treating each ticket in isolation. You will work a rotating shift that includes some evening coverage, since security incidents do not confine themselves to business hours. You will also help onboard newer support engineers onto the log analysis tooling, since that skill takes longest to build and directly determines how quickly someone can handle escalations independently. This role is hybrid out of the Krakow office, and strong log analysis skills matter more here than prior customer-facing experience.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.summary: Renewal conversations for security software tend to hinge on whether a customer's security team actually trusts the platform, not just whether the contract terms are favorable, and building that trust over the life of an account is the core of this senior customer success manager role. You will own a portfolio of mid-market and enterprise accounts, running onboarding through to renewal, tracking adoption of key detection features, and flagging accounts showing early signs of disengagement before they become churn risks. Expect close coordination with the technical account management team on your larger accounts and with the product team when customer feedback across your portfolio suggests a real roadmap gap. You will also build and deliver quarterly business reviews that translate platform usage data into a narrative the customer's leadership actually finds useful. This role is fully remote within Europe, and compensation includes a retention-linked bonus component on top of base salary.

jobs.title: Security Sales Engineer
jobs.summary: Prospective customers evaluating Ironvale almost always want to see the platform catch a simulated attack in their own environment before they trust it with real production traffic, and running that live demonstration convincingly is the core skill this sales engineer role builds. You will support account executives through the technical stages of the sales cycle, configuring proof-of-concept environments, answering architecture and deployment questions, and building custom demo scenarios that map to a specific prospect's threat model rather than a generic script. You will also respond to security questionnaires and compliance documentation requests, working with the security and legal teams to keep answer templates current. This is a growth-track role for someone earlier in a sales engineering career who wants to build toward more senior technical sales responsibility. You will shadow senior sales engineers on your first several proof-of-concept engagements before running one independently, and the team reviews demo scripts together monthly to keep them current against the product roadmap. The position is hybrid out of the Austin office, and there is a variable compensation component tied to sourced and supported deal value.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer
