jobs.summary: Every enterprise prospect arrives with a different existing security stack, and this senior solutions engineer role is responsible for designing a realistic integration architecture that fits Ironvale into that stack without requiring the customer to rip out tools they already trust. You will lead technical discovery calls, produce architecture diagrams and integration plans for the largest opportunities in the pipeline, and write formal responses to RFPs alongside the deal desk team. A significant part of the role involves partnering with product management, since the patterns you see across enterprise deals are often the clearest signal of where the platform's integration story has real gaps. You will also mentor two more junior sales engineers on solution design methodology. You will also maintain a shared library of architecture patterns other sales engineers reuse across similar deals, reducing how often every opportunity starts from a blank page. This role is fully remote within North America, with roughly twenty-five percent travel for onsite architecture workshops with the largest prospects, and success is tracked through technical win rate on opportunities you support.

jobs.title: Sales Operations Manager
jobs.summary: Sales processes that worked when Ironvale had twenty account executives start to break down at eighty, and this role exists to redesign those processes before they become a real bottleneck to growth. You will own the sales technology stack, including Salesforce configuration, quote generation, and the deal approval workflow, making changes based on direct feedback from account executives rather than top-down mandate alone. A current priority is rebuilding the territory assignment model, which has not kept pace with the company's shift toward larger enterprise deals. You will also run sales onboarding for new hires' first two weeks on the systems and process side, handing off to enablement for product training. This role partners closely with finance on compensation plan design and with the VP of Sales on quarterly planning. The position is hybrid out of the Austin office, three days a week, and success is measured by how little sales process friction shows up in quarterly rep feedback surveys.

jobs.title: Partner Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary: Ironvale sells a meaningful share of its enterprise business through managed security service provider partners, and this role provides the technical enablement those partners need to sell and deploy the platform without pulling in Ironvale's own sales engineering team every time. You will build partner-facing technical training materials, run enablement sessions for new partner engineers, and serve as the escalation point when a partner's deployment hits an issue their own team cannot resolve. A meaningful part of the role is technical, not just educational: you will occasionally join partner-led customer calls directly when a deal is large enough to warrant it. You will also maintain the technical certification program partner engineers complete before they are authorized to deploy Ironvale independently. This role has flexible working arrangements and is open to candidates globally, with the expectation of adjusting working hours occasionally to cover partner time zones outside North America.

jobs.title: Talent Sourcing Coordinator
jobs.summary: Filling specialized detection engineering and threat research roles at Ironvale requires sourcing candidates who rarely respond to generic outreach, and this part-time coordinator role focuses specifically on building and organizing those harder pipelines. You will research candidates across LinkedIn, security conference speaker lists, and open-source security tooling contributors, then coordinate initial outreach and schedule first-round conversations for the recruiting team. A meaningful part of the role is administrative precision: keeping the applicant tracking system current, ensuring interview feedback is logged promptly, and flagging candidates who have gone quiet so nothing falls through unnoticed. This role works roughly twenty-five hours a week, fully remote, with flexibility on which days those hours fall as long as there is overlap with the recruiting team's core hours for coordination.

jobs.title: Network QA Engineer
jobs.summary: Carrier networks generate a scale of telemetry that most testing tools were never designed for, and this senior QA role exists to make sure Lumenbridge's network analytics platform stays accurate as that data volume keeps growing. You will design and maintain automated test suites in Python that validate the platform's ingestion pipeline against real anonymized carrier traffic samples, catching data quality regressions before they reach a customer's operations dashboard. A recurring project this year is building load tests that simulate a full regional carrier's traffic volume, since the current test environment tops out well below what the largest customers actually push through the platform. You will work closely with the data engineering team to understand new ingestion formats before they ship, building test coverage in parallel rather than after the fact. Solid Python skills and comfort with networking concepts like NetFlow or SNMP will make the domain easier to pick up, though the team will train the right candidate on carrier-specific protocols. You will also contribute test scenarios to the shared fixture library other product teams draw from, since realistic carrier traffic samples are expensive to produce and valuable across more than just your own team's suite. This role is remote within Europe, and the team runs a shared on-call rotation covering ingestion pipeline incidents.

jobs.title: Staff SDET
jobs.summary: Lumenbridge's test infrastructure grew organically across five product teams over several years, and each team now maintains its own automation stack, its own CI configuration, and its own definition of what a passing build actually means, which slows every team down more than any of them realize. This staff SDET role exists to fix that at the architecture level rather than one team at a time. You will design a shared test infrastructure platform that every product team can adopt without rewriting their existing test suites from scratch, including a common CI orchestration layer, shared test data fixtures for carrier network simulations, and a unified flaky-test detection system. Expect significant cross-team negotiation, since asking five teams to migrate onto shared infrastructure requires convincing each one the switch is worth the short-term disruption. You will also serve as the final technical reviewer for any new automation framework a team proposes adopting, keeping the overall test ecosystem from fragmenting further. This role requires deep hands-on testing experience plus genuine platform engineering skill, since the deliverable is infrastructure other engineers build on, not test scripts for a single product. You will also publish short design-decision write-ups for the wider engineering organization as the shared platform takes shape. The position is fully remote within North America, and progress is tracked through a quarterly reduction in average CI run time across all five product teams.

jobs.title: Performance Test Engineer
jobs.summary: Load spikes during regional network outages are exactly when Lumenbridge's analytics platform needs to keep working, since that is when carriers rely on it most to understand what is failing, and this six-month contract role is focused on proving the platform holds up under those conditions. You will design and run performance test scenarios using JMeter that simulate sudden traffic surges into the ingestion pipeline, identify the components that degrade first, and document findings clearly enough for the platform engineering team to prioritize fixes. Expect to build a repeatable performance testing framework that the team can rerun before each major release, since currently performance testing happens ad hoc only when someone remembers to schedule it. You will report directly to the engineering lead for the ingestion pipeline and present findings at the end of each testing cycle. You will also document the specific bottlenecks uncovered during testing in enough technical detail that the platform engineering team can prioritize fixes without needing a live walkthrough of every test run. This is a remote, fixed-term contract open to candidates across Europe, running through the end of the current fiscal year with possible extension.

jobs.title: Mobile QA Engineer
jobs.summary: Field technicians at Lumenbridge's carrier customers rely on a mobile app to diagnose network issues on site, often in basements or remote cell tower locations with unreliable connectivity, and this senior QA role is responsible for making sure that app behaves correctly under exactly those difficult conditions. You will build and maintain Appium-based automated tests covering both iOS and Android versions of the app, with particular focus on offline mode behavior and sync reconciliation once connectivity returns. A significant part of the role is manual exploratory testing on physical devices in simulated poor-connectivity conditions, since automated tests alone do not reliably catch the flakiness that shows up on real hardware in the field. You will also work directly with field technicians during quarterly user research sessions to understand pain points that never surface in a bug report. You will also help maintain the device lab's aging hardware inventory, flagging when older test devices no longer represent what field technicians actually carry. This role is hybrid out of the Dublin office, three days a week, with a device lab onsite for physical testing that cannot be done remotely.

jobs.title: Accessibility QA Engineer
jobs.summary: Network operations dashboards at Lumenbridge are used around the clock by carrier operations staff, some of whom rely on screen readers or high-contrast modes due to visual impairments, and this role exists to make sure the platform's accessibility does not degrade as new dashboard features ship. You will audit new features against WCAG standards before release, test with actual screen reader software rather than only automated accessibility scanners, and file detailed remediation tickets when a component fails to meet the bar. You will also maintain the internal accessibility checklist that designers and engineers reference before starting new dashboard work, updating it as the platform's component library evolves. Expect to run periodic training sessions for the design team on common accessibility pitfalls in data-dense dashboard interfaces specifically, which behave differently than typical marketing pages. You will also coordinate with an external accessibility auditor who reviews the platform twice a year, tracking remediation of any findings through to actual completion rather than just filing tickets. This role is based onsite at the Warsaw office, working closely with the dashboard product team five days a week.

jobs.title: Principal Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Carrier engineering teams evaluating Lumenbridge's network analytics APIs are a narrow, technically sophisticated audience, and reaching them effectively looks nothing like typical developer marketing aimed at a broad consumer API audience. As principal developer advocate, you will set the entire developer relations strategy for this niche audience, deciding which telecom industry conferences are worth Lumenbridge's presence, which carrier engineering communities deserve direct outreach, and which technical content formats actually land with network engineers rather than general software developers. You will personally build the flagship reference integrations that showcase the platform's API against real carrier use cases like fraud detection and network capacity planning, since generic sample apps do not resonate with this audience. A core part of the role is representing the developer's technical perspective directly to the VP of Product during quarterly roadmap planning, using direct feedback from carrier engineering contacts rather than secondhand assumptions. You will also build and personally maintain relationships with a small number of technical champions inside major carrier customers, since in this industry a handful of respected voices carry more influence than broad top-of-funnel content ever will. This role requires deep credibility with a technical telecom audience, comfort operating with significant autonomy, and enough networking domain knowledge to be taken seriously in rooms full of network engineers. The position is fully remote globally, with quarterly travel to major telecom industry conferences, and impact is measured through qualified pipeline the advocacy program contributes rather than raw content metrics.

jobs.title: Developer Relations Manager
jobs.summary: Growing Lumenbridge's developer relations function from two individual contributors into a fuller team is the primary mandate of this manager role, reporting into the VP of Marketing. You will hire and manage a small team covering technical content, community, and developer advocacy, setting quarterly priorities that balance long-term community building against the more immediate demands of upcoming conference deadlines. Expect to personally take over some of the editorial planning responsibilities that currently sit informally with individual advocates, giving the function a coherent content calendar for the first time. You will represent developer relations in the broader marketing leadership team, defending the function's budget and headcount requests with concrete metrics on developer engagement and pipeline contribution. A near-term priority is standing up a proper event budget and calendar for telecom industry conferences, which the team has historically attended reactively rather than strategically. This posting is open to internal candidates first, given the specialized telecom industry knowledge the role benefits from. You will also manage the function's relationship with external conference organizers, negotiating speaking slots and booth placement well ahead of each major telecom industry event. The function's annual conference travel budget is reviewed and approved directly by marketing leadership each fiscal year. The position is hybrid out of the Dublin office, three days a week.

jobs.title: Technical Content Strategist
jobs.summary: Lumenbridge's technical content library has grown inconsistently over several years, with some topics covered by three overlapping articles and others, like the newer fraud detection API, barely documented at all, and this freelance engagement is focused on fixing that imbalance. You will audit the existing content library against actual product usage data to identify the highest-impact gaps, then build a content calendar and either write or commission the pieces needed to close them. Expect close collaboration with the product marketing team to make sure content strategy aligns with upcoming feature launches rather than working from an outdated roadmap. You will also establish basic content performance tracking so future prioritization can be data-driven rather than based on which topic someone happened to feel strongly about. You will also run a lightweight content audit every quarter, retiring outdated pieces that no longer reflect the current product rather than letting the library grow indefinitely. This is a remote, hourly engagement structured around a rolling twelve-week initial scope, with strong technical writing and content strategy experience required, ideally with some exposure to a technical or infrastructure product audience.

jobs.title: Carrier API Technical Writer
jobs.summary: Terminology and data formats in telecom differ meaningfully from general-purpose software APIs, so generic documentation templates translate poorly for the carrier engineers integrating Lumenbridge's network analytics API. This part-time role is responsible for maintaining and expanding that carrier-specific documentation, working directly with the API platform engineers to verify accuracy against actual endpoint behavior before publishing updates. You will also build worked examples using realistic anonymized carrier data, since documentation that only shows toy examples underperforms badly with this technically sophisticated audience. A recurring task is reviewing support ticket themes each month for documentation gaps that could have prevented the ticket entirely. This role works roughly twenty hours a week with flexible scheduling, remote within Europe, and is well suited to someone with prior telecom or networking domain exposure who wants a lighter weekly commitment.

jobs.title: Network Operations Success Engineer
jobs.summary: Carrier operations teams using Lumenbridge's platform to monitor their own network uptime have very little tolerance for the monitoring tool itself having problems, and this senior success engineer role exists to keep that relationship healthy through proactive technical partnership rather than reactive ticket handling. You will run technical health checks against your assigned accounts' platform configuration on a regular cadence, catching misconfigurations or underused features before they become a source of customer frustration. Expect to lead onboarding for new carrier customers through their first ninety days, coordinating with the professional services team on any custom integration work required. You will also build the technical justification for renewal and expansion conversations, working closely with the account's assigned salesperson. You will also collaborate with the professional services team on a shared account handoff process, since a rocky transition from onboarding into steady-state support is a common source of early account friction. This role has flexible working arrangements within Europe, and success is tracked through account health scores and the technical adoption rate of key platform features across your portfolio.

jobs.title: Senior Carrier Account Manager
jobs.summary: A small number of carrier accounts generate a disproportionate share of Lumenbridge's revenue, and this senior account manager role is responsible for the technical and commercial health of roughly a dozen of the largest ones. You will run quarterly business reviews that combine platform usage data with a clear-eyed view of the account's satisfaction, coordinate custom feature requests with product management, and manage the renewal process well ahead of contract expiration to avoid last-minute negotiation pressure. Because carrier procurement cycles move slowly and involve multiple stakeholders, you will need patience and organizational skill to keep a renewal moving through legal and procurement without losing momentum. Expect to travel occasionally to carrier customer sites for major account reviews or executive relationship building. This role is hybrid out of the Dublin office, and compensation includes a component tied to renewal and expansion revenue across your account portfolio.

jobs.title: Recruiting Coordinator
jobs.summary: Interview scheduling across five hiring teams and three time zones is more complex than it sounds, and this entry-level coordinator role is what keeps Lumenbridge's hiring process moving without candidates falling through administrative cracks. You will schedule interviews, prepare interviewer packets with candidate background and structured feedback forms, and make sure feedback gets logged in the applicant tracking system before the next interview stage is scheduled. You will also serve as a candidate's main point of contact throughout the process, answering logistics questions and keeping them informed about timeline, since a slow or confusing process is one of the most common reasons strong candidates drop out. Over time you will take on more sourcing support work as you learn the recruiting function more broadly. This posting is open to internal candidates first as part of Lumenbridge's internal mobility program, based onsite at the Warsaw office.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.summary: Closing new carrier logos is a long game, often twelve to eighteen months from first conversation to signed contract, and this senior account executive role is measured against a quota built around exactly that reality rather than shorter software sales cycles. You will own the full sales cycle for enterprise carrier accounts in your territory, from initial outbound through technical evaluation, working closely with a dedicated solutions engineer on every serious opportunity. Because carrier buying committees typically include network operations, IT security, and procurement stakeholders with different priorities, you will need to build a coalition of internal champions rather than relying on a single relationship. Expect regular collaboration with product marketing on competitive positioning against the two other analytics vendors carriers most commonly evaluate. Compensation includes a significant commission component tied to closed annual contract value, with accelerators for exceeding quota. This role is remote within North America, with regular travel to carrier customer sites and industry conferences.

jobs.title: Deal Desk Analyst
jobs.summary: Custom pricing terms and non-standard contract structures come up constantly in carrier deals, since large telecom customers rarely accept Lumenbridge's standard order form without modification, and this deal desk role exists to process those exceptions quickly without exposing the company to unnecessary risk. You will review deal terms against approval policy, route exceptions to the right internal stakeholder for sign-off, and maintain the pricing and discounting guidelines that sales reps reference when structuring a proposal. A recurring responsibility is auditing closed deals against the original approved terms to catch discrepancies before they cause revenue recognition problems later. You will also train new account executives on deal desk processes during their onboarding. This role is hybrid out of the Boston office, and closely partners with legal, finance, and revenue operations, especially during the final week of each quarter when deal volume spikes.

jobs.title: Test Automation Architect
jobs.summary: Matchmaking and session-management services at Northfen Interactive have to hold up under sudden concurrent-player spikes every time a new title launches or a major update drops, and this senior architect role is responsible for the automated test strategy that catches problems before millions of players do. You will design the test automation architecture for the multiplayer backend, choosing frameworks in Python that can simulate realistic concurrent player load against staging environments before every major release. A significant piece of the role is building chaos-style tests that deliberately fail individual backend services mid-match to verify the client degrades gracefully rather than disconnecting players outright. You will work closely with the backend engineering leads to embed test hooks directly into new services as they are built, rather than testing only from the outside after the fact. This role requires strong distributed systems intuition in addition to test automation skill, since the failure modes worth testing for are rarely obvious from the API surface alone. You will also run a quarterly architecture review with the automation leads on each of the studio's product teams, keeping the shared test infrastructure from drifting apart as individual teams evolve their own needs. The position is based onsite at the Montreal studio, working alongside the backend platform team five days a week.

jobs.title: Lead QA Engineer
jobs.summary: Launch day for a new Northfen title is when the quality team's work either holds up under real player load or does not, and this lead role is responsible for making sure the QA team is genuinely ready well before that day arrives. You will manage a team of six QA engineers across automated testing and structured playtesting, setting the test plan for each major release and deciding where the team's limited time is best spent between automation, exploratory testing, and organized playtest sessions. Expect to run the go or no-go readiness review before each release, presenting known issues and risk assessment directly to the studio's production leadership. You will also mentor two engineers currently transitioning from manual testing into automation, structuring their ramp-up so it does not slow the team's regular release cadence. A background in game QA specifically is preferred, since the bug patterns in live multiplayer titles differ meaningfully from typical enterprise software testing. You will also own the team's testing budget for external device farms and load-testing infrastructure, making the case for additional investment when the studio's growing player base outpaces current tooling capacity. The role also reports monthly quality metrics directly up to the director of quality engineering. This role is based onsite at the Montreal studio, and the team works an adjusted schedule around major launch weeks that can include weekend coverage.

jobs.title: Director of Quality Engineering
jobs.summary: Northfen Interactive ships live-service titles that players expect to keep working around the clock, and the quality organization this director role leads is responsible for the testing strategy across every studio team, from the core multiplayer backend through individual game clients. You will set quality standards and budget priorities across four QA teams currently reporting through separate leads, consolidating them under a shared strategy for the first time as the studio scales past its original single-title structure. A major initiative this year is building a dedicated live-ops testing capability that can validate in-game events and seasonal content changes without requiring a full regression pass each time, since the current process cannot keep pace with the studio's event cadence. You will report directly to the VP of Engineering and represent quality risk in executive release readiness discussions ahead of every major launch. This posting is open to internal candidates first, reflecting the studio's preference to promote from leaders who already understand its specific live-service challenges. You will also chair the studio's cross-team quality guild, a recurring forum where QA leads from every product team share techniques and calibrate severity definitions consistently. The role is based onsite at the Montreal studio, and success is measured through a sustained reduction in post-launch critical incidents across all titles.

jobs.title: Playtest QA Intern
jobs.summary: Spending a summer testing unreleased multiplayer game builds before anyone outside the studio has touched them is what this internship offers, working directly alongside Northfen's QA team on a current in-development title. You will run structured playtest sessions following detailed test scripts, log bugs with clear reproduction steps in the studio's bug tracking tool, and participate in daily bug triage meetings where you will see firsthand how the team prioritizes what gets fixed before launch versus what ships as a known issue. As the internship progresses you will take on small pieces of exploratory testing with less structure, building the judgment needed to find bugs that a script would not catch. This is a twelve-week paid internship based onsite at the Montreal studio, working full time alongside the permanent QA team, and is intended as a genuine entry point into a QA career in games rather than purely administrative work.

jobs.title: Live Ops QA Analyst
jobs.summary: Seasonal in-game events at Northfen's flagship title ship on a tight two-week cadence, and this role exists to test each one thoroughly within that short window without becoming the bottleneck that slows the live-ops team down. You will test new event content, limited-time modes, and in-game store changes against a checklist tuned specifically for live-ops releases, which move faster and carry different risk than the studio's larger quarterly content updates. A meaningful part of the role is verifying that in-game economy changes, like new currency sinks or reward tuning, behave as designed rather than accidentally breaking the game's balance. You will work directly with the live-ops production team, often testing content that is still being finalized right up until the deployment window. This role is hybrid out of the Helsinki studio, two to three days a week, and the team operates on a schedule aligned to the event release calendar rather than a standard weekly sprint.

jobs.title: Game SDK Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Third-party studios building on top of Northfen's multiplayer backend SDK need working reference implementations and responsive technical support to succeed, and this senior freelance advocate role is focused on exactly that developer-facing relationship. You will maintain and extend the SDK's sample game project, keeping it current as the underlying backend API evolves, and respond directly to integration questions from partner studio engineers in a dedicated developer forum. A recurring piece of the engagement is writing migration guides whenever a backend API version changes, since partner studios often lag several versions behind the latest release and need clear upgrade paths. You will also collect and organize partner feedback into structured input for the backend platform team's roadmap discussions. This is a remote, project-based freelance engagement open to candidates across North America, structured around a rolling six-month scope with the possibility of renewal.

jobs.title: Live Ops Support Engineer
jobs.summary: When a live multiplayer title goes down or a critical bug affects paying players mid-event, this senior support engineer role is one of the first technical responders, working directly with backend engineering to diagnose and mitigate the issue while communicating status to the broader studio. You will maintain and improve the runbooks that guide incident response for common failure patterns, own a share of the rotating on-call schedule covering live titles, and lead post-incident reviews that produce concrete follow-up actions rather than vague lessons-learned notes. Because live-service games generate unique failure modes around concurrent player load and real-money transactions, you will need to build genuine familiarity with the backend architecture rather than working purely from a support ticket queue. You will also partner with the community team during major incidents to ensure player-facing communication stays accurate as the technical picture develops. You will also help design the incident severity framework the studio uses to decide how aggressively to communicate with players during an outage, since overcommunicating minor issues erodes trust just as much as staying silent during a major one. Comfort making judgment calls under pressure, without waiting for perfect information, matters more here than deep game development background. This role is based onsite at the Vancouver studio, and the on-call rotation includes evening and weekend coverage during major launches and live events.

jobs.title: Studio Implementation Consultant
jobs.summary: New partner studios adopting Northfen's multiplayer backend need real implementation support during their first integration, not just documentation, and this consultant role provides that hands-on guidance through each studio's first several months on the platform. You will run technical kickoff sessions with new partner engineering teams, review their integration architecture for common pitfalls before they build too far in the wrong direction, and stay engaged through their first live launch on the platform. A meaningful part of the role involves translating what you learn from each implementation into improvements for the standard onboarding documentation, since patterns that trip up one studio usually trip up the next one too. You will also coordinate internally when a partner studio's timeline requires expedited support from backend engineering. You will also maintain a running log of common integration mistakes across studios, feeding that pattern data back into the SDK team's own roadmap prioritization discussions. This role is based onsite at the Helsinki studio, with occasional travel to partner studio offices for kickoff sessions when the relationship warrants an in-person start.

jobs.title: Player Support Operations Analyst
jobs.summary: Player support ticket volume at Northfen spikes unpredictably around content launches, live events, and the occasional server incident, and this six-month contract role is focused on building the operational visibility the support leadership team currently lacks into those patterns. You will build and maintain dashboards tracking ticket volume, resolution time, and category trends across the player support queue, and produce a weekly report that support leadership uses to staff shifts around predictable demand spikes. A specific project this contract will tackle is modeling expected ticket volume ahead of the next major content launch, using historical data from comparable past launches. You will also audit the support team's tagging taxonomy, which has drifted over time and now makes trend analysis harder than it should be. This is a remote, fixed-term contract open to candidates across North America, running through the end of the studio's current live-ops season.

jobs.title: Engineering Technical Recruiter
jobs.summary: Backend and multiplayer systems engineering roles are consistently the hardest to fill at Northfen, since the pool of engineers with real distributed systems experience in games specifically is small, and this recruiter role owns that hiring pipeline end to end. You will partner directly with backend engineering leads to build accurate role scorecards, manage candidates through the full interview process, and negotiate offers for the roles you own. Expect to build sourcing strategies that go beyond job postings, including outreach at game developer conferences and within specific online communities where backend engineers with the right experience tend to gather. You will also track and report time-to-fill and pipeline health metrics for your requisitions to the recruiting manager weekly. This role is hybrid out of the Montreal studio, three days a week, and works closely with the studio's employer branding efforts around major hiring pushes.

jobs.title: Senior Studio Recruiter
jobs.summary: Full-cycle recruiting for the Vancouver studio's growing live-ops and player support teams falls to this senior recruiter role, covering everything from initial intake conversations with hiring managers through offer negotiation. You will manage a full requisition load independently, coach less experienced hiring managers through structured interviewing, and identify where the studio's current interview process creates unnecessary drop-off among strong candidates. A specific initiative this year is reworking the studio's technical interview loop for support and operations roles, which currently mirrors the engineering interview process even though the skills being assessed are quite different. You will also represent the studio at regional hiring events and build relationships with local community colleges offering relevant technical programs. This role is hybrid out of the Vancouver studio, and success is measured through both time-to-fill and new-hire retention past the first year.

jobs.title: Engineering Recruiting Lead
jobs.summary: Coordinating hiring priorities across Northfen's Montreal, Helsinki, and Vancouver engineering teams requires someone who can see the whole picture rather than just one studio's immediate needs, and that coordination is the core of this recruiting lead role. You will manage a team of four recruiters, each aligned to a specific studio location, setting shared standards for interview process and candidate experience while allowing enough local flexibility for each studio's particular hiring culture. Expect to personally handle the most senior and sensitive searches, including engineering leadership roles, while your team covers individual contributor hiring. You will also own the recruiting team's own hiring and onboarding as the function continues to grow. This role has flexible working arrangements across North America, with regular travel to each studio location roughly once a quarter, and reports directly into the VP of People.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.summary: Independent game studios evaluating multiplayer backend providers rarely respond to a first cold email, and this role exists to build the outbound pipeline that eventually turns into qualified conversations for Northfen's account executive team. You will research target studios based on genre, team size, and current backend provider, then run structured outreach campaigns across email and relevant developer community channels. A meaningful part of the role is qualifying inbound interest from the studio's developer relations content, determining which leads have a real integration timeline versus which are only casually browsing. You will track every touchpoint in the CRM and hand off qualified opportunities to account executives with enough context that the first sales call does not start from zero. This role is based onsite at the Montreal studio, working closely with both the sales and developer relations teams.

jobs.title: Platform Partner Engineer
jobs.summary: Larger partner studios integrating Northfen's backend platform sometimes need custom integration work that goes beyond what standard SDK documentation covers, and this senior engineer role is the technical bridge between those partners and Northfen's own platform engineering team. You will scope and sometimes directly build custom integration solutions for the platform's largest partners, review partner integration architecture for scalability concerns before they become production incidents, and represent partner technical requirements in internal platform roadmap discussions. Expect to travel occasionally to partner studio offices for deeper technical work sessions when a remote relationship is not moving fast enough. You will also build internal tooling that makes future partner integrations faster to scope and support, reducing how much custom work each new partnership actually requires over time. You will also participate in a quarterly partner advisory session, gathering structured feedback that feeds directly into the platform engineering team's roadmap prioritization. This role is based onsite at the Vancouver studio, and requires strong backend engineering skills in addition to partner-facing communication ability.

jobs.title: Claims Systems QA Engineer
jobs.summary: A miscalculated payout in the claims automation engine at Stonebrook Assurance is not just a bug, it is money that either leaves the company incorrectly or leaves a policyholder underpaid, and this senior QA role exists to catch those errors before a single claim processes incorrectly in production. You will build and maintain automated regression suites in Java covering the claims calculation engine, focusing especially on the interaction between policy terms, state-specific insurance regulations, and payout rules that change more often than most software teams expect. A recurring project is expanding test coverage ahead of each quarterly regulatory update cycle, when claims logic often needs adjustment across multiple US states or European jurisdictions simultaneously. You will work closely with the actuarial and compliance teams to translate regulatory language into concrete test scenarios, since misreading a regulation produces a test suite that passes against the wrong expected behavior. You will also maintain a library of jurisdiction-specific test fixtures that the wider engineering team references when building new claims features, reducing how often a regulatory nuance gets missed during initial development. This role is remote within Europe, and the team runs an especially thorough release process around regulatory deadline dates given the financial and compliance stakes involved.

jobs.title: Underwriting API Developer Advocate
jobs.summary: Insurance carriers and brokers integrating Stonebrook's underwriting API are typically working within their own legacy policy administration systems, and this freelance advocate role exists to make that often-awkward integration path as smooth as possible. You will build and maintain sample integrations covering the most common carrier core systems Stonebrook's customers use, write onboarding guides that account for the compliance documentation carriers typically require before connecting a third-party API, and answer technical integration questions in the developer support forum. A recurring part of the engagement is joining onboarding calls for larger carrier prospects to answer technical questions the sales engineering team cannot fully address alone. This is a remote, hourly engagement open to candidates with insurance or fintech integration experience, structured around a rolling monthly scope tied to the current onboarding pipeline.

jobs.title: Policy Platform Customer Success Engineer
jobs.summary: Insurers running their policy administration on Stonebrook's platform depend on it for something as basic as issuing a new policy correctly, and this senior customer success engineer role is responsible for a portfolio of mid-size insurer accounts navigating that dependency day to day. You will run quarterly technical reviews covering platform adoption and configuration health, proactively identify accounts using outdated policy templates that create unnecessary manual work, and coordinate with the professional services team when an account needs a larger configuration change. Because insurance products vary significantly by line of business, from auto to property to specialty lines, you will need to develop genuine fluency in how each of your accounts' specific products are configured on the platform. Expect regular collaboration with the renewals team, providing the technical narrative that supports expansion conversations. This role is hybrid out of the London office, and success is measured through account health scores and reduction in configuration-related support tickets across your portfolio.

jobs.title: Claims Technical Account Manager
jobs.summary: A small set of large insurer accounts route all of their high-value claims through Stonebrook's automation engine, and this senior technical account manager role is the named point of contact those accounts rely on when something in that critical path needs attention. You will maintain deep technical familiarity with each assigned account's specific claims configuration, coordinate custom rule requests with the claims engineering team, and lead quarterly reviews that walk account stakeholders through platform performance and upcoming regulatory changes relevant to their jurisdictions. Expect to be pulled into escalations directly when a claims processing issue affects live payouts, since these accounts expect a technical owner who already understands their setup rather than a generic support intake process. You will also document account-specific configuration decisions thoroughly, since claims logic that seems reasonable in isolation can create unexpected interactions as an account's product lineup grows. You will also maintain a shared regulatory calendar across your accounts, since a jurisdiction's rule change affecting one insurer often affects several others in your portfolio around the same time. Fluency in at least one additional European language is a plus given the current account mix. This role is remote within Europe, and requires comfort working occasionally under real time pressure when a claims issue is actively affecting policyholders.

jobs.title: Support Operations Analyst
jobs.summary: Support ticket data at Stonebrook has historically lived in three disconnected systems, making it hard for support leadership to answer basic questions about where the team's time actually goes, and this analyst role exists to fix that visibility gap. You will consolidate reporting across the ticketing system, the phone support platform, and the internal escalation tracker into a single operational dashboard that support leadership reviews weekly. A recurring project is building a staffing model that accounts for the seasonal spike in claims-related tickets that follows major weather events, since the current staffing approach reacts to volume rather than anticipating it. You will also support the quarterly service-level review, pulling the data that determines whether the team is meeting its contractual response-time commitments to enterprise accounts. You will also benchmark Stonebrook's response times against the contractual service-level commitments made to its largest enterprise accounts, flagging any account trending toward a breach before it happens. This role is based onsite at the Dublin office, working closely with the support leadership team most heavily during the first week of each month when reporting is due.

jobs.title: Enterprise Escalation Engineer
jobs.summary: When a policy administration issue at a large insurer account cannot be resolved by the first-line support team, it lands with this senior escalation engineer role, which sits close enough to engineering to actually diagnose root cause rather than only relaying customer reports. You will investigate escalated issues using the platform's internal diagnostic tooling, determine whether the behavior reflects a genuine defect or a configuration issue on the customer's side, and drive fixes through to resolution by working directly with the relevant engineering team. A meaningful part of the role involves writing clear, non-technical status updates for customer-facing account teams during active escalations, since insurer stakeholders often need plain-language explanations rather than engineering detail. You will also contribute to a growing internal knowledge base of resolved escalations, reducing how often the same root cause needs to be rediscovered. You will also run a monthly retrospective with the first-line support team, sharing patterns from recent escalations so more issues get resolved before reaching your queue at all. Building genuine trust with account teams matters here, since they need to believe an escalation will actually get real engineering attention rather than a templated response. This role is hybrid out of the London office, and the position occasionally requires availability outside standard hours when a high-severity escalation is active.

jobs.title: Insurance Tech Sourcer
jobs.summary: Candidates with real experience in both software engineering and the specific regulatory complexity of insurance technology are genuinely rare, and this six-month contract sourcing role exists to build a deeper pipeline for Stonebrook's hardest-to-fill engineering searches. You will research and directly reach out to engineers with relevant insurtech or fintech backgrounds across LinkedIn and niche industry communities, qualify their interest and fit before handing them to the recruiting team, and track outreach performance to continuously refine messaging. A specific focus this contract is building a pipeline for claims engineering roles, which have been open longest among the team's current searches. You will work inside the team's ATS daily and report weekly on pipeline volume and quality to the recruiting manager. This is a remote, fixed-term contract open to candidates across North America, running through the end of the current hiring cycle.

jobs.title: Executive Search Recruiter
jobs.summary: Stonebrook's engineering leadership team is expanding to support the company's move into two new insurance lines, and this senior contract recruiter role is dedicated entirely to those leadership-level searches rather than the broader individual contributor hiring pipeline. You will run confidential executive searches for director and VP-level engineering roles, building longlists through direct outreach and executive network research, and managing candidates through an extended interview process that typically involves the CEO and board members for the most senior roles. Discretion matters considerably here, since some of these searches involve replacing or restructuring existing leadership before that is public internally. You will also coach hiring executives on how to assess leadership candidates against Stonebrook's specific scaling challenges rather than generic leadership competencies. You will also brief the CEO ahead of each finalist interview, aligning on the specific gaps the hiring team is probing for so evaluation stays consistent across a small interview panel. This is a remote, fixed-term contract engagement open to candidates across North America with prior executive search experience, ideally within technology or financial services.

jobs.title: Engineering Recruiting Manager
jobs.summary: Stonebrook's engineering recruiting team has grown from two recruiters to six over the past year without a clear management structure, and this manager role exists to give that team real leadership and consistent process for the first time. You will manage the team's day-to-day recruiting operations, set hiring priorities in partnership with engineering leadership, and personally take on the most senior or sensitive searches while your team covers the broader individual contributor pipeline. Expect to standardize the team's interview process across engineering, which currently varies significantly from team to team in ways that create an inconsistent candidate experience. You will also own the recruiting team's own headcount planning and represent recruiting capacity constraints honestly to engineering leadership rather than overcommitting on timelines. This posting is open to internal candidates first as part of Stonebrook's internal mobility program. You will also sit on the quarterly diversity hiring review, tracking whether sourcing and interview practices are actually broadening the pipeline rather than only appearing to. The role is hybrid out of the London office, three days a week.

jobs.title: Talent Operations Analyst
jobs.summary: Recruiting process data at Stonebrook currently lives mostly in individual recruiters' heads rather than in structured, reportable form, and this senior analyst role exists to change that as the recruiting function professionalizes. You will own the applicant tracking system's configuration and data quality, build the reporting that recruiting leadership uses for quarterly planning, and design process improvements based on where candidates most commonly drop out of the pipeline. A specific initiative underway is building a proper time-to-fill benchmark broken down by role type and seniority, since the current single blended metric hides meaningful differences between engineering and go-to-market hiring. You will also train recruiters on using the ATS consistently, since inconsistent data entry is currently the biggest obstacle to reliable reporting. You will also maintain the compensation benchmarking data recruiters reference when building offers, working closely with the people operations team to keep those figures current. This role has flexible working arrangements within Europe, and works most closely with the recruiting team during the final weeks of each quarter when planning reviews are due.

jobs.title: VP of Revenue Operations
jobs.summary: Sales, customer success, and renewals data at Stonebrook currently live in systems that do not talk to each other cleanly, and fixing that fragmentation while the company scales into new insurance lines is the mandate for this executive role. As VP of Revenue Operations, you will own the systems, processes, and analytics that support the entire go-to-market organization, reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and sitting on the broader executive leadership team. You will lead a team of eight across sales operations, deal desk, and revenue analytics, and be the executive owner of the forecasting process the CRO presents to the board each quarter. A major initiative in your first year will be consolidating the CRM, billing, and renewal systems that grew separately across the company's original and newly acquired insurance lines into a single coherent data model. You will also partner closely with finance on compensation plan design and with product on usage-based pricing models as the company expands its offerings. This role requires prior experience building revenue operations functions at a scaling B2B software company, strong executive presence, and comfort presenting directly to the board when required. The position is hybrid out of the London office, and success is judged against forecast accuracy and the operational efficiency of the broader go-to-market organization.

jobs.title: Sales Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: Insurance carrier evaluations of Stonebrook's platform almost always require a detailed technical proof of concept against real anonymized claims data, and this manager role leads the team of five sales engineers who run those evaluations across Stonebrook's largest opportunities. You will set technical qualification standards for which opportunities receive full sales engineering support, coach the team through complex enterprise proof-of-concept design, and personally step into the most strategic deals when needed. Expect to work closely with the product team, since proof-of-concept feedback from the sales engineering team is one of the clearer signals of where the platform's actual gaps show up against carrier requirements. You will also own the team's onboarding curriculum, which currently takes new sales engineers nearly six months to become fully productive, a timeline you are expected to shorten. You will also represent sales engineering in the quarterly product roadmap review, translating patterns across dozens of proof-of-concept engagements into a small number of concrete product requests leadership can actually act on. Hiring is a recurring part of the role as the team continues to grow alongside new insurance lines. This role is hybrid out of the Hartford office, with regular travel to carrier customer sites for the largest proof-of-concept engagements, and compensation includes a team-performance-linked bonus component.

jobs.title: Sales Engineering Intern
jobs.summary: Shadowing real enterprise sales cycles for insurance software is not something most internships offer, and that direct exposure is the core of this summer internship on Stonebrook's sales engineering team. You will support senior sales engineers in preparing demo environments, building slide decks that translate technical platform capabilities into language a carrier's business stakeholders understand, and researching prospect accounts ahead of discovery calls. As the internship progresses you will take on a small proof-of-concept configuration project under close supervision, giving you hands-on exposure to the platform's configuration tools rather than only observing from the sidelines. You will also sit in on live customer calls to see how sales engineers handle technical objections in real time. You will also complete a short capstone project at the end of the internship, presenting a mock proof-of-concept plan to the sales engineering team for feedback. This is a twelve-week paid internship based onsite at the Hartford office, working full time alongside the sales engineering team, and includes a structured mentorship program pairing you with a senior engineer for the full duration.

jobs.title: Pre-Sales Solutions Consultant
jobs.summary: Insurance carriers evaluating a new claims or policy administration platform typically want a working proof of concept configured against their own product lines before committing, and this senior contract consultant role is dedicated to running those proof-of-concept engagements for Stonebrook's largest active opportunities. You will configure demo environments using each prospect's actual policy structures and rating rules where possible, lead technical discovery sessions to understand the prospect's current pain points, and build the business case materials that account executives use to justify the deal internally to the prospect's leadership. This six-month contract is scoped around a specific set of active enterprise opportunities in the pipeline, with the possibility of extension based on deal timing. You will work closely with an account executive on each engagement rather than covering opportunities independently. You will also debrief each proof of concept with the product team, since patterns across your engagements often reveal where the platform's configuration tools still require too much manual workaround. This role is remote within North America, with occasional travel for onsite proof-of-concept kickoffs at the largest prospect accounts.

jobs.title: Booking Platform QA Analyst
jobs.summary: A double-booked hotel room because of a race condition in the reservation engine is the kind of bug that turns into an angry guest at a front desk, and this QA role exists to catch exactly that class of problem before it reaches a live property. You will test the booking platform's reservation and availability logic across common scenarios like overlapping date ranges, last-minute cancellations, and rate changes mid-booking, working primarily through manual and semi-scripted testing against the staging environment. You will log detailed bug reports in Jira and work directly with the booking engine engineers to verify fixes before each release goes out to properties. A recurring responsibility is maintaining the regression checklist that the team runs before every release, updating it as new booking scenarios are discovered through real property feedback. You will also participate in the monthly bug bash the wider engineering team runs ahead of major releases, bringing a QA perspective to areas outside your usual regression focus. This role is remote within North America, and the team ships booking engine updates on a biweekly cadence with a freeze period around major holiday booking windows.

jobs.title: Release Quality Engineer
jobs.summary: Aldercrest ships updates to its property management and point-of-sale products on a regular release train, and this freelance role exists to strengthen the regression testing that happens in the days before each release goes out to hotel and restaurant customers. You will execute the release regression suite across both products, prioritizing testing time toward the areas most recently changed, and coordinate with engineering to determine whether any newly discovered issue should block the release or ship with a documented workaround. Expect to help formalize the currently ad hoc release checklist into a repeatable process the team can hand off to a permanent hire eventually. This is a remote, project-based freelance engagement structured around a rolling three-month scope, with the expectation of availability during the specific days immediately before each release for focused regression testing.

jobs.title: Developer Educator
jobs.summary: Hotel and restaurant technology teams integrating Aldercrest's property management API often have less dedicated engineering support than typical software customers, and this senior developer educator role exists to teach them what documentation alone usually cannot. You will design and deliver structured training programs, including live workshops and self-paced video courses, that walk integration partners through common implementation patterns for booking sync, POS integration, and guest data handling. A significant part of the role is curriculum development: identifying where partners consistently struggle during onboarding calls and turning those patterns into proactive training content rather than repeated one-off explanations. You will also certify partner developers who complete the advanced integration track, a program you will build essentially from scratch in your first six months. You will also gather structured feedback after every workshop, using it to continuously revise the curriculum rather than treating the first version as final. Comfort presenting live to a mixed audience of engineers and less technical operations staff is essential, since Aldercrest's partner base spans both. This role is fully remote within North America, with occasional travel to host in-person training sessions at partner conferences, and success is measured by a reduction in basic integration support tickets from trained partners.

jobs.title: Integration Sample Code Engineer
jobs.summary: Working sample code is what most partner developers actually copy when integrating Aldercrest's booking and POS APIs, more than they read the prose documentation, and this freelance engineering role is focused entirely on building and maintaining that sample code library. You will write reference implementations covering the most common integration patterns, in the languages Aldercrest's partner base most frequently uses, and keep those samples current as the underlying APIs evolve. You will also respond to sample-code-specific questions in the developer support forum, distinguishing genuine sample bugs from partners misapplying the pattern to their own architecture. This is a remote, hourly engagement structured around a rolling engagement tied to the current API roadmap, with strong practical coding skills valued over polished technical writing ability.

jobs.title: Property Success Manager
jobs.summary: Independent hotels and boutique restaurant groups using Aldercrest's platform typically lack a dedicated IT team, which means this senior success manager role often ends up being the closest thing a property has to ongoing technical guidance. You will manage a portfolio of roughly thirty properties, running quarterly check-ins that cover both platform adoption and broader operational questions about how the property is using the system day to day. Expect to proactively identify properties underusing features that would genuinely help their operations, like automated guest messaging or integrated POS reporting, and guide them through adoption rather than waiting for them to ask. You will also coordinate renewal conversations with the account's assigned salesperson, providing the operational context that makes the renewal case concrete rather than abstract. Properties are grouped loosely by region, and you will coordinate with two other success managers to share playbooks for common seasonal challenges like holiday staffing shortages or sudden booking surges. This role is hybrid out of the Miami office, and success is measured through portfolio retention and feature adoption rates across your properties.

jobs.title: Support Engineering Manager
jobs.summary: Aldercrest's support team fields everything from a front desk terminal that will not connect to a genuine data sync bug between the booking engine and a property's channel manager, and this manager role leads the team of eight support engineers who triage that entire range. You will set team priorities, own the escalation process between support and engineering, and personally handle the small number of situations sensitive enough to need management-level involvement, such as a major property considering churn over an unresolved issue. Expect to rebuild the team's on-call rotation, which currently relies too heavily on two senior engineers, into something more evenly distributed and sustainable. You will also run weekly one-on-ones with each team member and own hiring for two open support engineer positions this quarter. This posting is open to internal candidates first. You will also partner with the customer success organization on a shared escalation definition, since support and success historically disagreed about which team owned a borderline issue. The role is based onsite at the Miami office, and requires comfort managing a team that supports properties across many time zones.

jobs.title: Director of Customer Success
jobs.summary: Customer success at Aldercrest has grown from a handful of account managers into a function spanning onboarding, ongoing success management, and renewals, and this director role exists to give that broader function coherent strategy and leadership for the first time. You will manage the leads of each customer success sub-team, set the shared metrics the entire function is measured against, and represent customer success in executive planning meetings alongside sales and product leadership. A major initiative this year is redesigning the onboarding program for new hotel and restaurant customers, which currently takes considerably longer than the team's target and creates avoidable early churn risk. You will also own the customer success budget and headcount planning, making the case to the executive team for additional investment where the data supports it. You will also chair a monthly cross-functional review with product and support leadership, surfacing systemic issues that show up repeatedly across the customer success sub-teams before they become renewal risks. This role is hybrid out of the Lisbon office, and success is judged against net revenue retention and onboarding time-to-value across the customer base.

jobs.title: Guest Support Intern
jobs.summary: Understanding how hotel front desk staff actually use Aldercrest's platform under real pressure, during a busy check-in rush or a system hiccup at the worst possible moment, is something this internship is built around rather than something interns pick up incidentally. You will handle a queue of straightforward support tickets under close supervision, shadow senior support engineers on more complex cases to see how escalation decisions get made, and help maintain the internal knowledge base article library that the wider team references daily. As you build confidence you will take on a growing share of tickets independently, with a mentor checking your resolutions before they close. This is a twelve-week paid internship based onsite at the Miami office, working full time alongside the support team, and is designed as a genuine entry point into a technical support career in hospitality technology.

jobs.title: Employer Brand Specialist
jobs.summary: Aldercrest's engineering employer brand is essentially nonexistent outside of job postings themselves, and this entry-level role exists to start building it deliberately as the company competes for technical talent against better-known hospitality technology brands. You will manage the company's presence on employer review platforms, create content showcasing the engineering team's work for social media and the careers page, and coordinate logistics for the company's presence at a small number of regional tech recruiting events. A meaningful part of the role is gathering authentic material to work with: interviewing current engineers about their work and translating that into content that reads as genuine rather than generic recruiting marketing. You will report into the recruiting manager and work closely with a handful of engineers who have volunteered to be occasional brand ambassadors. You will also track basic engagement metrics on the content you publish, using that data to double down on the formats candidates actually respond to rather than guessing. This role has flexible working arrangements within North America and is a good entry point into either recruiting or marketing career paths.

jobs.title: Hospitality Tech Recruiter
jobs.summary: Aldercrest is hiring across engineering, support, and customer success simultaneously to support its expansion into two new geographic markets, and this six-month contract recruiter role is brought on specifically to help the permanent recruiting team absorb that temporary surge in hiring volume. You will manage a full requisition load across multiple departments, run structured interviews, and coordinate offer approvals with hiring managers and the compensation team. Expect to ramp up quickly on the company's specific interview process and candidate scorecards, since the contract timeline does not allow for a long onboarding period. You will also provide candidate experience feedback to the permanent recruiting team, flagging any process friction you notice as a relatively fresh set of eyes on the pipeline. This is a remote, fixed-term contract open to candidates across North America, running through the end of the expansion hiring push.

jobs.title: Property Systems Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary: Hotel groups evaluating Aldercrest's property management platform often operate a patchwork of existing systems for booking, POS, and guest messaging, and this senior solutions engineer role is responsible for designing a realistic migration and integration plan that does not require ripping everything out on day one. You will lead technical discovery calls with prospective hotel and restaurant group customers, map their existing systems against Aldercrest's integration capabilities, and build phased migration plans that account for a property's operational realities, since a hotel cannot simply pause operations to switch systems. You will also write technical responses to procurement questionnaires, particularly around data security and PCI compliance for payment handling. This role is fully remote within North America, with occasional travel for onsite discovery at the largest prospective accounts, and success is measured by technical win rate on supported opportunities.

jobs.title: Customer Onboarding Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary: Migrating a hotel's existing booking and guest data onto Aldercrest's platform without disrupting live operations is a genuinely technical problem, and this senior solutions engineer role owns that migration process for the company's larger new customers. You will scope data migration requirements during the sales process, build the technical implementation plan once a deal closes, and lead the actual cutover working closely with the customer's operations team to time it around their lowest-occupancy period. A recurring challenge is reconciling data quality issues in a property's legacy system that only surface once you attempt the migration, requiring judgment calls about what can be automated versus what needs manual cleanup. You will also train the customer's staff on the platform during the final weeks of onboarding, handing off to the ongoing success team once the property is fully live. You will also maintain a running checklist of migration pitfalls discovered on past onboarding projects, updating it after every cutover so the next migration benefits from what the last one revealed. This role is hybrid out of the Miami office, and success is measured through onboarding timeline accuracy and post-launch support ticket volume.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Solutions Engineer
jobs.summary: Large hotel chain accounts occasionally require a level of technical customization and integration depth that goes well beyond Aldercrest's standard onboarding process, and this senior contract solutions engineer role is dedicated to supporting exactly those enterprise-scale opportunities for the next eight months. You will lead technical scoping for multi-property rollouts, design integration architecture for chains running centralized reservation systems across dozens of individual properties, and coordinate closely with engineering when a chain's requirements push against the platform's current capabilities. Expect direct exposure to chain-level IT leadership and correspondingly rigorous procurement and security review processes. This role has flexible working arrangements and is open globally, with the expectation of travel for the largest enterprise accounts when in-person technical workshops are required to keep a deal moving.

jobs.title: GTM Systems Analyst
jobs.summary: Go-to-market tooling at Aldercrest, spanning Salesforce, the marketing automation platform, and the billing system, has accumulated enough small inconsistencies over time that basic reporting questions take longer to answer than they should, and this part-time analyst role exists to clean that up incrementally. You will maintain data hygiene across the core go-to-market systems, build and update dashboards that sales and marketing leadership rely on for weekly reviews, and investigate specific data discrepancies flagged by the revenue operations team. A recurring project is standardizing how leads are tagged by source, which currently varies enough between the marketing and sales teams to make attribution reporting unreliable. This role works roughly twenty hours a week, fully remote within North America, and is well suited to someone with strong SQL and Salesforce skills looking for a lighter weekly commitment.

jobs.title: Senior Search Relevance Engineer
jobs.summary: Jobbbler Demo Systems maintains the fictional job catalog used to demonstrate how people and browser agents can find technology roles without configuring a separate integration, and this senior engineering role owns the quality of that discovery experience. You will improve full-text ranking, location and salary filtering, and deterministic result ordering across a TypeScript service backed by PostgreSQL and SQLite. The work combines offline evaluation with careful product judgment: a change that raises an aggregate relevance score is only useful when ordinary job seekers can understand why the results improved. You will build compact relevance fixtures, investigate zero-result and overly broad queries, and partner with product and accessibility specialists to keep filters predictable for keyboard, screen-reader, and agent-driven use. The team expects engineers to trace a search from public tool input through normalization, storage, and rendered output, then document the trade-offs clearly enough for future contributors to maintain. This is a fully remote role open across Europe and the United Kingdom, with a small overlap window for collaborative review and otherwise flexible working hours.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Candidate Workflows
jobs.summary: Jobbbler Demo Systems is refining the fictional application journey that demonstrates how a browser agent can prepare a candidate's answers while the candidate keeps control of consent and the final submission decision, and this product role owns that journey end to end. You will map the smallest useful workflow from discovering a role through reviewing prepared answers, resolve ambiguity in requirements before it becomes interface clutter, and define success measures that reflect saved effort rather than superficial engagement. Day to day, you will work with design, engineering, privacy, and developer-relations partners to turn protocol capabilities into language a mainstream job seeker can understand immediately. You will also review agent traces from weak and strong models, identify where tool descriptions or state transitions cause avoidable mistakes, and prioritize improvements that help both human and automated clients without creating two separate products. The role is hybrid between Berlin and Amsterdam, with regular remote collaboration, and suits a senior product manager who is comfortable moving between user research, API behavior, consent boundaries, and detailed interaction critique.
